item.title: Giving back is success secret mother taught me — Dangote
item.description: *…why I’m teaching my daughters too Following his delivery of the Keynote address themed “The Geography of Opportunity: Why the World Needs What Africa Has,” recently at the 25th anniversary conference of Women in Management, Business, and Public Service, WIMBIZ; special guest and President/Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Ltd, Aliko Dangote, GCON sat down to a historic fireside chat with Rolake Akinkugbe Filani. The chat, anchored by the CEO, EnergyInc Advisors while also fielding questions from an audience of about 2000 women, was according to him, with the largest exclusive assembly of women he has ever addressed. When we rolled out the private placement we got 3.7 billion, so we took only 2.5. What we want to do is spread this prosperity. item.content:encoded: *…why I’m teaching my daughters too Following his delivery of the Keynote address themed “The Geography of Opportunity: Why the World Needs What Africa Has,” recently at the 25th anniversary conference of Women in Management, Business, and Public Service, WIMBIZ; special guest and President/Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Ltd, Aliko Dangote, GCON sat down to a historic fireside chat with Rolake Akinkugbe Filani. The chat, anchored by the CEO, EnergyInc Advisors while also fielding questions from an audience of about 2000 women, was according to him, with the largest exclusive assembly of women he has ever addressed. Excerpts:- When your IPO closed some weeks ago, we heard that you had received a hundred and twenty applications and every single one of the 54 African countries had also applied. In your mind, Africans investing in the continent, is that one example of the geography of opportunity? Yes. What we have done with this IPO is trying to do something where, when there’s an offer in Kenya Nigerians will participate. When we did the private placement the whole idea was for us to sell 2.5 billion dollars. 1 billion was for private placement, 1.5 billion was for IPO. When we rolled out the private placement we got 3.7 billion, so we took only 2.5. What we want to do is spread this prosperity. Did this particular IPO change your view on how you mobilise capital from the African continent ? It has changed dramatically. Things are really changing very fast. Even abroad, people have a change of mind about Africa. We’ve gotten amazing demand. We’re talking about millions participating. Saudi Aramco worldwide was about 5million. We didn’t reach 10 million because of time constraints. A lot of people didn’t know how to access but the sheer trust of public enterprise that we have today in Africa, that’s why people are starting to remove their money from under their mattress to come and invest. Incredible achievement. You came from a long line of women who were in commerce, your mother, your great aunt and even your step grandmother. We want to hear if there are principles you learned by watching, by trends, by conversations, from the women in your family. From my mum it’s learning how to give back. she was always talking about giving back and she in the 80s would make sure that everyday we were feeding the poor, about 12000 people, three square meals and then we gave about 35,000 loaves of bread everyday. But right now, because there are so many in need I don’t want to announce it here, but we are looking at the possibilities of going to most of the vulnerable people to see if we can we do XYZ. We’re targeting feeding about 100m people every year. My children are ready to give. As a Muslim I am allowed to allocate one third of my wealth to charity and can actually donate to you. You don’t want when something happens to you then there will be arguments, so we actually put it in writing and got all of them to sign that in the event of my debut, one third is for the Foundation. All the good we are doing now will continue. You had a lot of naysayers when you were building the refinery and every woman here has a smaller version of that whether it be delayed contract, change in FX etc and women are used to being underestimated especially when the voices become loud and progress is invisible. During those times, what was really going through your mind? I must admit that when we were building the refinery we didn’t know what we were doing. If we knew we wouldn’t have gone near there at all. I always say that my greatest enemy, if I want to pray bad for him, I will pray that he will go and start building a refinery. Right now, that is history because we not only have one in Nigeria we have one in Namibia and possibly an additional one because we have a vision and that vision is x billion per annum but the x billion per annum which was 50 billion now has moved to 60 billion. First of all you must be trustworthy because money follows trust before profit. That your name that you have, protect it as much as you can. There will still be some few people who will try some stuff but then just be very careful, don’t let anybody frighten you. Let me give you a simple example, we have never ever gone abroad to try and raise funds but in June we went out to the market to say, we don’t have a rating and we are not going to do any guarantees. We went to what we call No Deal Road Show and at the end of it there was demand of 1.3 billion. We took 750 million. They came back to us, JP Morgan, bank of America, Merrill Lynch. We are making good money now, we went and raised another 750 in July. In August we thought, why don’t we do something that has not been done for a very long time in sub Saharan Africa, which is for a company to raise 10 years’ money. The 5 years’ money we raised, we had no rating, no collateral but you won’t believe we raised money. Our interest rate was below Federal Government rate. 10 years’ money, the demand was almost 1.5 billion but we took 750m. The sky is the limit. A lot of you should try. Don’t be scared. You say don’t be scared but it’s interesting that in order to succeed in business you have to be a bit delusional. For the women here looking for business opportunities whether local or international, how do you determine which opportunity to hold on to and which to hold back on? Whether you are a man or woman, don’t go into a business you don’t understand. You must understand that business both in and out and don’t let your own management come and be telling you. Today if you tell me, go into banking, I am not going to go into banking. You take a lot of money from the bank … It’s easy when I am borrowing the money, I have to read every single dot to make sure I do the right thing. There are some things, maybe if you look at numbers, maybe building a port, you can never ever go wrong. Port will make money. The capacity of demand is there. In 24 years by the Grace of God , we are going to be at 150 million and most of us don’t know, the population growth of Nigeria is 8.7 million babies every year. We must use every available land, we haven’t even used 10% of our arable land. People should please stop taking their money abroad no matter what. Why you see that Asia has done very well is because majority keep their money in their country at home and that money is useful to their economy. That’s why we want to bring something new. We want to start having our AGM in a stadium, not in a hall. It has to be a stadium because we have millions of shareholders. We don’t have the Asian culture of savings One in 5 people today is African. By 2050 it will be 1 in 4. Yet Africa contributes less than 3 cents of every dollar global output. When you see those stats is it a warning about what we need to do? Unfortunately we don’t plan. We need to plan ahead. Now, Let’s look at the price of food, does Europe have the land to grow their food? They don’t. Everyone in the next 24 years will turn to Africa because we have 60 percent of the world’s arable land, more than 37 percent of the minerals resources, critical minerals. The difficulty and the difference is that these people have seen us keeping our money abroad, we’re not investing here so they believe there’s a danger they don’t know. We Africans must derisk the real and also perceived risk. That is the only way other people would come and invest here. The median age in Africa is 19, in Europe it’s 40. Today if we don’t change, these GenZ s, if they get tired of us they will come and drive us away and they believe we have wasted so much time and we are not doing the right things. We have what it takes to turn around our fortunes. I can’t understand how someone that has a British passport can travel more freely in Africa than Africans. We are sort of scared of our own acceleration. Today we have 240 million Nigerians, but the president of Sao Tome when he gets to UN, has the same

item.title: How Mick Cronin hyped up Bruins before bounce-back win vs. Georgetown
item.description: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images How Mick Cronin hyped up Bruins before bounce-back win vs. Georgetown appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The UCLA Bruins suffered a disappointing defeat at the hands of the Saint Mary’s Gaels on Thursday afternoon, keeping them from advancing to the title game of the Rady Children’s Invitational. But the Bruins bounced back with a 75-63 win over Georgetown in the third-place game, and UCLA head coach Mick Cronin revealed how he challenged the team prior to the game, as per Connor David Dullinger of The LA Times. “I told the guys this is a chance to show what we’re made of. I challenged them pretty good last night,” Cronin said. “I told them that they need to have reverence and an appreciation for the jersey they wear … UCLA is a privilege to go there as a student.” With the win, UCLA improved to 7-1 on the season, although where they will fall when the new AP men’s basketball poll comes out on Monday, remains to be seen. The Bruins had been ranked at No. 6 coming into this past week. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It was an unlikely hero who led the way for UCLA in sophomore guard Azavier Robinson, finishing with a game-high 23 points. Robinson is in his first season with the Bruins after entering the transfer portal following his freshman year at Butler. UCLA is in the program’s eighth season with Mick Cronin at the helm as head coach. During that time, he’s led the Bruins to five NCAA Tournament appearances, including one Final Four run in 2020-21. UCLA’s next game is Tuesday, Dec. 1 as they begin Big Ten play with a matchup against the Oregon Ducks. item.title: 'Charger Magic' lifts Crest past South Point, into NCHSAA 5A West final
item.description: BOILING SPRINGS — For a half, Mark Barnes admitted the team he was watching Friday, Nov. 27 didn’t resemble the one which ran away with the Big South 5A/6A title and earned the NCHSAA 5A West bracket’s top seed. “(At halftime) We told them we were kind of disappointed because we thought they had lost their composure a little bit, doing some finger pointing. That’s not who we are,” he said. During the latter 24 minutes, Crest provided a more accurate resemblance of itself. MR. CONSISTENCY: What's the secret to Crest football's Paxton Dobbin's consistent play? TURNING THE PAGE: Crest football focused on improvement despite 2-0 start to 2026 season Down 21-7 at halftime, the Chargers outscored 4-seed South Point 28-0 in the second half to claim a 42-21 victory at Sid Bryson Stadium. All-purpose man Brock Melton had five rushing touchdowns in the game, with quarterback K.J. Bell and running back Malachi Gamble — who finished with 173 rushing yards — connecting on another. The win is Crest’s second this year over the Red Raiders, and fourth consecutive victory in the overall series. It is also the second year in a row the Chargers eliminated South Point from the playoffs. “You know, the score isn’t indicative of the type of football game this was (Friday night),” Barnes said. Kaveaun Pless opened things with a flourish for South Point, his 52-yard touchdown run giving his team a 7-0 lead. After forcing Crest to turn the ball over on downs, the Red Raiders responded with a Cayden Rumph TD run to put them in front by two scores. Crest answered on its ensuing drive, Brock Melton cutting the South Point lead to 14-7. The Red Raiders pushed it back to double digits on its next possession, Rumph scoring on a 10-yard TD scamper midway through the second quarter. Little did anyone know at the time, but it was the last time South Point would score in the game. Following a Crest turnover in South Point territory, it seemed South Point was primed to add to its lead. However, its field goal attempt was errant. A matter of plays later, Melton’s second TD of the night allowed the Chargers to take momentum with them into the locker room. “I told our kids before the game that (South Point) was going to put the ball on the ground. We just have to make sure we’re there to recover it,” Barnes said. Things flipped for good on South Point’s first possession of the second half, Crest recovering a South Point fumble near midfield. The Chargers immediately cashed the gift in, Melton’s third TD run tying the game at 21. Following a three-and-out, senior standout Javion Hopper blocked a South Point punt, the ball recovered at the Red Raider 2-yard line. CONSISTENCY: What's the secret to Crest football's Paxton Dobbin's consistent play? TURNING THE PAGE: Crest football focused on improvement despite 2-0 start to 2026 season Down 21-7 at halftime, the Chargers outscored 4-seed South Point 28-0 in the second half to claim a 42-21 victory at Sid Bryson Stadium. Kaveaun Pless opened things with a flourish for South Point, his 52-yard touchdown run giving his team a 7-0 lead. After forcing Crest to turn the ball over on downs, the Red Raiders responded with a Cayden Rumph TD run to put them in front by two scores. Crest answered on its ensuing drive, Brock Melton cutting the South Point lead to 14-7. The Red Raiders pushed it back to double digits on its next possession, Rumph scoring on a 10-yard TD scamper midway through the second quarter. Little did anyone know at the time, but it was the last time South Point would score in the game. Following a Crest turnover in South Point territory, it seemed South Point was primed to add to its lead. However, its field goal attempt was errant. A matter of plays later, Melton’s second TD of the night allowed the Chargers to take momentum with them into the locker room. “I told our kids before the game that (South Point) was going to put the ball on the ground. We just have to make sure we’re there to recover it,” Barnes said. Things flipped for good on South Point’s first possession of the second half, Crest recovering a South Point fumble near midfield. The Chargers immediately cashed the gift in, Melton’s third TD run tying the game at 21. Following a three-and-out, senior standout Javion Hopper blocked a South Point punt, the ball recovered at the Red Raider 2-yard line. Melton made light work of the distance required, muscling his way in for a TD and Crest’s first lead of the night at 28-21. Bell’s TD pass to Gamble upped the Crest advantage to 35-21 at the end of three quarters. Melton added his last TD run in the fourth to put the game away. “There’s something to (Charger Magic),” Barnes said. “But it isn’t given to you, and you got to be prepared for the opportunities when they come to you. We have to play the way we’re supposed to play and give ourselves an opportunity to be rewarded and that ‘Charger Magic’ will happen.” The top-seeded Chargers advance to a second NCHSAA 5A West final in a row. Crest will host No. 3 Jay M. Robinson, which outlasted 7-seed East Lincoln 42-34 to advance. Kickoff is at 7 p.m. on Friday, Dec. 4. item.title: 49ers' Mac Jones wouldn't have minded a trade. A tradeoff? He gets to start vs. Seattle
item.description: Quarterback Mac Jones started eight games for the 49ers last season while Brock Purdy was hurt. Jones will get the start Sunday against the Seahawks while Purdy recovers from an ankle injury. (Ryan Sun/Associated Press) Mac Jones will start for a franchise Sunday that he was at least halfway hoping would get rid of him less than three weeks ago. On Friday, when asked about the interest he generated before the NFL's trade deadline on Nov. 10, the San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback was candid. Did Jones think it sounded more appealing to start for a playoff contender in need of a QB rather than keep collecting dust behind Brock Purdy ? "Yeah, definitely have thought about it," Jones said. "And I was just glad that the deadline was over because I got to move forward." On Sunday, Jones will move into the starting lineup with Purdy sidelined with a sprained left ankle. And Jones will have a chance to show why the 49ers have declined to deal him after his brilliant 2025 relief work made him an appealing trade target. After playing 20 mop-up snaps this season, Jones' first real action will be a real challenge: He'll face the Seahawks' top-ranked defense at Levi's Stadium with rain in the forecast. Jones, 28, noted he long ago gained NFL experience playing in wet conditions against a formidable foe. On Oct. 3, 2021, in his fourth career start as a rookie, Jones faced Tampa Bay, then the defending Super Bowl champions, and QB Tom Brady in Brady's only game against New England, his employer for his first 20 seasons. Jones completed 31 of 40 passes for 275 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in a 19-17 loss in a downpour. "That was like the game of the century," Jones said, laughing. "And I wasn't freaking out about the rain. I just went out there and played. So that's what I'm going to do this time." Jones' work last season gives the 49ers confidence he can deliver on the promise. Jones went 5-3, ranked second in the NFL in completion percentage (69.6), 12th in yards per attempt (7.4) and 13th in passer rating (97.4) among the 36 QBs who had at least 200 pass attempts. In his final start, a 42-26 loss to the Rams, he became the third QB in franchise history to complete 30-plus passes with a completion percentage of at least 80%, joining Steve Young and Jeff Garcia. In his penultimate start, a 34-24 road win against the Giants, he completed 19 of 24 passes, and he joined Young and Joe Montana as the only QBs in franchise history to complete at least 14 consecutive passes to start a game. item.content:encoded: Quarterback Mac Jones started eight games for the 49ers last season while Brock Purdy was hurt. Jones will get the start Sunday against the Seahawks while Purdy recovers from an ankle injury. (Ryan Sun/Associated Press) Mac Jones will start for a franchise Sunday that he was at least halfway hoping would get rid of him less than three weeks ago. On Friday, when asked about the interest he generated before the NFL's trade deadline on Nov. 10, the San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback was candid. Did Jones think it sounded more appealing to start for a playoff contender in need of a QB rather than keep collecting dust behind Brock Purdy ? "Yeah, definitely have thought about it," Jones said. "And I was just glad that the deadline was over because I got to move forward." On Sunday, Jones will move into the starting lineup with Purdy sidelined with a sprained left ankle. And Jones will have a chance to show why the 49ers have declined to deal him after his brilliant 2025 relief work made him an appealing trade target. After playing 20 mop-up snaps this season, Jones' first real action will be a real challenge: He'll face the Seahawks' top-ranked defense at Levi's Stadium with rain in the forecast. Jones, 28, noted he long ago gained NFL experience playing in wet conditions against a formidable foe. On Oct. 3, 2021, in his fourth career start as a rookie, Jones faced Tampa Bay, then the defending Super Bowl champions, and QB Tom Brady in Brady's only game against New England, his employer for his first 20 seasons. Jones completed 31 of 40 passes for 275 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in a 19-17 loss in a downpour. "That was like the game of the century," Jones said, laughing. "And I wasn't freaking out about the rain. I just went out there and played. So that's what I'm going to do this time." Jones' work last season gives the 49ers confidence he can deliver on the promise. Jones went 5-3, ranked second in the NFL in completion percentage (69.6), 12th in yards per attempt (7.4) and 13th in passer rating (97.4) among the 36 QBs who had at least 200 pass attempts. In his final start, a 42-26 loss to the Rams, he became the third QB in franchise history to complete 30-plus passes with a completion percentage of at least 80%, joining Steve Young and Jeff Garcia. In his penultimate start, a 34-24 road win against the Giants, he completed 19 of 24 passes, and he joined Young and Joe Montana as the only QBs in franchise history to complete at least 14 consecutive passes to start a game. "Anytime you have a backup quarterback who you believe could be one of the better starters in this league, that's a hell of a deal," head coach Kyle Shanahan said. "… Really grateful that he's here. And I'm glad we didn't make a trade." That was quick: Looking ahead to Sunday's game, 49ers pass rusher Nick Bosa said of the Seahawks, "We're definitely not taking them lightly." The seemingly innocuous comment reflected how much the tenor has changed since the 49ers beat Seattle 32-29 in Week 5. Before that game, 49ers players were asked about facing the defending Super Bowl champions who trampled them en route to a title last season. The Seahawks handed the 49ers their second-worst playoff loss in franchise history in a 41-6 divisional-round win after wresting the NFC's No. 1 seed from them with a 13-3 victory in the regular-season finale. Now, the 49ers (9-1) can essentially ensure the Seahawks (6-4) won't repeat as NFC West champions if they beat them Sunday to sweep the regular-season series. Left tackle Trent Williams, 38, was asked about how quickly storylines can change in the NFL. "I think I remember getting asked a question at the end of last year, like, ‘What do you guys do? There's no way you can beat Seattle. The defense is not slowing down. You guys are getting older, X, Y, Z.'" Williams said. "What I said last year is that it's all about playing the game on Sunday. All of the roster doesn't matter. The history doesn't matter. The only thing that matters is quarter one through four on Sunday." Healthy backfield: When the 49ers played the Seahawks on Oct. 11, they game-planned for the team's third-string running back. Emanuel Wilson had 20 carries for only 61 yards - and failed to break off a run longer than eight yards - in San Francisco's win. The Seahawks' offense looked one-dimensional. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the only true threat. Things will look much different this time around, as the 49ers will face Seattle's top two rushers in Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price. Over their past three contests since returning a healthy Charbonnet and Price, the Seahawks' ground attack has vastly improved. Price, a rookie first-round pick, collected his first career touchdown in the Seahawks' last game before their bye week, a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Charbonnet, working his way back from a January torn ACL, has gone from six to 16 to 20 carries over his past three contests. He had a season-high 94 rushing yards against Las Vegas on Nov. 15. The 49ers lead the league in rushing yards allowed per game (81.2). Making Seattle's run game moot, in an expected rain game, could go a long way toward shutting down a passing offense that ranks in the bottom half of the league. With defensive tackles DeForest Buckner, Osa Odighizuwa and CJ West, plus defensive ends Bosa, Keion White and Mykel Williams all healthy, Sunday will provide a strong test as to how legitimate San Francisco's run defense truly is. Darnold returns: Quarterback Sam Darnold (quad) will return for Seattle after missing the team's past two games. The Seahawks said "thanks, but no thanks" to backup quarterback Drew Lock, who has led them to a 4-0 record across Darnold's two stretches of absences. Lock this season has a passer rating of 125.6. That would lead all quarterbacks who have started at least four games. Darnold's passer rating this season is 79.5. Head coach Mike Macdonald shut down speculation of Darnold losing his job while he was still out. On Nov. 16, asked about the possibility of inserting Lock for the remainder of the season, Macdonald said, "Drew's been fantastic. He's been phenomenal. … But Sam's our quarterback." The 49ers are 2-2 against Darnold as a Seahawk over the past 1½ seasons, including their 41-6 divisional round loss in January. Darnold's numbers over those four games: 667 passing yards, two touchdowns, two interceptions, 69.5% completion rate. Asked Friday if he feels the healthiest he's been all season, Darnold told local reporters: "I feel really good. I'm not going to compare it to any other point in the season, but I feel really good right now." Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. This article originally published at 49ers' Mac Jones wouldn't have minded a trade. A tradeoff? He gets to start vs. Seattle .

item.title: Last-minute fantasy football streaming options for Week 12: Wide Receiver
item.description: Last-minute fantasy football streaming options for Week 12: Wide Receiver appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Holiday-week scheduling always compresses the fantasy football calendar. Week 12 has already locked 10 teams out of managers’ lineup decisions. Between Wednesday’s Rams-Packers opener, Thursday’s Thanksgiving tripleheader, and Friday’s AFC tilt in Pittsburgh, nearly a third of the league’s wideouts are no longer available. This leaves managers scrambling to patch holes before Sunday’s slate kicks off. item.title: ‘In a weird way’: Mason Rudolph shares how the Aaron Rodgers drama actually helped Steelers beat Broncos
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers capped off a very difficult week with a fine win over the Denver Broncos. The drama surrounding Aaron Rodgers, who was released earlier this week, dominated the headlines, and many felt that would have an impact on the team. However, the Steelers were incredibly dominant, beating the Broncos 27-5. Mason Rudolph says the Aaron Rodgers ‘adversity’ brought the Steelers together Mason Rudolph hadn’t been involved in first-team reps all week, which is why he had to put in extra work on Thursday ahead of Friday’s game. The quarterback, who took over Rodgers’ role, definitely played his part, delivering a clean, efficient and turnover-free game-manager performance. Unsurprisingly, the questions after the game were always going to be dominated by the Rodgers saga during the week. Rudolph was asked about it too, and he claimed that the controversy helped, as it brought the team a lot closer ahead of the win against the Broncos. He said on Prime Video: “It was a lot. Sort of unprecedented, nothing I’ve ever been through and probably the same for all my teammates. “We’re so proud of the way we turned the page on Wednesday, and the veteran leadership – Cameron Heyward, Jalen Ramsey, T. J. Watt – really led us forward.” Rudolph further added: “I think the leadership council just sort of rallied around Coach McCarthy. And I think, in a weird way, you know, the adversity brought us probably closer together. And I think we’ll just keep carrying that into week after week.” The 31-year-old hadn’t started a game for over a year, so the pressure was on for him to deliver after taking Rodgers’ place against the Broncos. Rudolph finished the game with nine of 15 passes completed (60.0%) for 142 yards and one touchdown. He took a sack for a 12-yard loss, which was really the only blemish in his performance, while posting a 113.8 passer rating. All in all, it was a fine outing for the Steelers after what has been a tough week. We’re sure Rudolph and everyone else will be delighted with how the game panned out. item.title: Rams’ Bill Murray suffers brutal injury blow after first NFL start
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams have lost another offensive lineman after Bill Murray suffered a torn Achilles tendon against the Green Bay Packers . NFL insider Jeremy Fowler reported the injury on X, and Murray will miss the remainder of the season. The offensive guard made his first NFL start during Wednesday’s 26-13 victory over Green Bay. “Rams offensive guard Bill Murray tore his Achilles tendon Wednesday vs. Green Bay, per sources,” Fowler wrote. “Murray started the game at left guard and acquitted himself well. Los Angeles down another offensive lineman.” MORE: Rams lose Davis Allen to potential season-ending injury Rams offensive guard Bill Murray tore his Achilles tendon Wednesday vs. Green Bay, per sources. Murray started the game at left guard and acquitted himself well. Los Angeles down another offensive lineman. — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 28, 2026 Murray stepped into the starting lineup because Steve Avila remained sidelined with a hamstring injury. He played 56 of 75 offensive snaps before leaving during the fourth quarter. The injury represents another setback for a Rams offensive line already dealing with several absences. Murray’s first start also came during an important stretch of the team’s playoff push. Rams face growing problems along offensive line Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams center Dylan McMahon (63) enters the field at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Murray joins Dylan McMahon, Coleman Shelton, and Avila among the injured offensive linemen. McMahon has a season-ending patellar tendon injury, while Shelton continues dealing with a hamstring problem. Avila’s availability remains uncertain ahead of the Rams’ Week 13 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Justin Dedich stepped in for Murray against Green Bay and could receive another starting opportunity. The Rams will need their remaining linemen to handle the workload as the schedule gets tougher. Their offensive line depth now faces another serious test. Los Angeles improved to 7-4 after defeating Green Bay, extending its winning streak to five games. The team remains firmly involved in the NFC playoff race. MORE: Latest report is bad news for Kyren Williams fantasy football owners However, the Chiefs present a difficult next challenge on December 3. Protecting the quarterback and maintaining the running game will become even more important with Murray unavailable. Murray’s injury also comes at a difficult point in his career. The 29-year-old joined Los Angeles in July and was beginning to earn a larger opportunity. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: “Accepting Your Apologies”: Broncos Legend Wastes No Time in Sending a Brutal Reality Check on Bo Nix After Awful Game in Loss to Steelers
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, IN – MARCH 01: Oregon quarterback Bo Nix answers questions from the media during the NFL, American Football Herren, USA Scouting Combine on March 1, 2024, at the Indiana Convention Center in Indianapolis, IN. Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire NFL: MAR 01 Scouting Combine EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon2403010491 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Bo Nix’s rough outing against the Steelers has drawn a pointed response from a familiar voice in Denver. Broncos legend Mark Schlereth, who has followed the team closely for years, did not hold back in assessing the quarterback’s performance. He did not wait long to say ‘I told you so.’ “For all you Bo apologists who were angry with me last week… I am currently accepting your apologies!,” Mark Schlereth posted on X . Nix completed 22 of 40 passes for 169 yards. He threw no touchdowns, tossed two interceptions, and was sacked three times. His QBR landed at 24.7 and his passer rating at 44.7. Nix did not dodge it afterward. In his postgame press conference, he owned the result. When a Broncos icon speaks, Denver listens. Subscribe to stay on top of the hard truths reshaping the franchise's quarterback future. “It’s frustrating, for sure,” Nix said. “I let the team down today, and that’s the last thing I want to do as the quarterback and the leader of the team.” This was not a sudden turn for Schlereth, either. A few weeks earlier, the former NFL offensive lineman used “The Stinkin’ Truth Podcast” to go after the Broncos’ offense, and he set aside a full segment for Nix’s struggles. “I still look at the Denver Broncos, and I am ready to just go, I relent,” Schlereth said. “I give. I don’t understand it. Because you look at this offense, it’s not just anemic; it’s dreadful for stretches, and there is no rhyme, no reason. Bo Nix, he looks terrible from the pocket.” He has also been clear about where he thinks the blame belongs. In the past, Schlereth admitted that Nix has been “a major part of the offensive woes” and “a major part of the problem,” adding that the quarterback needed to play better and be held accountable. Last week, in an episode on the Broncos’ ceiling, Schlereth spoke on Nix’s past issues regarding getting out of the pocket. He acknowledged that the QB has become a little braver and noted his development, but Nix is yet to pass the test for Schlereth. “If you look at yourself as a football team, you’re like, ‘Man, we’re 7-2 right now during the toughest part of our schedule, and we have not played well as an offense at all.’ We haven’t run the ball. item.content:encoded: INDIANAPOLIS, IN – MARCH 01: Oregon quarterback Bo Nix answers questions from the media during the NFL, American Football Herren, USA Scouting Combine on March 1, 2024, at the Indiana Convention Center in Indianapolis, IN. Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire NFL: MAR 01 Scouting Combine EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon2403010491 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Bo Nix’s rough outing against the Steelers has drawn a pointed response from a familiar voice in Denver. Broncos legend Mark Schlereth, who has followed the team closely for years, did not hold back in assessing the quarterback’s performance. He did not wait long to say ‘I told you so.’ “For all you Bo apologists who were angry with me last week… I am currently accepting your apologies!,” Mark Schlereth posted on X . Nix completed 22 of 40 passes for 169 yards. He threw no touchdowns, tossed two interceptions, and was sacked three times. His QBR landed at 24.7 and his passer rating at 44.7. Nix did not dodge it afterward. In his postgame press conference, he owned the result. When a Broncos icon speaks, Denver listens. Subscribe to stay on top of the hard truths reshaping the franchise's quarterback future. “It’s frustrating, for sure,” Nix said. “I let the team down today, and that’s the last thing I want to do as the quarterback and the leader of the team.” This was not a sudden turn for Schlereth, either. A few weeks earlier, the former NFL offensive lineman used “The Stinkin’ Truth Podcast” to go after the Broncos’ offense, and he set aside a full segment for Nix’s struggles. “I still look at the Denver Broncos, and I am ready to just go, I relent,” Schlereth said. “I give. I don’t understand it. Because you look at this offense, it’s not just anemic; it’s dreadful for stretches, and there is no rhyme, no reason. Bo Nix, he looks terrible from the pocket.” He has also been clear about where he thinks the blame belongs. In the past, Schlereth admitted that Nix has been “a major part of the offensive woes” and “a major part of the problem,” adding that the quarterback needed to play better and be held accountable. Last week, in an episode on the Broncos’ ceiling, Schlereth spoke on Nix’s past issues regarding getting out of the pocket. He acknowledged that the QB has become a little braver and noted his development, but Nix is yet to pass the test for Schlereth. “If you look at yourself as a football team, you’re like, ‘Man, we’re 7-2 right now during the toughest part of our schedule, and we have not played well as an offense at all.’ We haven’t run the ball. We haven’t been dynamic in the passing game. Our quarterback really struggled early. He’s gotten better the last three games, but we’ve got all this lack of production from a throwing standpoint, from a running standpoint.” The team numbers back up some of that frustration. Denver’s average of 284.7 yards per game ranks 28th among the 32 teams, per ESPN. Most of it comes through the air, with 1,891 net passing yards (189.1 per game), while the ground game has added 956 yards (95.6 per game). Nix’s lack of production in the ground game has also come under scrutiny. Against Pittsburgh on Friday, however, Nix had been a major disappointment. His struggles in bad weather proved to be a limiting factor, but he also gave away opportunities to the Steelers. On a third-and-15 (!) from Denver’s 19 in the first quarter, Nix lost control of the ball, allowing Pittsburgh to recover it and score a touchdown. He also had a pick-six late in the second quarter, allowing Pittsburgh to be ahead of Denver 24-5 at halftime. In only two quarters, Nix was responsible for 14 of Pittsburgh’s points, as pointed out by Predominantly Orange’s Sayre Bedinger. Head coach Sean Payton, though, made sure Nix was not left to take the heat alone. “Well, obviously, disappointing loss…it starts with me,” Payton said. “You know, I felt like our prep coming into this week, relative to the schedule, was good. You know, we knew it was going to be a tough challenge coming in here; they played well at home, and I think early on, we gave them opportunities of momentum, and that falls on me.” Payton also expressed confidence that his quarterback will recover, saying “he’ll bounce back.” He added, “It’s our job to give him those opportunities to bounce back,” as relayed by Stevens. Nix’s production has been poorer this season, which is a disappointing reality. He thrived in Sean Payton’s offense for the last two years. The latter giving up playcalling at the start of the season might have a role in Nix’s drop in performance, but Payton is now back as playcaller. The QB doesn’t seem to have found his rhythm back yet. For now, the Broncos have to move on from a loss that ended their six-game winning streak. Their upcoming matchup with the Miami Dolphins gives Nix a chance to answer the criticism on the field, which is the only place it will really be settled. item.title: "I'm Bouta Come Out of Retirement": Ex-Cowboys WR & Super Bowl Champ Eyes NFL Return After Abrupt Retirement at 28
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NC – OCTOBER 12: Dallas Cowboys helmet during an NFL, American Football Herren, USA football game between the Carolina Panthers and the Dallas Cowboys on October 12, 2025 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire NFL: OCT 12 Cowboys at Panthers EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon251012059 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Parris Campbell already has the kind of souvenir players spend entire careers chasing: a Super Bowl ring with the Philadelphia Eagles. He suddenly said goodbye to the NFL in May, less than two months ahead of his 29th birthday. Six months later, one short message has given that farewell a curious little twist. “Man, I’m bouta come out of retirement,” Campbell wrote in an Instagram post. The former Dallas Cowboys wide receiver, Campbell, offered no details on timing, team, or league, leaving his comeback status uncertain. Still, those few words were enough to make people wonder whether his cleats might be getting restless. His original exit arrived on May 27, when the Cowboys moved him to the reserve/retired list. Four months later, he abruptly stepped away without making a formal public retirement announcement. The Cowboys, too, didn’t say much about why he stepped away right before voluntary workouts, and after seven injury-riddled seasons, nobody really expected him back on the field. A Super Bowl winner walking away at his peak, then reconsidering it all. Subscribe to stay updated on whether this veteran makes his unexpected comeback. Things looked a lot brighter coming out of Ohio State. Campbell earned first-team All-Big Ten honors in 2018 after piling up 90 catches, 1,063 yards, and 12 touchdowns, convincing the Indianapolis Colts to spend a second-round pick on him at No. 59 overall in 2019. His body had other plans once he reached the pros. A broken foot cut his rookie season short, a torn MCL and PCL against the Vikings knocked him out in Week 2 of 2020, and another trip to injured reserve followed in 2021. By 2022, he finally got a full runway. Playing in all 17 games, Campbell posted career highs with 63 receptions, 623 yards, and three scores. For a player who had spent so much time working his way back, it was a welcome glimpse of what steady playing time could bring. That momentum did not travel with him to the New York Giants. Campbell managed 20 catches for 104 yards in 2023 and was inactive for the final five weeks. His next chance came from Philadelphia, but even that road took a sharp turn when the Eagles released him in August 2024. A practice squad spot was available, although accepting it was far from automatic. “I immediately was like, no. That’s not me. That’s not for me,” Campbell recalled. item.content:encoded: CHARLOTTE, NC – OCTOBER 12: Dallas Cowboys helmet during an NFL, American Football Herren, USA football game between the Carolina Panthers and the Dallas Cowboys on October 12, 2025 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire NFL: OCT 12 Cowboys at Panthers EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon251012059 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Parris Campbell already has the kind of souvenir players spend entire careers chasing: a Super Bowl ring with the Philadelphia Eagles. He suddenly said goodbye to the NFL in May, less than two months ahead of his 29th birthday. Six months later, one short message has given that farewell a curious little twist. “Man, I’m bouta come out of retirement,” Campbell wrote in an Instagram post. The former Dallas Cowboys wide receiver, Campbell, offered no details on timing, team, or league, leaving his comeback status uncertain. Still, those few words were enough to make people wonder whether his cleats might be getting restless. His original exit arrived on May 27, when the Cowboys moved him to the reserve/retired list. Four months later, he abruptly stepped away without making a formal public retirement announcement. The Cowboys, too, didn’t say much about why he stepped away right before voluntary workouts, and after seven injury-riddled seasons, nobody really expected him back on the field. A Super Bowl winner walking away at his peak, then reconsidering it all. Subscribe to stay updated on whether this veteran makes his unexpected comeback. Things looked a lot brighter coming out of Ohio State. Campbell earned first-team All-Big Ten honors in 2018 after piling up 90 catches, 1,063 yards, and 12 touchdowns, convincing the Indianapolis Colts to spend a second-round pick on him at No. 59 overall in 2019. His body had other plans once he reached the pros. A broken foot cut his rookie season short, a torn MCL and PCL against the Vikings knocked him out in Week 2 of 2020, and another trip to injured reserve followed in 2021. By 2022, he finally got a full runway. Playing in all 17 games, Campbell posted career highs with 63 receptions, 623 yards, and three scores. For a player who had spent so much time working his way back, it was a welcome glimpse of what steady playing time could bring. That momentum did not travel with him to the New York Giants. Campbell managed 20 catches for 104 yards in 2023 and was inactive for the final five weeks. His next chance came from Philadelphia, but even that road took a sharp turn when the Eagles released him in August 2024. A practice squad spot was available, although accepting it was far from automatic. “I immediately was like, no. That’s not me. That’s not for me,” Campbell recalled. Retirement was suddenly on his mind, long before the day he eventually walked away. Then Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni called. Having previously worked with Campbell in Indianapolis, Sirianni encouraged him to stay. Campbell took the practice squad opportunity and earned a promotion to the active roster in October. That decision kept him around for a ride he certainly would not have wanted to miss. Philadelphia went all the way to Super Bowl LIX and defeated the Kansas City Chiefs. “From the last season in Indy to now, there’s been a lot of ups and downs, bumps and bruises, good times, bad times,” Campbell said. By the end of it, those bruises came with a championship attached. Dallas was next in March 2025, but another uphill climb awaited. Campbell went on injured reserve, was released in August, and later returned to the practice squad. The Cowboys brought him back on a reserve/future contract in January 2026, only for his retirement to arrive that May. His career stat sheet finishes at 123 receptions, 1,117 yards, and six touchdowns. Even so, the numbers miss the best part of the story: from endless injury rehab to a healthy rebound and a championship ring after he had already thought about quitting. One social media post does not make a comeback, and Dallas still holds his rights on the retired list anyway. Still, Campbell just left the door cracked open, and his next move will prove whether he is simply testing the waters or ready to dive back in. item.title: What Pete Edochie wanted to be remembered for
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku When Vanguard encountered Pete Edochie, the Lion of Africa in his den on two different occasions, it was never just an interview.It was an audience with a king. Ebubedike sat on his throne, spoke in proverbs, laughed loudly, sipped from a glass of fresh palm wine and dropped revelations that have now become timeless. Those conversations carried the full weight of Pete Edochie and what he represented on the big screen and in real life. The first encounter was in a hotel room in Owerri, in 2015, where he displayed rare qualities that set him apart from his contemporaries: his sense of humour, his values as a father and an actor, as well as his impeccable command of the English language. The second encounter was at his Trans Ekulu, Enugu residence in 2022. During the encounter, Ebubedike was in his element. His imposing duplex dotted with images of his artistic journey, laurels and his image as the godfather of the Nigerian movie industry set the tone for the timeless conversation. In real life, he was a man of honour and class. When you were with him, you would not be tired of laughing. item.content:encoded: By Benjamin Njoku When Vanguard encountered Pete Edochie, the Lion of Africa in his den on two different occasions, it was never just an interview.It was an audience with a king. Ebubedike sat on his throne, spoke in proverbs, laughed loudly, sipped from a glass of fresh palm wine and dropped revelations that have now become timeless. Those conversations carried the full weight of Pete Edochie and what he represented on the big screen and in real life. The first encounter was in a hotel room in Owerri, in 2015, where he displayed rare qualities that set him apart from his contemporaries: his sense of humour, his values as a father and an actor, as well as his impeccable command of the English language. The second encounter was at his Trans Ekulu, Enugu residence in 2022. During the encounter, Ebubedike was in his element. His imposing duplex dotted with images of his artistic journey, laurels and his image as the godfather of the Nigerian movie industry set the tone for the timeless conversation. When you were eventually ushered into his living room, you were bound to appreciate why Chinua Achebe preferred to call him ‘Ebubedike’ after the iconic role he played as Okonkwo in the NTA adaptation of the classic novel, ‘Things Fall Apart.’ The Lion of Africa roared as he sat on his throne, “You are welcome to my home, feel comfortable.” Indeed, Pete Edochie was inseparable from his movie characters. In real life, he was a man of honour and class. When you were with him, you would not be tired of laughing. Intermittently, he would smile to encourage his guests while sharing his story passionately with them. As we recount those encounters spanning our august visit to him in Enugu in 2022, his repeated battles with rumours of his death, his reflections on Nollywood, family and mortality, now read like a final testament after his death on Wednesday, due to prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His love for classical music Beyond acting, Pete Edochie was an ardent lover of classical music and once presented a programme called ‘Music from the Masters’ while working as a broadcaster with Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Corporation, ENBC and the Anambra State Broadcasting Service. Recalling how he developed the passion for classical music, the movie legend revealed that his wife influenced his interest in classical music. “My wife influenced me. She was very fond of classical music. When I met her she looked me in the face and said: ‘there’s something you don’t know about yourself, you are deeper than you think. You are very emotional, I see you with your friends expressing yourselves at a social gathering. But deep down, you are a very serious person’. “One day, she joined me in the preview room, where we played some classical music. At one point, when we were playing some aspects of Mozart’s songs, I got drawn into it, forcing me to go back to play it again. Before I knew what was happening, it stuck,” he told Vanguard. Edochie, however, boasted of having in his archives all the works of Mozart and George Campbell who wrote songs such as “Messiah”, “Saul”, “Solomon” among others. He confessed to placing orders for classical music from abroad, and even urged his friends travelling abroad to buy classical music for him as a gift, instead of shoes, ties and wrist watches. How he wanted to be remembered There are many things to remember Pete Edochie for. His deep baritone voice. His age-long beard. His intimidating look. His danc steps and his father-figure role in Nollywood. But beyond all of these, Ebubedike wanted to be remembered for something far simpler, and far deeper. He wanted to be remembered as a man who brought happiness and joy to many homes in Africa and beyond with his craft. Speaking with Vanguard as he celebrated his 76th birthday in 2023, Edochie opened up on his legacy, honour and fulfilment: “If people feel that my contributions toward the growth of the Nigerian movie industry have affected their lives in one way or the other, it means that posterity would award me good marks. Our industry is very challenging. While you are playing different characters in movies, you are still expected to live up to your billing as a man of honour. “People enjoy me going by their reactions to what I do. It gives me a lot of satisfaction that people think this man knows what he’s doing. If I am remembered as one who injected some life into his audiences in Nigeria and beyond, I feel accomplished,” he said. It was a simple but profound desire from a man whose career spanned more than five decades. For Edochie, acting was not just entertainment. It was a ministry. It was a service. It was a calling to heal homes with laughter, with wisdom, and with stories that mirrored real life. In his own words, all he ever wanted was to bring joy into people’s homes. And by all accounts, that is precisely what he did for more than 50 years, before bowing out of the stage. Landing role of Okonkwo in the NTA adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s ‘Things Fall Apart’ Pete Edochie did not start his journey as an actor. He started as a broadcaster in 1967 before gaining widespread recognition through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s celebrated novel, “Things Fall Apart” in the 80s. Recalling how he landed that iconic role in our 2022 interview with him, Edochie said his former colleague, the late G. C. Ugwu, recommended him for the role of Okonkwo. “He was the Zonal Director of NTA in Benin in those days. Engr Ugwu had always watched me in the broadcasting house, and the moment they decided to produce the play, the first person that came to his mind, who would play the role of Okonkwo was me”, he said. He disclosed that he had never read “Things Fall Apart” before the adaptation and his first encounter with the story was through the script. According to him, he auditioned at the University of Nigeria’s Enugu campus. In his account, the production team offered him the role after hearing him read. The performance drew attention beyond Nigeria, and the BBC team travelled to the country to interview him about it. That one role changed African television forever. It made him a household name. It made Okonkwo very popular. And it made Pete Edochie the standard by which every other African actor would be judged. Narrating the story, Edochie agreed that there was always a reflection of the Okonkwo character in most of his roles in movies. “That’s what many people said. When I started in ‘Things Fall Apart’, I was 38 years old. People still call me, “Ebubedike.” Before Chinua Achebe died, he was calling me Ebubedike. He never called me Pete, and we were very close. “Each time people visited him in America then, he would ask after me. Achebe created the character and he felt I interpreted the role excellently. He named me after Okonkwo- Ebube Dike. So, many people still see me and refer to me as an Ebubedike.” He said when the script was handed over to him, he felt it was an opportunity to read the novel since he didn’t have the privilege to do so while he was in school. “I was delighted to read the novel. Before then, I had not read it, I knew nothing about it,” Edochie stated. Ebubedike was not the only actor who auditioned for the iconic role of Okonkwo, but his talent stood him out in the crowd. According to him, “there were other actors who came for the audition held at the main auditorium of the University of Nigeria, Enugu campus. The moment I walked into the auditorium, the white woman who was invited to handle the costume and other things sighted me and screamed, ‘if this man could act, that’s the man we want for the role’. “She never met me before. I walked in and was given the script. Other people were also given the script to read, and when I read mine, they shook hands with me and said, we are good to go. They said there was no point continuing with the audition. That was how I landed the role.” Before featur

item.title: NDSU Successfully Debuts New QB vs. SJSU
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 10: Preston Brown #0 of the North Dakota State Bison runs against Kal-El Togafau #44 of the UNLV Rebels at Allegiant Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Louis Grasse/Getty Images) Getty Injuries finally caught up with North Dakota State senior quarterback Nathan Hayes after 11 games this season. His oblique injury kept him out of Friday’s game against San Jose State, so the Bison debuted freshman quarterback Preston Brown in his first career start. Brown started with a bang on a 49-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Jackson Williams in the first quarter. The Missouri native kept it going in the first half, leading four scoring drives to a 24-7 lead, and he did enough to help the Bison hold on to a 38-31 win in San Jose. Brown went 12-23 for 226 yards and a touchdown versus an interception. He also rushed for 31 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. His rushing score came when the Bison needed it most in the fourth quarter to make it 38-24, which capped a six-play, 71-yard scoring drive. Brown also had ample support for the running game in his debut with 183 yards and three touchdowns overall. Bison Skill Players Step Up Running back D.J. Scott led the way with 86 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries. Fellow running back Nyeoti Punni rushed for 34 yards on five carries. Running back Barry Kpeenu also chipped in 16 yards on five carries, and he had a 21-yard reception. Wide receiver Chris Kiel had 12 yards on two carries, and he caught a 51-yard pass. Brown also connected well with Williams in the passing game, as the lead wideout had seven catches for 117 yards and the score. Wide receiver Jordan McCants had a 20-yard reception, and Brown spread the ball around to six different pass catchers overall. NDSU Waits Next NDSU improved to 10-2 overall and will await this weekend’s Mountain West Conference results to see if they land in the title game. Winning helped the Bison if things came down to a tiebreaker based on computer ratings amid a logjam of conference teams with 6-2 league records. The Mountain West championship game is Dec. 4, and the matchup will be known after the UNLV-Nevada game on Saturday. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post NDSU Successfully Debuts New QB vs. SJSU appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Somers ends a magical season for Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football in state semifinals
item.description: The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team's season ended with a state semifinal loss to Somers on Friday in Middletown. (Jim Franco/Times Union) MIDDLETOWN - The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team put in plenty of work this season, which resulted in the Spartans tripling their win total from 2025. But on Friday evening, the Spartans' incredible turnaround season came to a crushing conclusion. The Spartans could not get anything going of consequence during the first half of the their Class A state semifinal showdown against top-ranked Somers. Meanwhile, the Tuskers produced touchdowns on all four of their offensive series in the first half and cruised to a comfortable 35-7 victory at Middletown High School. Ty Starr made sure the Spartans were not shut out when the senior took a handoff and swept off the left side for a 56-yard touchdown run with 18 seconds left in the game. "They are a really good team. We played our hearts out - everyone throughout the team, and that is that," BH-BL senior linebacker Logan Tomlinson said. "At the end of the day, they won. Good for them. Have them go win it all. We fell short." Somers (13-0) is a program with four Class A state titles to its credit since 2016, including three straight championships from 2022 to 2024. The Tuskers proved too tough for BH-BL to contain during the first half as the Section 1 champions produced touchdown drives covering 62, 81, 98 and 61 yards in establishing a 28-0 halftime cushion. "We always talk about life. Life isn't perfect," BH-BL coach Kevin DeBonis said. "We just lost to a very good team. We came out uncharacteristic. We stubbed our toes with assignments. That's what happens. Unfortunately, they exposed that. They are a very good team. It is hard to go down like that. It was sort of an avalanche early on." Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake, making its 11th state playoff appearance since 2006, hasn't reached the final since claiming the program's first state championship in 2012. A win would have sent the Spartans to the title game for the fifth time and the first with DeBonis as head coach. This season's squad ended up matching the program record for wins in a season with 12, a standard first established in 2009 and matched by the state championship squad from 14 years ago. "We had the biggest bounce back (season) of my life," Tomlinson said. "At the end of the day, we won 12 games. If we didn't do that, I would be a little bit more upset." BH-BL will bring back 30 juniors from its 2026 squad. DeBonis lauded his senior's contributions and added how proud he was regarding his squad's second-half showing Friday. "Kudos to the kids. They kept playing," DeBonis said. Tomlinson, who will play lacrosse next year at Siena, believes the returning players gained plenty from this season's playoff run. "Obviously, I hope they use it. I think they will," Tomlinson said. Key moment Somers ended up stopping BH-BL on downs at the Tuskers' 19-yard line to halt the Spartans' the second offensive series. On the next play, junior receiver Chris D'Ippolito caught a pass from Tristan Iglesias in stride near midfield. He pulled away to produce an 81-yard touchdown catch to help Somers establish a 14-0 advantage with 1:58 left in the first quarter. Star of the game Iglesias connected on 12 of 15 passes for 250 yards and two touchdowns. He also added 40 yards on the ground and scored on a 4-yard touchdown four seconds into the fourth quarter to build his team's lead to 35-0. Numbers to know 397: Yards gained by the Tuskers managed on offense, including 147 yards rushing on 30 attempts. 240: Yards of offense amassed by Burnt Hills despite its slow start to the game. 123: Receiving yards for Somers' D'Ippolito on only five receptions. The junior finished the first half with three receptions for 106 yards and one touchdown. What's next Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake: The Spartans, who were making the program's first state semifinal appearance in 10 years, conclude their season with a 12-1 record. Somers: The Tuskers will attempt to claim the program's fifth state title Dec. 4 at the JMA Wireless Dome in Syracuse. Somers will meet Section 5 champion Hilton. item.title: Spurs guards Dylan Harper, De'Aaron Fox return to action against Lakers
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper (2) walks off the court during the NBA game against the Detroit Pistons at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) The Spurs upgraded Dylan Harper and De'Aaron Fox to available for Friday night's game against the Los Angeles Lakers after the guards went through warmups. Harper returns after a four-game absence due to a hip injury. Fox is back after a two-game absence because of an injured shin. Harper, the team's second-leading scorer with an 18.4 per-game average, will come off the bench due to a minutes restriction while Fox will start. Harper, 20, returns after the Spurs originally said he would be out two to three weeks. He suffered his injury in a 105-93 loss to Detroit on Nov. 17. Coach Mitch Johnson credited Harper's swift recovery to a combination of diligent rehab and the team's "as good as it gets" medical staff. "He's done everything that's been asked of him and more," Johnson said. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: UH plays like a No. 1 to beat Oakland behind Mercy Miller's career-high 23 points
item.description: Houston guard Mercy Miller, right, collides with Oakland forward Nate Ahner, left, during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, in Houston. (AP Photo/Kevin M. Cox) (Kevin M. Cox/Associated Press) Mercy Miller set a career-high with 23 points as No. 1 Houston cruised to a 77-46 win over Oakland at the Fertitta Center on Friday night. UH (7-0) was playing its first game since moving into the top spot after sweeping three games at the Players Era 8 tournament, including wins over then-No. 1 Florida and No. 11 Kansas. Miller set his previous career-high with 21 points in the all-Big 12 final against the Jayhawks. Chendall Weaver , who received a temporary injunction Wednesday that allows him to remain eligible for the rest of the season, added 14 points and five rebounds off the bench. The Cougars jumped out to a 21-2 lead, sparked by 3-pointers by Miller and Weavers, and held the Grizzlies to just two field goals in the first 8 1/2 minutes. Joseph Tugler finished with four points, eight rebounds, three assists and one block for the Cougars, who have won 44 consecutive regular-season games against unranked opponents. Miller scored 12 of UH's first 17 points to begin the second half, pushing the lead to 58-26. He finished 7-of-10 shooting and 6-of-6 from the free-throw line. Chris Fields Jr. scored 10 points for Oakland, a member of the Horizon League that was coming off a 46-point loss at Purdue. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. item.title: Uduere Killings in Delta: Six trucks of policemen, yet bullets still found targets
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi The sound of gunfire shattered the campaign atmosphere at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, November 23. People who had gathered for a political rally suddenly scrambled for safety. Women ran, campaigners scattered and, in the ensuing chaos, bullets found human targets. By the time the shooting stopped, families had lost loved ones, several people critically wounded and communities plunged into mourning. Among the disturbing details was that six truckloads of policemen had reportedly been deployed to provide security. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, put their number at close to 50. Yet, according to accounts from both political camps, the violence escalated despite the robust security presence. The tragedy has since generated competing accusations between the All Progressives Congress, APC, and the National Democratic Congress, NDC. Beneath the political blame game are grieving families, wounded survivors and ordinary citizens asking why a political gathering should become a death trap. A Trail Of Troubled Political Gatherings Uduere was not an isolated incident in the build-up to Delta 2027 elections. September 18, a one-million-man march organised by the NDC in the Warri-Effurun axis was disrupted by violence, leaving persons wounded. An AK-47 allegedly recovered from a suspect identified as Collins became a subject of controversy between the party and police. The NDC alleged the suspect was released the following day, a claim that formed part of its subsequent complaints about police handling of the incident. October 3, the party held a 10,000-man march against hunger in Ughelli. The following day, the Ughelli North Local Government Council, chaired by Chief Jaro Egbo, issued a notice, sealed the business premises and impounded truck belonging to Tobore Alex Agbah, who led the march. Agbah would later become one of the victims of the Uduere violence. November 7, another NDC one-million-man march in Asaba ended in violence, with one fatality recorded. The recurrence of disturbances has fuelled allegations that NDC gatherings are being targeted by political opponents allegedly linked to the ruling APC. Delta State Commissioner for Information, Charles Aniagwu, however, rejected the suggestion of a pattern. “It’s not a pattern, because when you talk about a pattern, it means that it’s continuously and then you are linking it to be able to join one to the other,” he said. He argued: “The NDC is not being attacked, there are a number of local governments where we have not had any disturbances. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Egufe Yafugborhi The sound of gunfire shattered the campaign atmosphere at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, November 23. People who had gathered for a political rally suddenly scrambled for safety. Women ran, campaigners scattered and, in the ensuing chaos, bullets found human targets. By the time the shooting stopped, families had lost loved ones, several people critically wounded and communities plunged into mourning. Among the disturbing details was that six truckloads of policemen had reportedly been deployed to provide security. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, put their number at close to 50. Yet, according to accounts from both political camps, the violence escalated despite the robust security presence. The tragedy has since generated competing accusations between the All Progressives Congress, APC, and the National Democratic Congress, NDC. Beneath the political blame game are grieving families, wounded survivors and ordinary citizens asking why a political gathering should become a death trap. A Trail Of Troubled Political Gatherings Uduere was not an isolated incident in the build-up to Delta 2027 elections. September 18, a one-million-man march organised by the NDC in the Warri-Effurun axis was disrupted by violence, leaving persons wounded. An AK-47 allegedly recovered from a suspect identified as Collins became a subject of controversy between the party and police. The NDC alleged the suspect was released the following day, a claim that formed part of its subsequent complaints about police handling of the incident. October 3, the party held a 10,000-man march against hunger in Ughelli. The following day, the Ughelli North Local Government Council, chaired by Chief Jaro Egbo, issued a notice, sealed the business premises and impounded truck belonging to Tobore Alex Agbah, who led the march. Agbah would later become one of the victims of the Uduere violence. November 7, another NDC one-million-man march in Asaba ended in violence, with one fatality recorded. The recurrence of disturbances has fuelled allegations that NDC gatherings are being targeted by political opponents allegedly linked to the ruling APC. Delta State Commissioner for Information, Charles Aniagwu, however, rejected the suggestion of a pattern. “It’s not a pattern, because when you talk about a pattern, it means that it’s continuously and then you are linking it to be able to join one to the other,” he said. He argued: “The NDC is not being attacked, there are a number of local governments where we have not had any disturbances. The APC in Delta is holding sway, the underdogs in this case are the members of the NDC who are few.” But NDC governorship candidate, Chris Iyovwaye, disagreed, recalling the September incident. “Another thug of APC was caught with an AK-47 and was handed over to the police. To our surprise, he was let off the hook the very next day,” he alleged. On the Asaba attack, he said: “Every time we are exercising our democratic rights, they’re always there to stop us.” Regarding Uduere, Iyovwaye said the party had secured police approval and was promised six truckloads of policemen. “Yet the consequence of that is that four of our men are dead and 15 seriously injured, some of them still in ICU,” he said. Two Camps, Competing Accusations The Uduere violence has produced sharply conflicting accounts from Egbo and Omo-Agege. Egbo, who hails from the community, accused Omo-Agege and his entourage of instigating the violence. He claimed two of his associates, Prince Oharisi and a man identified simply as Oche, were shot dead as Omo-Agege was concluding his campaign activities. Egbo alleged that Omo-Agege arrived after APC members had secured the town hall for a ceremony. “He came there and started abusing everybody, according to what I was told, saying I was his PA, I was his boy, and all of that,” he said. He further alleged: “On his way out, he ordered one of his boys, Efemena Umukoro, Akhima, one of the NDC key mobilisers who lost his life in the melee, to open fire on our people.” Egbo also said the community’s President-General, Cosmos Ejovwoke, was attacked and killed. “I found out that they clubbed and shot the President-General of the community,” he said. He demanded investigation by the Inspector-General of Police, declaring: “You come to my community to kill my President-General, killing my people, and you don’t even feel any remorse? We must do something about it. If we continue like this, then our democracy is in danger.” Omo-Agege, however, accused Egbo and his alleged political backers of orchestrating the attack. He listed four members of his campaign organisation as dead, including former Federal Character Commissioner, Moses Anaughe, while about 15 others sustained critical injuries. He questioned why the violence occurred despite the deployment of policemen. “We went to the campaign with full expectations, that with six trucks of policemen deployed to that venue to protect us in that event, we expected protection for everybody in that venue,” he said. “It never occurred to us that they (police) were merely coming to watch me principally executed.” He added: “There is no way you have close to 50 policemen in a venue and a minute after commencement of the attack, all of them ran away and left only you there.” Survivors’ Accounts Of Blood And Bullets One of the most harrowing accounts came from Chief Evans Ivwurie, Chairman of Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation, who was shot during the violence. Ivwurie alleged that the atmosphere became tense as the rival political gatherings proceeded, adding he personally complained to police officers about gunfire from the opposing gathering. “The Policemen told me they (APC supporters) were not shooting guns, that they were shooting knockouts (fireworks). I said but you can see them brandishing pump actions openly, shooting it,” he recounted. He alleged that violence erupted while Omo-Agege was addressing the campaign. “These APC thugs led by Egbo, the LG Chairman, started throwing stones at the direction of Omo-Agege and our people gathered there. They ended throwing the stones and all of a sudden they started shooting.” As people fled, he said, he tried to establish whether Omo-Agege was safe, alleging a man identified as Gueke, chairman of Ughelli Motor Parks, shot him in the head. “Immediately he saw me at a close range, he just shot at me, on my head. The bullet was so heavy, I fell flat to the ground without any energy,” he said. He further alleged that the gunman shot Anaughe twice in the chest. Another victim, Agbah, who had earlier been affected by the council’s action following his October rally, was shot in the neck. During a visit by Peter Obi, the NDC presidential figure, Agbah, who was receiving treatment, disclosed that five bullets remained lodged in his body. “I’ve five bullets in me. I’m happy to see you Sir. The target was to kill me. There are five bullets in me now,” he told Obi. Mothers And Communities Mourn The killings have provoked emotional reactions beyond the two political camps. Peter Obi, who visited the families of slain Anaughe and Efemena Umukoro, popularly known as Akima, alongside Omo-Agege and Iyovwaye, condemned the killings. “This is totally unexpected during these campaigns period, that people would die because they have a different view or belong to a different party from the ruling party,” he said. “We cannot kill people, harm people because we want to be political leaders.” President-General of the Urhobo Progress Union, Ese Gam, expressed concern that political rivalry was tearing the Urhobo nation apart. “Now we’re not contending with others. It’s now Urhobo against Urhobo,” he said. “If we continue to kill ourselves like this in the name of fighting for power, who are we going to lead at the end of the day?” Unanswered Security Questions The reported fa

item.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
item.description: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

item.title: Saunders: Credit Steelers Veterans for Righting the Ship
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt in a game against the Denver Broncos on Nov. 27, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — I underestimated these Pittsburgh Steelers. Not in terms of their playing ability — I think we’ve got that pretty well dialed in at this point. The Steelers are a good but not great team, with a very good defense, that is capable of beating almost anyone on its best day and losing to almost anyone on its worst day. Since they first convened in July, they’ve looked a lot like a 10 or 11-win team, and they’re probably still headed for somewhere in that range after beating the Denver Broncos, 27-5 on Friday. But over the last week, that outlook certainly seemed to be in jeopardy. It started when the team was upset by the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, a dreadful loss to a hapless-looking team that featured star wide receiver DK Metcalf getting himself ejected. It continued when head coach Mike McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers came to loggerheads after practice on Tuesday. McCarthy benched Rodgers. Rodgers went nuclear, ripping McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show , and accusing him of what amounts to coaching malfeasance — sleeping through meetings, skipping practice, not getting to know his defense and more. The scene in the team’s locker room on Wednesday was surreal. The Steelers players were shell-shocked. I didn’t think there was any chance that the team I saw on Wednesday would be able to turn things around in less than two days, with Mason Rudolph filling in at quarterback with two practices under his belt. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph and general manager Omar Khan at practice on Nov. 25, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The downgrade from a well-prepared Rodgers to a thrust-into-action Rudolph felt signifiant, but not nearly as significant as the mental toll of the week’s drama. I expected the Steelers to come out flat and listless against a Broncos team that is very comfortable playing a game with the air taken out of the ball. If the Steelers had another offensive start like the week before in Philly, this thing could have been over before it got started. Instead, the Steelers leaders showed up, and righted the ship. Starting Thursday at practice, Cam Heyward and T.J. Watt were men on a mission to not let the malaise of Wednesday bleed into Friday’s game — and potentially sink the season. Their passion set up an inspired practice session on the holiday — usually a short day of work in NFL land. Rudolph stayed at the facility long after the practice ended, working hand-in-hand with McCarthy to try to get the offense dialed in. That work mattered, but not nearly as much as the direction this team’s leaders set for the team. “What came out of it was urgency,” McCarthy said. “I thought our leaders did a tremendous job of bringing the urgency to their rooms, and it definitely showed up.
