item.content:encoded: Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt in a game against the Denver Broncos on Nov. 27, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — I underestimated these Pittsburgh Steelers. Not in terms of their playing ability — I think we’ve got that pretty well dialed in at this point. The Steelers are a good but not great team, with a very good defense, that is capable of beating almost anyone on its best day and losing to almost anyone on its worst day. Since they first convened in July, they’ve looked a lot like a 10 or 11-win team, and they’re probably still headed for somewhere in that range after beating the Denver Broncos, 27-5 on Friday. But over the last week, that outlook certainly seemed to be in jeopardy. It started when the team was upset by the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, a dreadful loss to a hapless-looking team that featured star wide receiver DK Metcalf getting himself ejected. It continued when head coach Mike McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers came to loggerheads after practice on Tuesday. McCarthy benched Rodgers. Rodgers went nuclear, ripping McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show , and accusing him of what amounts to coaching malfeasance — sleeping through meetings, skipping practice, not getting to know his defense and more. The scene in the team’s locker room on Wednesday was surreal. The Steelers players were shell-shocked. I didn’t think there was any chance that the team I saw on Wednesday would be able to turn things around in less than two days, with Mason Rudolph filling in at quarterback with two practices under his belt. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph and general manager Omar Khan at practice on Nov. 25, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The downgrade from a well-prepared Rodgers to a thrust-into-action Rudolph felt signifiant, but not nearly as significant as the mental toll of the week’s drama. I expected the Steelers to come out flat and listless against a Broncos team that is very comfortable playing a game with the air taken out of the ball. If the Steelers had another offensive start like the week before in Philly, this thing could have been over before it got started. Instead, the Steelers leaders showed up, and righted the ship. Starting Thursday at practice, Cam Heyward and T.J. Watt were men on a mission to not let the malaise of Wednesday bleed into Friday’s game — and potentially sink the season. Their passion set up an inspired practice session on the holiday — usually a short day of work in NFL land. Rudolph stayed at the facility long after the practice ended, working hand-in-hand with McCarthy to try to get the offense dialed in. That work mattered, but not nearly as much as the direction this team’s leaders set for the team. “What came out of it was urgency,” McCarthy said. “I thought our leaders did a tremendous job of bringing the urgency to their rooms, and it definitely showed up. So we were able to complete our preparation process yesterday, everybody was able to get to where they should be with their families in the evening, and you definitely saw the urgency today.” Pittsburgh Steelers defensive captain Cam Heyward in a game against the Detroit Lions on Dec. 21, 2025. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Watt and Heyward are career Steelers. They’re two of the best players to ever wear black and gold and when they’re done playing, they have dates with gold jackets waiting. But there are still some in this town that doubt their abilities as leaders, because they haven’t had much postseason success. Let’s put that to rest right now. After lighting a fire under the team on Thursday, Heyward and Watt and Jalen Ramsey pulled the same trick on Friday with a passionate pregame speech that had the locker room buzzing after the game. “I ain’t gonna lie, for the past couple days, we kind of, as players, we [talked],” Ramsey said. “We were like, ‘Coach, you good. Let us turn this up. Let us get in our zone,’” Ramsey said. “T.J., he got in his zone. Cam did the same thing.” “There was a lot going on this week,” Heyward said. “I can’t say enough about the men just locking back in. The situation happens, and it can go one of two ways. For our group to just strengthen and hold each other accountable and move forward, I think is huge. Our guys did that today.” At one point on the postgame Amazon Prime Video broadcast, Heyward was asked what Mike McCarthy’s message to the team was at halftime. “What did he say?” Heyward asked his teammates. “I don’t think he said anything.” That says it all. Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now McCarthy was under fire this week. And players were still not disputing the veracity of Rodgers’ allegations. There remains a frostiness between the head coach and especially the team’s defense, which McCarthy admitted he needs to spend more time with. Heyward was asked if he thinks things will be better in the future after the drama of the week and answered only, “we’ll see.” Posed the same question, Watt said, “Time will tell.” That’s not exactly a glowing endorsement. It mostly seems that whatever resentment the Steelers players have for their beleaguered head coach, they hate losing a heck of a lot more. With the offense most impacted by the week’s events, the defense needed to step up and carry them for a little bit today. They did that and then some, essentially winning the game on their own. The Steelers defense scored 14 points off turnovers and allowed only three. “Yeah, after the last two games, we haven’t provided short fields,” Heyward said. “We haven’t provided splash enough, and I thought we did that today. I thought we took care of the run early, got a touchdown by T.J. and a touchdown by Jalen. Just giving them a little bit more short fields. When things are just a little bit gone awry, I think you’ve got to provide that for your oﬀense.” They also did it from the very beginning of the game. The crowd at Acrisure Stadium on Friday was reflective of the weird week the team had. There were “Go, Pack Go,” chants, mocking McCarthy’s blunder in Philly the week before, and also “F*** Aaron Rodgers” chants. But if things went sideways, if the Steelers started like they had the week before, the restlessness could have gotten awfully loud. “Huge,” Watt said. “I mean, keeping the crowd into it — the crowd was incredible tonight from the start. We most definitely feed oﬀ of them and they kept us going throughout the whole night.” Instead, it was Watt with a huge play to open the game, scoring a touchdown on a first-quarter fumble recover that put the Steelers ahead for good. T.J. WATT RECOVERS THE FUMBLE FOR A STEELERS TD 😱 (via @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/Iek29UL6jD — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 27, 2026 This is not a great Steelers team. It will face challenges down the way from an Xs and Os and talent-level standpoints. They don’t have a quarterback like a Joe Burrow, a Josh Allen or a Patrick Mahomes. But if the challenge is mental, a question of fortitude or toughness or the ability to bring people together in the pursuit of a common goal, then don’t count the Steelers out. They’ll prove you wrong. Trust me, I know. Related Headlines Howe It Happened: The Steelers Funeral That Wasn’t Jalen Ramsey Heaps Praise on Emerging Steelers Rookie Steelers Now Postgame: Steelers 27, Broncos 5 Read more at Steelers Now

item.description: NCAA women's soccer tournament schedule 2026: TV channels, times, live streams, scores for every college game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NCAA women's soccer tournament is back, with a blend of familiar powers and emerging programs set to strive for a national championship. While the regular season indicates there should be several legitimate contenders to lift the trophy in Cary, North Carolina, there is one safe bet entering the tournament: The ACC will play a prominent role. At least one ACC team has appeared in the championship game each of the last eight years, with a conference team bringing home the national title each of the last three years. Florida State took the 2025 and 2023 crowns, but the Seminoles have looked mortal this year as the sport's most decorated program has reemerged. North Carolina, which won its 22nd national championship two years ago, looks like the team to beat once again after taking the ACC title. There will be challengers, though. Vanderbilt suffered its first loss of the season in the SEC quarterfinals and is looking for its first NCAA title, along with a trio of Big Ten teams in Purdue, Michigan State and Ohio State. Who will emerge from the 64-team field? Here's all you need to know to watch every game. item.title: The M5 MacBook Air just got its biggest discount since Apple raised the price
item.description: The M5-powered MacBook Air is $300 off in both size configurations for Black Friday. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge If you’ve been holding off on buying a new MacBook Air since Apple raised prices by $200 in June , you’re in luck. The 13-inch M5 MacBook Air is on sale at Amazon and Best Buy with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage starting at $999 ($300 off) for Black Friday, which is the lowest price we’ve seen since the hike. If you want a larger display, Amazon and Best Buy are also taking $300 off the otherwise identical 15-inch model with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, dropping it to $1,199. Apple MacBook Air 13 (M5) Where to Buy: $1299 $999 at Amazon (512GB) $1299 $999 at Best Buy (512GB) $1599 $1199 at Amazon (1TB) Apple MacBook Air 15 (M5) Where to Buy: $1299 $1199 at Amazon (512GB) $1299 $1199 at Best Buy (512GB) $1799 $1499 at Amazon (1TB) The M5-equipped MacBook Air is a good middle ground if you need more power than the MacBook Neo — which, thanks to a $100 discount , is $599 — but don’t want to splurge on a MacBook Pro. Its faster chip, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage make it better suited for multitasking and creative work in apps like Photoshop and Premiere. You also get a higher-resolution display, better speakers, a backlit keyboard that makes typing in the dark easier, and faster ports. Plus, its sharper webcam supports Apple’s Center Stage feature, which automatically adjusts the framing to keep you in view during video calls. Of course, the Air can’t match the performance or higher-end displays you can get with a MacBook Pro, whether you opt for an M5 model , the newer M5 Pro model with a PROLED XDR Display , or one of the M6-powered machines . A Pro may be worth the extra money if you regularly edit video or work on more demanding creative projects. But if you mostly need a laptop for work, browsing, and occasional photo or video editing, the M5 Air is more than capable. Read our M5-powered MacBook Air review .

item.title: Steelers Crowd Caught Hurling Profane Chants at Aaron Rodgers During Amazon Prime Broadcast Amid McCarthy Controversy
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA – NOVEMBER 22: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers 8 reacts during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburg Steelers on November 22nd, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire NFL, American Football Herren, USA NOV 22 Steelers vs Eagles EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon261122235 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Aaron Rodgers thought he was dropping the final word on his messy divorce from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this week when he blasted head coach Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show. Instead, the 42-year-old quarterback found himself caught in the crosshairs of Acrisure Stadium on Black Friday, even though he was “barred” from the facility. As the Steelers dismantled the Denver Broncos in a dominant 27-5 victory (broadcast on Amazon Prime Video), the home crowd let their feelings known through a profane chant. “F— you Rodgers,” the fans shouted in unison in the fourth quarter of the game on Friday. Even sports reporter Kari Anderson highlighted this in her coverage, saying, “A chant of “F*** you Rodgers” from some Steelers fans is audible on the broadcast. So far, this has been a dominant form of revenge for Pittsburgh after everything that went down with Aaron Rodgers this week.” Meanwhile, Rodgers couldn’t even enter the Steelers facility to confront the higher-ups. So he decided to put his voice up on McAfee’s talk show. The quarterback even sent a text message to play-by-play commentator Al Michaels, trying to justify why he went to McAfee’s show after Michaels called the blowout. When NFL crowds cross the line, it reshapes the narrative around the game itself. Stay subscribed for the analysis behind the headlines and what it means for the league. “A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room,” Rodgers told play-by-play broadcaster Al Michaels through a text message. “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. item.content:encoded: PHILADELPHIA, PA – NOVEMBER 22: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers 8 reacts during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburg Steelers on November 22nd, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire NFL, American Football Herren, USA NOV 22 Steelers vs Eagles EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon261122235 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Aaron Rodgers thought he was dropping the final word on his messy divorce from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this week when he blasted head coach Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show. Instead, the 42-year-old quarterback found himself caught in the crosshairs of Acrisure Stadium on Black Friday, even though he was “barred” from the facility. As the Steelers dismantled the Denver Broncos in a dominant 27-5 victory (broadcast on Amazon Prime Video), the home crowd let their feelings known through a profane chant. “F— you Rodgers,” the fans shouted in unison in the fourth quarter of the game on Friday. Even sports reporter Kari Anderson highlighted this in her coverage, saying, “A chant of “F*** you Rodgers” from some Steelers fans is audible on the broadcast. So far, this has been a dominant form of revenge for Pittsburgh after everything that went down with Aaron Rodgers this week.” Meanwhile, Rodgers couldn’t even enter the Steelers facility to confront the higher-ups. So he decided to put his voice up on McAfee’s talk show. The quarterback even sent a text message to play-by-play commentator Al Michaels, trying to justify why he went to McAfee’s show after Michaels called the blowout. When NFL crowds cross the line, it reshapes the narrative around the game itself. Stay subscribed for the analysis behind the headlines and what it means for the league. “A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room,” Rodgers told play-by-play broadcaster Al Michaels through a text message. “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leak at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee.” It seemed like a jab at Tom Brady, who had criticized Rodgers on Thursday for violating the “sanctity of an NFL locker room” during his appearance on FOX Sports. Rodgers was certainly shocked earlier in the week when he received a phone call from tight end Pat Freiermuth and learned that he was being benched for the Week 12 game. In retaliation, the quarterback took to The Pat McAfee Show and lashed out at head coach Mike McCarthy for putting him on the sideline. What irked him was the fact that McCarthy didn’t even bring up the word “benching” during their previous conversations. “Last Wednesday, we’re in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring,” Rogers revealed on The Pat McAfee Show. “Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. Less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened. “Doesn’t come to the first walkthrough. Doesn’t come to the protection walkthrough on Thursday. Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don’t have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason in Philly. And then comes Sunday, when obviously we struggled, and the product wasn’t great.” He further ripped into the head coach’s lack of interest in the defense. Well, according to Rodgers, McCarthy blatantly refused to lean into the defensive players. He went on to criticize McCarthy for mistaking the Steelers for the Green Bay Packers during halftime. On the other hand, Mason Rudolph stepped into the starting lineup in place of Rodgers and helped Pittsburgh cruise to a statement win. He played clean, turnover-free football. The quarterback completed 9-of-15 passes for 142 yards and one touchdown. It’s worth noting that the Broncos were 8-2 coming into the game. Yet, the Steelers’ defense didn’t let it score more than five points. Rodgers’ text message did little to dampen the celebration in the Steel City. Snapping a two-game losing streak and improving to 7-4, McCarthy and Rudolph delivered the loudest possible response on the field. Meanwhile, the Steelers fans proved that they have already moved on from their former quarterback through their chants in the final quarter of the Week 12 game. item.title: The absolute best Black Friday deals you can still get
item.description: Black Friday is nearly over, but many of this year’s best deals are still available. You can still find some of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games , wireless earbuds , TVs , robot vacuums , and so much more. We can’t guarantee a deal you’ve had your eye on will last through Cyber Monday; however, if prior years are any indication, most will stick around through the long weekend. As usual, we sorted through thousands of deals to find the ones truly worth sharing, with an eye for the products and services we’ve tested here at The Verge . With prices up across multiple categories due to RAMageddon, some deals may not seem as big as in prior years. For example, Apple’s latest MacBook Air recently fell to its pre-price-hike level for the first time since July. That’s a deal to us, and several other discounts are taking a similar shape. As Black Friday winds down, we’ll keep providing context when possible and update this post as deals come and go. AirPods Pro 3 Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review . Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons , Andor , Toy Story 5 , and The Fantastic Four: First Steps . It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage. item.title: What's next for USWNT? USA women qualify for 2027 World Cup with win over El Salvador, gun for CONCACAF title
item.description: What's next for USWNT? USA women qualify for 2027 World Cup with win over El Salvador, gun for CONCACAF title originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The U.S. women smacked El Salvador 8-0, advancing to the CONCACAF Championship semifinals and, most importantly, qualifying for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil. That's all to say Saturday's game was meaningful, even if it was less than thrilling. The Americans led 7-0 at halftime and cruised to victory without any semblance of drama. Ashley Sanchez's hat trick was in the bag before halftime, and the Americans' victory was never in doubt. The USWNT recorded 15 shots on goal to El Salvador's zero and dominated possession at a 72-percent clip. There was no statistical category capable of making the rout seem even marginally close. Now that the USWNT has qualified for next summer's World Cup, here's what comes next in the immediate future as the team advances in continental competition. In addition to Sanchez's hat trick, Mallory Swanson, Tierna Davidson and Sophia Wilson also notched goals for the Americans. MORE: Looking ahead to the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cups USWNT advance to CONCACAF W Championship semifinals The U.S. will take the field next on Tuesday, Dec. 1, against Jamaica, with kickoff set for 8:30 p.m. ET. Jamaica advanced to the semifinals by virtue of a 3-0 win over Costa Rica and will look to stay hot and score an upset against a heavily favored USA squad. The USWNT has won three straight CONCACAF W Championship titles and has only failed to win the competition twice, in 1998 and 2010, when Canada won both times. When does the 2027 Women's World Cup begin? The 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup will take place in Brazil starting on June 24, 2027 and running for almost exactly a month. The final will be on July 25 in Rio de Janeiro at the famous Maracana Stadium. The draw for the World Cup will be held on December 11 at the Museum of Modern Art in Rio, solidifying the entire group stage with the exception of the three intercontinental playoff qualifiers.
item.content:encoded: What's next for USWNT? USA women qualify for 2027 World Cup with win over El Salvador, gun for CONCACAF title originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The U.S. women smacked El Salvador 8-0, advancing to the CONCACAF Championship semifinals and, most importantly, qualifying for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil. That's all to say Saturday's game was meaningful, even if it was less than thrilling. The Americans led 7-0 at halftime and cruised to victory without any semblance of drama. Ashley Sanchez's hat trick was in the bag before halftime, and the Americans' victory was never in doubt. The USWNT recorded 15 shots on goal to El Salvador's zero and dominated possession at a 72-percent clip. There was no statistical category capable of making the rout seem even marginally close. Now that the USWNT has qualified for next summer's World Cup, here's what comes next in the immediate future as the team advances in continental competition. In addition to Sanchez's hat trick, Mallory Swanson, Tierna Davidson and Sophia Wilson also notched goals for the Americans. MORE: Looking ahead to the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cups USWNT advance to CONCACAF W Championship semifinals The U.S. will take the field next on Tuesday, Dec. 1, against Jamaica, with kickoff set for 8:30 p.m. ET. Jamaica advanced to the semifinals by virtue of a 3-0 win over Costa Rica and will look to stay hot and score an upset against a heavily favored USA squad. The USWNT has won three straight CONCACAF W Championship titles and has only failed to win the competition twice, in 1998 and 2010, when Canada won both times. When does the 2027 Women's World Cup begin? The 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup will take place in Brazil starting on June 24, 2027 and running for almost exactly a month. The final will be on July 25 in Rio de Janeiro at the famous Maracana Stadium. The draw for the World Cup will be held on December 11 at the Museum of Modern Art in Rio, solidifying the entire group stage with the exception of the three intercontinental playoff qualifiers.

item.title: Michigan hoops coach provides injury updates on two pieces of rotation
item.description: LAS VEGAS — The Wolverines were without two rotation players in their third and final game of the Players Era 16 tournament at T-Mobile Arena. Starting guard Roddy Gayle Jr. and reserve forward Oscar Goodman were both sidelined and watched Michigan’s 98-69 win over Kansas State from the bench on Friday, Nov. 27. Gayle had his left foot in a boot a day after he was hurt in the Nov. 26 loss against Miami (Fla.) . The injury occurred in the second half when Gayle appeared to roll his left ankle on a drive to the rim. He needed assistance from trainer Chris Williams to get off the court and was on crutches afterward. “He's got a sprained ankle. We held him out today because he really couldn't put pressure on it,” coach Mike Boynton Jr. said. “We don't have our resources to the full capacity here in the hotel. When we get back (to Ann Arbor), we’ll do some more X-rays, make sure there's nothing further there. “But at this point, we think he's going to be fine. We think it'll be a short-term deal. We'll get a better evaluation when we get back to Ann Arbor.” Ricky Liburd replaced Gayle in the lineup and made his first start. For Gayle, who’s averaging 11.7 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 26.1 minutes, it marked the first game he’s missed this season and third game overall in his three years at Michigan. Goodman, who’s averaging 3.5 points and three rebounds, missed his second straight game with what Boynton described as a “minor” issue. According to a program spokesperson, a medical issue occurred with Goodman shortly after the Nov. 24 loss to Creighton . “Just another evaluation when we get back to Ann Arbor, kind of check his status,” Boynton said. With Gayle and Goodman unavailable against Kansas State, Michigan received a big lift from transfer guard Kenny Noland and freshman guard Joseph Hartman. The two combined for 21 of Michigan 32 bench points and turned in their best outings yet. Noland tied his season high with 11 points and dished out seven of Michigan’s 27 assists. Hartman, who made his debut against Creighton after recovering from a preseason shoulder injury, tallied 10 points on 4-for-5 shooting, three assists and two steals in just his third collegiate game. “We think both of those guys can really help us long-term,” Boynton said. “Kenny, we were very intentional about bringing him into our program once we lost L.J. (Cason), having a guy who can be a pretty high floor backup point guard for us. “Joe unfortunately dealt with an injury in the last month or so that's kept him out. But he was trending this way right before that and injuries are part of the game. Good to see him get out there. I think he's going to be a guy that continues to grow. He plays with positive spirit. He makes winning plays. He plays super unselfishly.” Michigan will return to action when it hosts Mississippi Valley State at Crisler Center on Tuesday, Dec. 1. It’ll be Michigan’s first home game in over two weeks after playing its past four games on the road

item.title: Maple Leafs Announce Multi-Year Contract for Defenseman
item.description: TORONTO, ONTARIO - MAY 4: John Chayka speaks at a press conference where he was announced as General Manager of the Toronto Maple Leafs and Mats Sundin was introduced as Senior Executive Advisor of Hockey Operations at Real Sports Bar & Grill on May 4, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Michael Chisholm/Getty Images) Getty John Chayka Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs have managed to win two straight games following what was a truly miserable nine-game losing skid that sank them to the bottom of the Atlantic Division standings. The Maple Leafs, who lost defenseman Chris Tanev during Friday’s 3-1 win over the divisional rival Boston Bruins, have announced that they’ve signed 2026 second-round pick Alexander Bilecki, who is currently playing with the OHL’s Kitchener Rangers, to an entry-level contract. The Toronto Maple Leafs Have Signed 2026 Draft Pick Alexander Bilecki To An Entry-Level COntract Getty John Chayka On Friday, the Maple Leafs announced that they had signed 2026 Draft selection Alexander Bilecki to an entry-level contract. “We’ve signed defenceman Alexander Bilecki to a three-year entry-level contract,” the Maple Leafs reported on X, formerly known as Twitter. Soon afterwards, Maple Leafs fans began expressing their approval with the move. “Great to reward his OHL play this season with the contract now,” one fan said. “Great news. Kid looks great this season,” another fan wrote. Another fan said, “WELL YEAH. Would be horrifically dumb if you didn’t.” This fan wrote , “What a snipe by Chayka in the late second round.” Finally, this fan said , “Well deserved. Been a helluva player to start the year in the O.” So far this season with the Kitchener Rangers, Bilecki has scored five goals while adding 23 assists, along with a plus-16 rating. “Just more mature and playing in every situation, power play, penalty kill, overtime, four on four, whatever it may be, being the guy that is relied upon,” Bilecki explained about his playing style via The Toronto Sun . “I’m going out there to help the team win. If I have to lay a hit, block a shot, make a play in the O-zone or score a goal … being able to do it all and being an X factor on the back end for us (is important).” The Maple Leafs Lost Chris Tanev During Friday’s Win The Maple Leafs, despite picking up their second straight win, lost defenseman Chris Tanev, who missed all but 11 games with injuries last season. “Didn’t finish. Never a good sign for me. I don’t have an update. When a guy’s night’s over, it’s never great,” said head coach Jim Hiller. “I just feel really bad for him. He’s obviously missed quite a bit of hockey over the last couple of years. He loves to play, and you just feel bad for him when he’s not able to be out there,” Hiller said. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Maple Leafs Announce Multi-Year Contract for Defenseman appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Jasprit Bumrah overlooked for MI captaincy, reportedly rejects Rohit Sharma's deputy role: Is his future with MI in doubt?
item.description: Jasprit Bumrah overlooked for MI captaincy, reportedly rejects Rohit Sharma's deputy role: Is his future with MI in doubt? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mumbai Indians have officially handed the captaincy back to Rohit Sharma after three disappointing IPL seasons and a dressing room that had lost trust. Jasprit Bumrah was not considered for the top job and reportedly turned down the vice-captaincy offered to him in the first week of October. Bumrah turns 32 in December, and talk is growing that he could explore his options at the 2028 mega auction. MORE: Fans go wild as Rohit Sharma returns as MI captain Will Jasprit Bumrah leave Mumbai Indians after being overlooked for captaincy in IPL 2027? Jasprit Bumrah has been overlooked for the Mumbai Indians captaincy, and the fast bowler has reportedly said no to the chance of serving as Rohit Sharma's deputy, which has raised fresh doubts about whether his long-term future lies with the franchise. Rohit's return to the top job is now official, ending a period of uncertainty that had hung over the five-time champions for some time. The franchise made the move mainly because of its poor results across the last three IPL seasons. A bigger factor, though, was the broken trust inside the dressing room after Hardik Pandya took over as captain. The decision was in fact taken in the first week of October, well before Hardik's move to Punjab Kings was confirmed, which suggests the management had already made up its mind on the way forward, as reported by India Today . Mumbai Indians did not turn to Suryakumar Yadav, even though he led India to the T20 World Cup title earlier this year. Bumrah and Tilak Varma, who is currently India's T20 vice-captain, were not seriously looked at either. MORE: Rohit back as MI captain: Inside story of how MI convinced 'Hitman' to take over The franchise has its own reasons for leaving Suryakumar out, and those haven't been made public. Tilak, on the other hand, is still seen as a player who needs more time to develop into a leader. That leaves the question of Bumrah, who is among the most valuable members of the squad. Mumbai Indians don't name a regular vice-captain, but they do need a senior figure to step in when the skipper is unavailable. Suryakumar and Bumrah shared those duties last season while Hardik was out. The franchise did approach Bumrah, but with an offer of the vice-captaincy rather than the top job, since Rohit had already been picked as captain. The offer came from the top leadership in the first week of October. Bumrah politely turned it down, and he alone knows his reasons. His own earlier words add some context. When he was given the stand-in captain's job for the 2026 season, he spoke about how unexpected it all felt. "I didn't think that I will be a Test captain before becoming the MI captain." Jasprit Bumrah has been overlooked for the Mumbai Indians captaincy, and the fast bowler has reportedly said no to the chance of serving as Rohit Sharma's deputy, which has raised fresh doubts about whether his long-term future lies with the franchise. Rohit's return to the top job is now official, ending a period of uncertainty that had hung over the five-time champions for some time. The franchise made the move mainly because of its poor results across the last three IPL seasons. A bigger factor, though, was the broken trust inside the dressing room after Hardik Pandya took over as captain. The decision was in fact taken in the first week of October, well before Hardik's move to Punjab Kings was confirmed, which suggests the management had already made up its mind on the way forward, as reported by India Today . Mumbai Indians did not turn to Suryakumar Yadav, even though he led India to the T20 World Cup title earlier this year. Bumrah and Tilak Varma, who is currently India's T20 vice-captain, were not seriously looked at either. MORE: Rohit back as MI captain: Inside story of how MI convinced 'Hitman' to take over The franchise has its own reasons for leaving Suryakumar out, and those haven't been made public. Tilak, on the other hand, is still seen as a player who needs more time to develop into a leader. That leaves the question of Bumrah, who is among the most valuable members of the squad. Mumbai Indians don't name a regular vice-captain, but they do need a senior figure to step in when the skipper is unavailable. Suryakumar and Bumrah shared those duties last season while Hardik was out. The franchise did approach Bumrah, but with an offer of the vice-captaincy rather than the top job, since Rohit had already been picked as captain. The offer came from the top leadership in the first week of October. Bumrah politely turned it down, and he alone knows his reasons. His own earlier words add some context. When he was given the stand-in captain's job for the 2026 season, he spoke about how unexpected it all felt. "I didn't think that I will be a Test captain before becoming the MI captain." MORE: ‘There is a deeper issue here’: R Ashwin warns Rohit Sharma's return won't solve Mumbai Indians' problems BCCI/Creimas What next for Bumrah ahead of the 2028 IPL mega auction? Rohit is well known for his man-management, and there is a strong chance he will lead the side for at least two more years, possibly longer. Bumrah will turn 32 early in December, so this may well have been his best and perhaps last real shot at captaining the team. With the top hierarchy looking past him for the leadership group, it remains to be seen whether the moody fast bowler will weigh his choices when the next mega auction takes place before the 2028 season. MORE: Khawaja admits speaking earlier would have ended career; Smith told him to 'shut up' Mumbai Indians may have misread Bumrah Mumbai Indians have been sensible in bringing Rohit back, since the team needed calm and a leader the players trust. Where the franchise may have slipped is in how it handled Bumrah, who has given them more than a decade of service and still isn't being offered the real prize. A vice-captaincy offer to a bowler who has already led the side must have felt, to him at least, like a polite way of saying he wasn't in the long-term plans. His refusal is easy to understand. A player of his stature, who took a pay-cut-free retention deal at Rs 18 crore and kept delivering, would want to be seen as a leader and not as a backup. Fast bowlers also have a short shelf life, and at 32 he can't wait around for a role that may never come. That said, walking away would be a big call. Mumbai is where he became Bumrah, and no other franchise will offer the same comfort and history. The sensible path is an open conversation between the player and the management well before the 2028 auction, because losing him to a rival would hurt far more than any captaincy row. If the talks fail, Mumbai Indians will have only themselves to blame. item.title: How Tinubu fought Obasanjo to reclaim Lagos coastline – Fashola
item.description: By Juliet Umeh As the 2027 general elections draw closer, political defections, shifting alliances and questions about leadership are beginning to shape the debate over who should govern Nigeria for another four years. But for former Lagos State Governor, Mr Babatunde Fashola, one important test for anyone seeking to lead the country is the ability to build relationships, work with others and remain committed to a political team, even in difficult times. Fashola believes President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated these qualities, arguing that his ability to retain political associates and bring former opponents into his camp makes him better placed to manage Nigeria’s diversity. In a pointed challenge to opposition leaders, the former governor asked voters to examine what happened to the people who worked with other presidential contenders and why many of them were no longer in their political camps. Speaking during an interview on Arise Television, Fashola said political relationships should serve as a reference point for assessing the leadership capacity of those seeking the presidency. “Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question. For those who want to vote, where are all the people who worked with these people? Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him when he was governor still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so, out of office, when he wasn’t a president,” he said. According to him, the ability to work with people is essential for anyone entrusted with managing a country as diverse as Nigeria. “If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team. And you don’t just get up and jump away when there’s a crisis in the fold,” he said. Fashola noted that Tinubu remained in the All Progressives Congress, APC, despite internal disagreements, while some political leaders had abandoned parties that helped build their political careers. He also pointed to Tinubu’s ability to bring former opponents into his political fold, describing it as evidence of his capacity to build relationships across political divides. “Not just those who worked with him before, those who opposed him are now working with him. item.content:encoded: By Juliet Umeh As the 2027 general elections draw closer, political defections, shifting alliances and questions about leadership are beginning to shape the debate over who should govern Nigeria for another four years. But for former Lagos State Governor, Mr Babatunde Fashola, one important test for anyone seeking to lead the country is the ability to build relationships, work with others and remain committed to a political team, even in difficult times. Fashola believes President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated these qualities, arguing that his ability to retain political associates and bring former opponents into his camp makes him better placed to manage Nigeria’s diversity. In a pointed challenge to opposition leaders, the former governor asked voters to examine what happened to the people who worked with other presidential contenders and why many of them were no longer in their political camps. Speaking during an interview on Arise Television, Fashola said political relationships should serve as a reference point for assessing the leadership capacity of those seeking the presidency. “Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question. For those who want to vote, where are all the people who worked with these people? Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him when he was governor still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so, out of office, when he wasn’t a president,” he said. According to him, the ability to work with people is essential for anyone entrusted with managing a country as diverse as Nigeria. “If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team. And you don’t just get up and jump away when there’s a crisis in the fold,” he said. Fashola noted that Tinubu remained in the All Progressives Congress, APC, despite internal disagreements, while some political leaders had abandoned parties that helped build their political careers. He also pointed to Tinubu’s ability to bring former opponents into his political fold, describing it as evidence of his capacity to build relationships across political divides. “Not just those who worked with him before, those who opposed him are now working with him. That’s how he has built a coalition of 30 state governors from one state, from Lagos. And that is profound, whether you like him or not,” he said. Why I refused to join another party Fashola’s argument about political loyalty also reflects his own experience as Lagos governor, when he said he resisted pressure to abandon his political platform in exchange for certain benefits from the Federal Government. He recalled that during a meeting with a former President, an unnamed governor suggested that Lagos would only regain access to Lagos House, Marina, if he joined the ruling party at the time. Fashola said he rejected the condition, insisting that political conviction should not be traded for government privileges. “I said, look, Mr President, if that is the condition, keep the house. And as long as I am alive, I won’t join your party. If unfortunately I die, and they bring my body into your party, I’ll wake up,” he recalled. He said his administration also faced disagreements with the Federal Government over issues including approval for the proposed Lekki Port and access to funds belonging to Lagos State. How Tinubu fought Obasanjo over Lagos coastline Fashola also defended Tinubu’s claim that he played a major role in efforts to protect the Lagos coastline from the Atlantic Ocean, particularly around Victoria Island. He recalled that the Federal Government had spent about N4 billion pumping sand to protect the coastline, but erosion continued to threaten properties and infrastructure. According to him, Tinubu repeatedly wrote to former President Olusegun Obasanjo seeking approval for a lasting solution, but the requests were initially rejected. Fashola, who served as Tinubu’s Chief of Staff at the time, said he personally drafted several of the letters. “I drafted those letters on his instructions to President Obasanjo every time. President Obasanjo would reply, no. The last one, I think it was something like, almost like, look, get out of my life, I will find a copy of the letter. I still have it in my records,” he said. He said about seven letters were written, with Tinubu insisting that the administration should continue pressing for approval. “Nobody should take the credit away from him. I was his Chief of Staff,” Fashola said, maintaining that Tinubu deserved recognition for the initiative. Certificate controversy, foreign trips On the controversy surrounding Tinubu’s academic records, Fashola described the debate as a distraction from pressing national issues, arguing that attention should instead be focused on the cost of living, fuel prices, employment, education and security. “How does this (controversy on certificate) reduce the cost of living crisis? No, how does that reduce the cost of fuel? How does it reduce their travel time? How does it pay their children’s school fees, which NELFUND does? How does it create jobs?” he asked. He also defended the President’s foreign trips, while acknowledging that Nigerians had the right to demand explanations about public spending. “Nigerians are entitled to ask questions about their president’s utilisation of the time and resources,” he said. However, he challenged opposition parties to go beyond criticising the administration and present practical alternatives to its policies. He argued that international engagements could support investment, infrastructure development and service delivery. Funsho Williams: Fashola seeks better investigations Away from the 2027 political debate, Fashola reflected on the unresolved murder of former Lagos governorship aspirant, Funsho Williams, who was killed at his Ikoyi residence in July 2006. Following the discharge and acquittal of the six men charged over the case in 2014, Fashola expressed sympathy with the Williams family, describing the late politician as a peaceful man and an outstanding public servant. “Funsho Williams was a man of peace, a fine gentleman, an outstanding public servant. No one deserved to be treated the way he was cruelly murdered,” he said. He said the case demonstrated the need for more effective police investigations and the use of forensic tools, including DNA analysis and fingerprint evidence, to identify suspects and secure convictions. Fashola also called for the prosecution of sponsors of electoral violence, arguing that holding prominent offenders accountable could discourage others. He, however, opposed the ‘rig and die’ slogan for election riggers, insisting that punishment must follow the law and respect due process. Electricity providers owe Nigerians explanation On Nigeria’s persistent electricity challenges, the former Minister of Power said electricity providers must explain their service failures to consumers. He recalled that more than 11 million Nigerians were connected to electricity during his four years as Minister of Power, adding that his administration pursued incremental improvements towards stable and uninterrupted supply. Fashola also welcomed the decentralisation of the power sector, saying greater participation by state governments could attract investment and introduce new solutions. No plans to return to politics After years in public service, Fashola said he was rebuilding his legal practice and had no immediate plans to return to elective politics. Asked whether he would consider another political contest, he suggested that his time in public office had run its course. “I’ve run as hard as I can. So it’s time to stop running. It was a very humbling privilege to have served my country. I don’t take that for granted,” he said. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Steve Oko, Regional Editor, South-East Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Ojukwu, has enthused that the future of Ndigbo is great despite their current challenges. She, however, lamented the disunity among Igbo political leaders, particularly governors in the South-East, accusing them of allowing political rivalries and personal interests to undermine the collective progress of the region. The Minister urged Ndigbo to build bridges across existing divisions and embrace unity, mutual respect and collective purpose. Mrs Ojukwu also lamented the abandonment of her late husband, the Biafran leader, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu-Ojukwu, by some political leaders who benefited from his political influence and support, accusing them of turning their backs on his legacy after attaining power. Bianca spoke at the 15th anniversary memorial of Ojukwu held at the Ojukwu Memorial Library, Owerri, Imo State, where she called for a renewed commitment to Igbo unity, peace and development. She lamented that Igbo governors had failed to demonstrate sufficient unity in addressing issues affecting the people, noting that political antagonism and mutual suspicion were weakening the region’s ability to speak with one voice. “We cannot continue to celebrate Igbo greatness while tolerating the disunity that undermines it,” she declared. The minister said Ndigbo could not demand recognition and solidarity from other ethnic groups while failing to extend the same values to one another, stressing that unity must go beyond speeches, cultural celebrations and symbolic gestures. She urged political leaders in the South-East to put aside their differences and work together for the common good, insisting that the region’s future could not be built on rivalry, personal ambition and political bitterness. Bianca expressed disappointment with some political elites who, despite benefiting from the political legacy and influence of her late husband, had abandoned him and his ideals She recalled that some politicians Ojukwu supported and campaigned for to attain political power would, upon succeeding, make removing his portrait from their offices a priority and replacing it with their own. “I know people my husband gave flag and campaigned for to gain political power, the first thing they want to do is to remove his portrait and replace it with their own,” she lamented. She said Ojukwu’s legacy should not be reduced to his military exploits, titles, speeches and political struggles, but should be reflected in his convictions, humanity and commitment to justice, dignity and the welfare of the people. Describing her late husband as a soldier, statesman, intellectual and patriarch, Bianca said his life was driven by a deep conviction that people deserved to live in dignity and without fear. Reflecting on the painful history of the Igbo, including the 1966 pogroms, displacement and civil war, she said Ojukwu’s memorial should inspire a commitment to ensuring that such tragedies never happen again. She called on traditional rulers to provide moral leadership, political leaders to rise above personal interests, and businessmen and women to invest in the homeland, while urging young people to channel their energies into innovation, enterprise and productive ventures. The minister also cautioned Igbo youths in the diaspora against the pursuit of illicit wealth, warning that criminal activities had brought disgrace to the people and landed some young people in detention rather than helping them build meaningful futures. She urged them to become worthy ambassadors of Igbo culture and contribute to creating a homeland where businesses could thrive, investors could operate confidently and families could celebrate festivities without fear. Bianca lamented the insecurity and economic difficulties in parts of the South-East, saying the region could not attract investment or encourage its people in the diaspora to return home if communities remained unsafe, businesses shut down and streets deserted. “Our land must once again become a place where our children are excited to return,” she said, stressing the need to restore confidence in the region’s business and investment climate She said Ojukwu’s ideals would only endure when they were translated into practical actions by those who inherited his legacy, noting that annual memorials alone could not adequately preserve the values of a great leader. The minister also criticised the neglect of prominent Igbo leaders and their legacies, citing the prolonged delay in completing the Zik Mausoleum. She regretted that it took former President Muhammadu Buhari to build a mausoleum for Nnamdi Azikiwe, 22 years after his death, accusing successive administrations in Anambra of failing to give the project the attention it deserved. Bianca said some leaders lived as though they were immortal but eventually faded into obscurity, unlike those whose courage, sacrifices and contributions continued to inspire generations. She thanked individuals and groups who had sustained Ojukwu’s memory through the annual memorial and particularly commended the founder of the Movement for the Actualisation of the Sovereign State of Biafra, MASSOB-BIM, Chief Ralph Uwazurike, for instituting the event. Uwazurike demands Nnamdi Kanu’s release Meanwhile, Uwazurike renewed his call for the release of detained Biafra agitator, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, insisting that he had committed no offence deserving of his continued detention. The MASSOB founder compared Kanu’s situation with that of Yoruba agitator, Sunday Igboho, who he said had been released, arguing that the difference in their circumstances was political. “Where is Sunday Igboho? Kanu didn’t commit any offence that is bigger or more sinister than that of Igboho. The only difference is that Sunday Igboho has a brother that is presently the President of Nigeria,” Uwazurike said. He added that Kanu would have been released if Peter Obi were Nigeria’s President. Uwazurike, who advocated non-violent agitation for Biafra, cautioned youths against resorting to violence, saying many had misunderstood the principles of self-determination and allowed social media narratives to distort the struggle. He urged the younger generation to embrace peaceful advocacy, insisting that violence was incompatible with the pursuit of self-determination. “I urge the new generation of indigenous people to abide by the principles of non-violence,” he said, citing Mahatma Gandhi as his inspiration. Uwazurike said he had no regrets over the sacrifices he made in the course of the Biafra struggle, including persecution and the destruction of his residence, insisting he was prepared to make even greater sacrifices if the quest could be achieved through peaceful means. “I want to even sacrifice more if Biafra could be actualised through non-violence,” he said, warning that violence would only undermine the struggle. He lamented the absence of a unifying Igbo leader since Ojukwu’s death, expressing hope that another leader with the capacity to rally the people around a common cause would emerge. Uwazurike said Ojukwu remained a rallying point for many Igbo people despite his death, adding that the memorial was also an opportunity to promote unity and preserve his ideals. He dismissed the absence of political elites at the event, saying the memorial was primarily about the people and not politicians, whom he accused of being divided by personal interests. He urged Ndigbo to preserve unity, which he described as one of Ojukwu’s enduring legacies. The event featured cultural displays, masquerades, a march-past by delegations from states in the old Eastern Region, lectures and goodwill messages. item.title: INEC tests BVAS, result portal today
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), about seven weeks before the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. He said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV, v,lidation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. Amupitan said the Commission had procured new accreditation machines and set a lower voter threshold for the actual election in January. “INEC will deploy over 1.41 million ad hoc personnel alongside 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, calibrated at a reduced threshold of 850 voters per machine,” he said. He told the gathering that the rehearsal was as much a test of coordination with security agencies as of technology. “Strategy without rehearsal is merely aspiration,” he said. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. The list gives the state, local government area, ward, polling unit and delimitation code of each selected location. It runs alphabetically from Abia State to Zamfara State, with the FCT last. Abia has 368 entries, while Adamawa follows with 452. In the FCT, 124 polling units were selected across the six area councils. Abaji, Bwari, Gwagwalada, Kuje and Kwali have 20 each, while the Municipal Area Council has 24. The exercise will simulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. INEC said the value of the exercise lies in the faults it find

item.title: Death on the River: Some who came for rescue were more interested in stealing phones, bags, money — Survivor
item.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled for survival as the overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun who is married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat that was unfit to carry the large number of passengers. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but when none was available, a local boat was brought to convey them. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after boarding, raising fears among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from one side to another, forcing passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, creating panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. She said when she resurfaced, she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, apparently to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young lady die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she was particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said, “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. People were shouting, and before we knew what was happening, the boat collapsed and started sinking.” Narrating how she managed to save herself and her children, Silas said she used her swimming skills to guide her son through the water. item.content:encoded: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled for survival as the overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun who is married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat that was unfit to carry the large number of passengers. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but when none was available, a local boat was brought to convey them. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after boarding, raising fears among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from one side to another, forcing passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, creating panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. She said when she resurfaced, she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, apparently to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young lady die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she was particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said, “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. People were shouting, and before we knew what was happening, the boat collapsed and started sinking.” Narrating how she managed to save herself and her children, Silas said she used her swimming skills to guide her son through the water. She said the situation became more dangerous when other passengers struggling under water began dragging her, forcing her to fight to free herself. She added, “When the incident happened, I told my son to remain calm and follow my instructions so that we would not perish. I know how to swim, so I was guiding him. “Suddenly, people who were trapped and struggling under the water started dragging me. I saw a bag floating and grabbed it, then gave it to my son to hold so he could stay afloat. “I had to bite the hands of those holding me underwater before they released me. I continued swimming until I was able to reach the shore. At a point, I became exhausted, but by God’s grace, I survived. “When I got to the shore and looked back into the river, I saw many people drowning. Most of them were children between the ages of two and eight, screaming for help. The children were the biggest casualties.” Silas also accused some youths who arrived from a neighbouring community of abandoning the rescue effort to fight over and steal the belongings of victims. She said she called their attention to the people drowning but they allegedly refused to help. “By the grace of God, I survived with all my children and other members of my family,” she added. ‘I LOST SEVEN FAMILY MEMBERS’ For Dr Timi Austin, the tragedy has left a painful family loss that he said would be difficult to overcome. Austin said seven members of his family, including his wife’s two younger sisters and five children, died in the accident, while the body of one of the children was yet to be recovered. He blamed the state government and the relevant maritime authorities for what he described as a failure to enforce safety regulations on the waterways. According to him, the absence of proper monitoring, passenger manifests and emergency response arrangements contributed to the tragedy. He said, “If you are to measure how I feel, I believe there will be no proper measurement for what I am going through because I am deeply pained. I don’t know how to explain the pain, but we have to leave everything to God. However, we will take this up because it shows a failed system of government. “The Bayelsa State Government and the maritime agency have failed in their responsibilities. If there was an enforcement team monitoring the maritime sector, this kind of thing would not have happened. “I am also blaming the maritime agency because there was no manifest for the boat. Some people whose family members travelled from Delta State, Lagos, Port Harcourt and other places do not even know the whereabouts of their loved ones. “Some people may still be thinking that their family members are somewhere, without knowing whether they are alive or dead. What are the authorities going to do about such people?” Austin said his wife and daughter were initially expected to be part of the journey, but his wife changed her mind at the last minute while they were at the waterfront. He said the family had been left devastated by the loss of seven relatives. “My wife’s two younger sisters died. One had just one daughter, and both of them died, leaving only her husband. The other had four children, and she and her four children died. The last daughter is yet to be found. We have not even seen the corpse of that child. “My wife and my daughter were supposed to be part of that journey. My wife was already at the waterfront where they were loading passengers, but she changed her mind at the last minute,” he said. Asked how the family intended to recover from the loss, Austin said the pain was beyond words. “I don’t even know the process of recovery because I cannot even look at their mother’s face. Losing two daughters and grandchildren, how do we recover? It will take time, but we will take it up with the government and the maritime sector. “We are also considering taking some government agencies to court. We are consulting with people within and outside the state and the country,” he added. He further accused the state government of treating the tragedy casually, insisting that an emergency response team should have been deployed to the scene immediately after the incident. According to him, the accident happened during working hours on Friday, but the government did not send an emergency team to assess the situation until after the incident had generated public concern. ‘SEVEN OUT of EIGHT FAMILY MEMBERS’ ARE DEAD’ Another bereaved family member, Ms Diepreye Timipre, said seven of the eight members of her family who travelled for the burial died in the accident. She said the victims were her uncle’s children, comprising two women and their children, while only a little child survived after someone carried her and swam to safety. She said, “Out of the eight members of my family who embarked on that journey, seven are dead, while only a small child survived. “Somebody carried the child and swam to the shore. They were my uncle’s children, two women with their children. We were able to see and identify their corpses. We are from Ukubie Community.” ‘GIVE US

item.title: 2027 Presidential poll: What will influence our votes — Nigerians
item.description: *Torn between Tinubu’s reforms, Obi’s change message, Atiku’s comeback *Say, Tinubu has capacity to take bold decisions, Obi possesses good credentials, Atiku may reduce petrol price By Dayo Johnson, Regional Editor, South West The 2027 general election is barely two months away. Some of the political parties that will be on the ballot have already hit the streets campaigning. Many of the candidates are seeking to renew the mandate that was given to them in 2023. Others who didn’t make it in the last election are back again hoping to succeed this time around. The candidates are making fresh promises. The electorate, on their part, have been speaking on what will inform their choice of who to vote for during the elections and their responses reveal an electorate pulled in sharply different directions. We did not embark on data collation but randomly spoke with some Nigerians in the southwest, southeast, south south and the northern region of the country. Backers of President Bola Tinubu defend him on his capacity to push restructuring and take bold decisions, arguing that but for him the economy would have collapsed completely, even as some concede that his reforms have yet to ease hardship. But they have hope and argue that Nigeria would be better under Tinubu in the years to come. A few voices break from the Obi-Tinubu argument entirely, backing Atiku, the ADC, or local candidates on performance. In markets, campuses and government offices, a strong current of support for Peter Obi runs through everyday voters- market women, traders, students and civil servants, who point to the rising cost of living, government borrowing and hunger for change. Another powerful theme in their responses is the widespread distrust of the electoral system itself. Many voters express lack of faith in the process and expect politicians to rig and litigate rather than accept the people’s verdict, even as the spate of ongoing violence is already scaring them. Professionals frame their choices more cautiously arguing that they will be guided by candidates’ positions on sustainable development, Niger Delta equity and resource justice rather than ethnicity or party. From conviction to civic duty to indecision, the message from the streets is clear: a wary electorate is watching, and waiting to decide amidst fears of violence. Speaking, Amaebi Clarkson, a lawyer in Lagos , said: “The Campaigns have been intense, with grandiose promises. But beyond the rhetoric, Peter Obi obviously has good credentials, with proven track records to make a good pl president. I think he has good intentions for Nigeria and is better poised to positively drive the country. “However, I prefer Tinubu to be the president at this crucial time, not because he will bring any tangible development or perform any miracle. Many voters express lack of faith in the process and expect politicians to rig and litigate rather than accept the people’s verdict, even as the spate of ongoing violence is already scaring them. Professionals frame their choices more cautiously arguing that they will be guided by candidates’ positions on sustainable development, Niger Delta equity and resource justice rather than ethnicity or party. From conviction to civic duty to indecision, the message from the streets is clear: a wary electorate is watching, and waiting to decide amidst fears of violence. Speaking, Amaebi Clarkson, a lawyer in Lagos , said: “The Campaigns have been intense, with grandiose promises. But beyond the rhetoric, Peter Obi obviously has good credentials, with proven track records to make a good pl president. I think he has good intentions for Nigeria and is better poised to positively drive the country. “However, I prefer Tinubu to be the president at this crucial time, not because he will bring any tangible development or perform any miracle. It is a known fact that the fundamental malaise of this country is its flawed structure, and the only way to salvage it is to restructure it along regional lines and give the regions the latitude to develop at their own pace. Tinubu has the stamina and the reach to push for the restructuring of the country.” For Joseph Ambakederimo, Convener of the South South Reawakening Group: “Audacity requires holding the strategic line through the immediate political noise, taking bold decisions. In governance, audacity is not political theatricality; it is the deliberate expenditure of political capital to break structural inertia. So far, President Bola Tinubu of the APC is audacity personified. The ability to take bold decisions and stand by them is what our country needs at this time. “Enough of Nigerians living in borrowed robes, let us face the headwinds once and for all. President Bola Tinubu is my choice.” In his reaction Father Joseph Opelema, a priest said: “I do not have faith in our electoral process at the moment. But at the same time, I will exercise my right by voting during the 2027 elections, in case Nigerians wake up from their slumber and make their votes count, so that mine will be counted too. “Regarding campaigns, even as politicians are campaigning, they are making alternative plans to rig the elections. They do not believe that the people have the final say; rather, they believe in the courts that will ratify their manipulations.” Prof Benjamin Okaba, a university don said: “My decision on who to vote for in the 2027 presidential election will be guided by how convinced I am about how the various candidates address sustainable development concerns affecting humanity, Nigerians generally, and my Ijaw people, not by sentiments, political affiliations, or ethnic considerations. “Nigeria is at a critical juncture and needs leadership that demonstrates vision, capacity, integrity, and genuine commitment to national unity, economic recovery, security, social justice, and inclusive development. As an Ijaw man and stakeholder in the Niger Delta struggle, I will also be guided by the place of the Niger Delta and its people in the national development agenda, particularly issues of equity, resource justice, environmental sustainability, and federalism. Ultimately, my vote will go to the candidate whose vision, antecedents, and policy commitments offer the most credible pathway towards building a just, equitable, and prosperous Nigeria for all. “As President of the Ijaw National Congress, I had presented and canvassed, on behalf of Congress, a list of prescient conditions that candidates seeking the support of the Ijaw people must demonstrate a clear understanding of and commitment to actualizing if they emerge victorious. These include the repeal of all obnoxious legislations that deny our people the right to own and manage their God-given resources.” According to Mr Benjamin Jonah, “I will vote for Peter Obi because I believe Nigeria needs a new direction and a genuine change in leadership. He has expressed the desire to make a difference, and I believe the country deserves an opportunity to explore a different approach. The cost of living is rising, things are becoming increasingly expensive, and ordinary Nigerians are struggling to survive. We cannot continue to accept the status quo while hoping for a different outcome.” Mr Aiwere Okungbowa said, “I will be voting for President Bola Tinubu because of the reforms his administration has initiated. Although inflation and the high cost of living remain major concerns, I believe these challenges are temporary and will ease in the near future. The reforms are already beginning to produce visible results, and I believe the country is gradually moving in the right direction. For these reasons, I will be voting for the All Progressives Congress (APC) to sustain the reforms and build on the progress being made.” Tope Okeowo, political analyst “My voting pattern depends on the candidate’s track record and performance. I will also consider the zone where he or she comes from. I hate marginalisation”. Ayo Fadaka, political analyst “So far, only the APC is seen to be making strenuous efforts at selling itself and agenda. The opposition parties are merely groping in the dark with their campaign messages seriously grounded in pettiness. None of them has proposed anything new and inspiring as an alternative to the APC. “Their immaturity, unseriousness and general inexperience they display points to the fact that the only person that still has an understanding of the enormous responsibilities the office of the President requires is Bola Ahmed Tinubu. That is the man to vote for, in the interest of our tomorrow. So I am going to vote for President Tinubu”. Chief Ola Amure, legal practitioner “What will influence my vote in the 2027 Presidential Election is not political sentiment, party loyalty or propaganda, but the need for competent leadership, economic recovery, security and improved living conditions for Nigerians. There is an urgent need for a change of government at the federal level because the present APC-led admini

item.title: 63 Years Later, CBS's Legendary 70-Episode Series Still Has the Only Vampire Worth Watching
item.description: It’s Fangsgiving here at Polygon, our Thanksgiving celebration of stories about fanged creatures of all types and especially vampires . I didn't want to be left out, but, to be honest, I always thought vampires were kind of dumb. They're a horror movie staple, but they’re rarely all that scary. There’s usually a romantic element to their stories that I also find tiresome . Perhaps I’ve just never seen the right vampire movies, but overall I find vampires to be pretty lame.
