item.title: Tinubu, the Igbo and the politics of bread soaked in water, by Emmanuel Aziken
item.description: Four years ago, when Bola Ahmed Tinubu visited Enugu as a presidential candidate, he confronted a crowd that appeared less than enthusiastic about his ambition with a warning that has since acquired an enduring political significance. If they refused to support him and he eventually became president, he suggested, they might have to make do with a slice of bread soaked in water. It may have been intended as political banter, but the message was not lost on the people of the South-East. The symbolism became even more pronounced after his victory when the president-elect constituted his inauguration committee without a single Igbo representative. For many in the region, it was an early indication of the place they might occupy in the new political order. Three and a half years into his presidency, Tinubu’s relationship with the South-East has remained a mixture of gestures of inclusion and lingering questions about the region’s place in his administration. To his credit, he departed from the approach of his predecessor, Muhammadu Buhari, by appointing Igbo into the commanding heights of the military. However, beyond that, questions remain about the administration’s commitment to equitable representation. The South-West presently has 10 ministers and ministers of state in the federal cabinet, compared with four from the South-East, following the exit of former Minister of State for Labour, Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, from Abia State. While constitutional requirements for ministerial representation are being met, the disparity raises legitimate questions about the spirit of federal character and the extent to which every region enjoys a sense of belonging in the federation. Curiously, some supporters of Tinubu in the South-East insist that the region has never had it so good in terms of appointments, access and federal patronage. Their position deserves consideration, but it does not erase the wider perception that the region remains inadequately represented in the distribution of political opportunities. There is also the question of electoral calculation. Before the 2023 election, Tinubu’s political strategy appeared to depend heavily on consolidating support in the South-West and making significant gains in the North. The political landscape has since changed. His administration is facing growing discontent in parts of the North, while the economic consequences of its policies have generated opposition across the country. Against this background, the President’s renewed courtship of the South-East appears to carry greater political significance. His meeting with Igbo residents in Lagos last Monday was particularly revealing. The atmosphere was warm and enthusiastic. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: Four years ago, when Bola Ahmed Tinubu visited Enugu as a presidential candidate, he confronted a crowd that appeared less than enthusiastic about his ambition with a warning that has since acquired an enduring political significance. If they refused to support him and he eventually became president, he suggested, they might have to make do with a slice of bread soaked in water. It may have been intended as political banter, but the message was not lost on the people of the South-East. The symbolism became even more pronounced after his victory when the president-elect constituted his inauguration committee without a single Igbo representative. For many in the region, it was an early indication of the place they might occupy in the new political order. Three and a half years into his presidency, Tinubu’s relationship with the South-East has remained a mixture of gestures of inclusion and lingering questions about the region’s place in his administration. To his credit, he departed from the approach of his predecessor, Muhammadu Buhari, by appointing Igbo into the commanding heights of the military. However, beyond that, questions remain about the administration’s commitment to equitable representation. The South-West presently has 10 ministers and ministers of state in the federal cabinet, compared with four from the South-East, following the exit of former Minister of State for Labour, Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, from Abia State. While constitutional requirements for ministerial representation are being met, the disparity raises legitimate questions about the spirit of federal character and the extent to which every region enjoys a sense of belonging in the federation. Curiously, some supporters of Tinubu in the South-East insist that the region has never had it so good in terms of appointments, access and federal patronage. Their position deserves consideration, but it does not erase the wider perception that the region remains inadequately represented in the distribution of political opportunities. There is also the question of electoral calculation. Before the 2023 election, Tinubu’s political strategy appeared to depend heavily on consolidating support in the South-West and making significant gains in the North. The political landscape has since changed. His administration is facing growing discontent in parts of the North, while the economic consequences of its policies have generated opposition across the country. Against this background, the President’s renewed courtship of the South-East appears to carry greater political significance. His meeting with Igbo residents in Lagos last Monday was particularly revealing. The atmosphere was warm and enthusiastic. Unlike the stern warning of four years ago, Tinubu was relaxed and playful, even reminding his audience of how they had disappointed him in 2023. He was referring to his defeat by Peter Obi in Lagos during the presidential election. Unfortunately, the President and some of his political associates appear not to have properly understood the reasons behind that electoral outcome. Rather than recognise the democratic choices of Lagos residents, some resorted to an ethnic interpretation that deepened divisions. One of the most unfortunate reactions came from Bayo Onanuga, then a spokesman for Tinubu’s presidential campaign and now a presidential spokesman. Shortly after the 2023 election, he issued a controversial warning to Igbo residents in Lagos, accusing them of interfering in the state’s politics. In his tweet, he declared: “Let 2023 be the last time of Igbo interference in Lagos politics. Let there be no repeat in 2027. Lagos is like Anambra, Imo, any Nigerian state. It is not No Man’s Land, not Federal Capital Territory. It is Yoruba land. Mind your business.” That statement was deeply troubling. It suggested that the political rights of Nigerian citizens could be restricted by their ethnic origins or ancestry. Lagos, like every other Nigerian state, belongs to all Nigerians who live, work and participate in its development. No ethnic group has an exclusive constitutional right to determine how other Nigerians should vote. Onanuga’s diagnosis was also defective. Tinubu’s defeat in Lagos was not the product of an Igbo conspiracy. He faced opposition from different political tendencies, including influential Yoruba figures. Afenifere, the prominent Yoruba socio-cultural organisation, endorsed Peter Obi in the 2023 presidential election. The Labour Party’s Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour also mounted a serious challenge to Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu. Reducing these political developments to ethnic interference was therefore an attempt to avoid the more important questions about voter preferences, political dissatisfaction and the right of citizens to make independent electoral choices. What makes the episode particularly disappointing is the inclusive political reputation Tinubu built before becoming President. He popularised the appointment of non-indigenes into prominent positions in Lagos and demonstrated an ability to accommodate people from different ethnic backgrounds. He also facilitated the emergence of Joe Igbokwe, an Igbo man, as a prominent voice in the ruling political structure in Lagos. His own family connections reflect Nigeria’s diversity, with his son, Seyi, married to a woman of Igbo ancestry. It is against this background that the President must be careful about remarks that suggest lingering resentment over how the South-East or Igbo voters exercised their democratic rights in 2023. When Tinubu reminds the Igbo that they disappointed him at the polls, he risks reducing the relationship between the presidency and an entire region to electoral gratitude and punishment. That is not the essence of democratic leadership. The South-East does not need bread soaked in water, whether as a joke or a political metaphor. It needs infrastructure, industrial investment, federal appointments that reflect its place in the federation and equal opportunities for its citizens. Above all, it needs a President who recognises that no Nigerian should be made to feel like a second-class citizen because of where they come from or whom they voted for. Tinubu has an opportunity to correct the unfortunate impressions created by some of the rhetoric surrounding his emergence. His recent engagement with Igbo residents in Lagos was a welcome departure from the divisive exchanges of 2023. But warm words and political banter must translate into concrete action. The President should not be preoccupied with how the Igbo voted in 2023. He should be concerned about how Nigerians across all regions will assess his performance in 2027. Nigeria wants the Tinubu who embraces every community, irrespective of colour, creed, culture or political preference. The presidency is not a reward for those who voted for the winner, nor a punishment for those who chose otherwise. It is a national trust. Tinubu must govern as President of all Nigerians, not merely those who supported his ambition. The post Tinubu, the Igbo and the politics of bread soaked in water, by Emmanuel Aziken appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: A tale of interlocking blocks, by Muyiwa Adetiba
item.description: The traffic in Victoria Island in the past month had to be experienced to be appreciated. I once spent two hours from Falomo Bridge, Ikoyi to the Mobil petrol station on Victoria Island, a journey that would have been walkable if the weather was kinder and security better. The case of an ‘egbon’ was even worse. He reportedly left Metropolitan Club for his home off Ligali Ayorinde. It is a journey that would take 10 to 15 minutes on a good day. It took him three hours on this fateful evening. It was so bad that this 85year-old man was tempted to walk but for the restraint of his driver and the caution of the friend he was chatting with on the phone. The ostensible reason for the gridlock was the work being done on an Ozumba Mbadiwe stretch which had refused to acknowledge the several palliatives done on it during the rainy season. Lagos State in its wisdom then decided to do something more permanent by using interlocking blocks. Hopefully, the traffic nightmare is over. At least for the time being. The use of interlocking blocks, otherwise called Interlocking Concrete Block Pavements (ICBP) for some roads, seems the way to go. Especially in waterlogged areas with heavy traffic. It is said to be a system where individual blocks which are held together without mortar or adhesives, serve to distribute heavy loads across multiple units. Its strength, like a broom, is in the collective. It is, also like a broom, a pitiable sight when loosened or dislodged. It is even hazardous as loose blocks can cause havoc to motorists. I am no expert, but in my opinion, the blocks are invariably dislodged when the foundation is not tight and firmly compressed before the laying of interlocking blocks with the result that certain areas begin to sink or cave in with time. It could also happen when the edges are not properly fused together with concrete. They are, in other words, as strong as their weakest link. And when this weak link is not quickly remedied, the road begins to disintegrate. This is when a stitch in time would have saved nine. This is when unfortunately, from all I have seen, authorities look the other way. I virtually witnessed the creation and almost the disintegration of a road in Oniru, Victoria Island. Sometimes called the Alternative Road, Akinogun Road was first constructed as a two lane road during the Fashola era to take traffic off Ozumba Mbadiwe by bye-passing the Lekki toll gate. To underscore its importance, the Sanwo-Olu era turned it to four lanes with interlocking blocks. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: The traffic in Victoria Island in the past month had to be experienced to be appreciated. I once spent two hours from Falomo Bridge, Ikoyi to the Mobil petrol station on Victoria Island, a journey that would have been walkable if the weather was kinder and security better. The case of an ‘egbon’ was even worse. He reportedly left Metropolitan Club for his home off Ligali Ayorinde. It is a journey that would take 10 to 15 minutes on a good day. It took him three hours on this fateful evening. It was so bad that this 85year-old man was tempted to walk but for the restraint of his driver and the caution of the friend he was chatting with on the phone. The ostensible reason for the gridlock was the work being done on an Ozumba Mbadiwe stretch which had refused to acknowledge the several palliatives done on it during the rainy season. Lagos State in its wisdom then decided to do something more permanent by using interlocking blocks. Hopefully, the traffic nightmare is over. At least for the time being. The use of interlocking blocks, otherwise called Interlocking Concrete Block Pavements (ICBP) for some roads, seems the way to go. Especially in waterlogged areas with heavy traffic. It is said to be a system where individual blocks which are held together without mortar or adhesives, serve to distribute heavy loads across multiple units. Its strength, like a broom, is in the collective. It is, also like a broom, a pitiable sight when loosened or dislodged. It is even hazardous as loose blocks can cause havoc to motorists. I am no expert, but in my opinion, the blocks are invariably dislodged when the foundation is not tight and firmly compressed before the laying of interlocking blocks with the result that certain areas begin to sink or cave in with time. It could also happen when the edges are not properly fused together with concrete. They are, in other words, as strong as their weakest link. And when this weak link is not quickly remedied, the road begins to disintegrate. This is when a stitch in time would have saved nine. This is when unfortunately, from all I have seen, authorities look the other way. I virtually witnessed the creation and almost the disintegration of a road in Oniru, Victoria Island. Sometimes called the Alternative Road, Akinogun Road was first constructed as a two lane road during the Fashola era to take traffic off Ozumba Mbadiwe by bye-passing the Lekki toll gate. To underscore its importance, the Sanwo-Olu era turned it to four lanes with interlocking blocks. If it was important before, it is now even more so because it is the road that now links commuters in that axis to the Coastal Road. Traffic has understandably, become heavier on the road. And probably because of this, especially during peak periods, another U-turn was very recently created that was probably not in the original design. This U-turn makes access to the Coastal Road easier and faster. It is unfortunately from the creation of this U-turn that the disintegration of the road started. Something that held the interlocking blocks together must have chipped off when the U-turn was created. As usual, it started with just one or two loose blocks. At this stage, a cup of mixed cement would have done the job. It would have been a stitch in time. But nothing was done. It became wider over the weeks as block after block were loosened. Soon, it became difficult for heavy duty trucks to do a U-turn without their tyres screeching. Then, it became obvious that smaller cars were trying to avoid the damaged area. But the damaged area was getting wider and soon became more and more difficult to avoid. Then, it threatened to cut one side of the road in two. A couple of days ago, I passed the road to find that a part of the U-turn had been sealed off for repairs. Thank God! Hopefully, the discomfort of regular commuters would be over soon. The wonder though, as always, is why things have to deteriorate before being fixed. Why we have to wait for a torn garment to need more than a dozen stitches to fix when a stitch in time would have saved the day and the embarrassment. Or why a simple repair work has to deteriorate in order to justify the award of a new contract. The Alternative Road is a busy road. Not only in terms of traffic, but also in terms of personnel. Government officials of different hues visit the road for one reason or the other. Even a bird would be challenged and accosted quickly if it perched wrongly along the road. It is therefore, hard to believe that the arm of government responsible for minor road repairs was not, until now, aware of this damage. It is hard to believe that the vigilance of government officials is only limited to perceived misdemeanors by the public and blind to things that need to be put right for the comfort of citizens and ease of governance. Government officials are quick to attack illegal structures and slow to repair damaged structures. The tale of the gradual dislodgement of interlocking blocks on this road, is in a way for me, a metaphor for the state of our national life. We tend to turn a blind eye to things until they get irredeemably wrong. The colossal sums we have spent on insecurity for example, could have been better spent elsewhere if things had been nipped in the bud. Instead, some northern politicians saw ‘Boko Haram’, its progenitor, as a card to be used against a Southern Christian President. The four national refineries would still be functioning today if leaders, starting from the military, saw them as national priorities instead of cash cows to be milked from time to time. Now, they are almost like scraps because the necessary stitching was not done as at when due. The proliferation of fake products is another issue. Fake products would not be this pervasive if concerned officials had acted swiftly to nip things in the bud. The list is endless. And together, they have made our national pathway to prosperity almost impassable. The second lesson, especially in this electioneering season, is that interlocking blocks are strong when held together just as unity gives a nation strength. Yet, we have politicians who are currently playing up ethnic and religious divisions for catchment votes. They play up weaknesses and fault lines. These leaders will rather see things damaged than repaired. They will rather see them destroyed than nurtured. They will rather weaken than strengthen. In fact, they delight in pointing out the loosened blocks in our national life. Their incessant attacks on the nation’s psyche are worse than the benign neglect of that road in Oniru, Victoria Island. The post A tale of interlocking blocks, by Muyiwa Adetiba appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Tinubu failed to fulfil his promises, he must go – Obi
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has said President Bola Tinubu must be voted out in the 2027 presidential election for Nigeria to experience the change and development it desires. Obi, who spoke on Friday at the Primetime Event Centre, along the Port Harcourt-Aba Expressway, Aba, Abia State, accused the Tinubu administration of failing to fulfil its campaign promises and worsening poverty in the country. He assured residents that the government he and his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, were seeking to form would unite the country and transform its economic and social sectors. The former Anambra State governor said the presidency required energy and commitment, arguing that it should not be treated as a retirement home. “Tinubu has failed to fulfil all his promises, including the restoration of the power sector. We will generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000MW. Any money we borrow must be for investment. “The presidency requires energy; it is not a retirement home. We are tired of Tinubu’s government. Tinubu must go for a better Nigeria to emerge,” he said. Obi said his proposed administration would prioritise national unity, recalling that Nigeria had previously enjoyed stronger bonds across its different regions. “Let me assure you that the government Kwankwaso and I are seeking to form will unite Nigeria. Yesterday, I was in Minna, and I told them that Nigeria used to be united. No wonder Nnamdi Azikiwe and Chukwuemeka Ojukwu were born in Zungeru. We are going to reunite Nigeria. “The Nigeria we want is one where a child of nobody can become somebody,” he said. He also criticised the Federal Government’s borrowing, alleging that the Tinubu administration had borrowed more than previous administrations combined without commensurate visible results. According to him, his proposed government would focus on production, job creation and economic prosperity rather than continued dependence on consumption. “Kwankwaso and I want to form a government that will not give you excuses. We are going to form a government that will bring prosperity and production back to Nigeria. We will remove this country from consumption to production. “We already know the excuses, and we will tackle the challenges. Our government will demonstrate compassion, commitment and the zeal to get the job done,” he said. On corruption, Obi pledged that his administration would ensure public funds were deployed for the benefit of Nigerians. He questioned the utilisation of government loans, contrasting current borrowing with previous investments in major infrastructure projects such as the Kainji Dam. Obi further claimed that the number of Nigerians living in poverty had increased from 87 million when Tinubu assumed office to more than 140 million. On corruption, Obi pledged that his administration would ensure public funds were deployed for the benefit of Nigerians. He questioned the utilisation of government loans, contrasting current borrowing with previous investments in major infrastructure projects such as the Kainji Dam. Obi further claimed that the number of Nigerians living in poverty had increased from 87 million when Tinubu assumed office to more than 140 million. He also expressed concern over youth unemployment, promising increased investment in education and healthcare if elected. Turning to the economy of Abia State, the NDC candidate promised to transform Aba, the state’s commercial centre, into an export hub and link it with Port Harcourt to establish a new economic corridor within the first few years of his administration. He also pledged to address the country’s security challenges, particularly the abduction of schoolchildren. “We cannot be in government while schoolchildren are being kidnapped and others taken into the bush. We will be in that bush with them,” Obi said. The post 2027: Tinubu failed to fulfil his promises, he must go – Obi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: This purple electric Chinese minivan can go up to 559 miles on a charge
item.description: Electric minivans could be the ultimate in utility, with room for passengers, gear, and huge batteries. While VW's ID Buzz only gave us 200 miles of real-world driving on a charge in 2023 , China's BYD has just announced a flagship purple peoplemover that can go an estimated 559 miles (900 km) on electricity. It's called the BYD Whale, and some back-of-the-napkin math suggests it lives up to the name. The van would be bigger than a Honda Odyssey, bigger than a Chrysler Pacifica, and bigger than a Toyota Sienna, at 17.3 feet (5,270mm) long, 6.5 feet (1,996mm) wide, 6 feet (1,815mm) tall, and with a 123-inch (3,130mm) wheelbase. item.title: The best Black Friday deals you can still get on AirPods, Macs, and other Apple gear
item.description: The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR has hit a new low price just a few months after release. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge Black Friday is entering the evening, which means one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch is coming to a close. After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear. Some discounts still apply to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro , too, which are available at their lowest prices to date. In addition to a variety of discounts across retailers, Apple is offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases between November 27th and November 30th. How much you get back is determined by how much you spend, with up to $100 available for some iPhone and Apple Watch purchases, and up to $300 for the 16-inch MacBook Pro. That said, in some cases you may be able to save more by buying from other retailers. Earbud and headphone deals AirPods Pro 3 The latest AirPods Pro offer improved noise cancellation and richer bass, along with built-in heart sensors that work with Apple’s Fitness app to monitor calories burned across more than 50 workouts. Read our review. Where to Buy: $249 $149 at Amazon $249 $149 at Walmart $249 $149.99 at Best Buy Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 Beats’ fitness-focused earbuds feature ear hooks designed to stay put during even the most intense workouts as well as built-in heart rate monitoring. They also deliver relatively bass-rich sound for their design, along with solid noise cancellation, wireless charging, and AirPods features like adaptive audio thanks to Apple’s H2 chip. Read our review. Where to Buy: $249 $179.95 at Amazon $249 $179.95 at Walmart $249.99 $179.99 at Best Buy You can buy the AirPods 4 on sale at Walmart for around $89 ($40 off), which is $20 shy of their best price. Apple’s last-gen earbuds lack active noise cancellation, but they still deliver good, relatively bass-rich sound, even if they don’t quite match the newer AirPods 5. They also offer voice call quality on par with the latest AirPods Pro. Read our review . The second-gen AirPods Max are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon and Best Buy , which is $19 shy of their best price to date ( Target also has them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review . Beats Studio Pro The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review . Where to Buy: $349.99 $139.95 at Amazon (select colors) $349.99

Beats Studio Pro The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. Where to Buy: $349.99 $139.95 at Amazon (select colors) $349.99 $99 at Walmart (select colors) $349.99 $139.95 at Best Buy (select colors) Beats 360 headphones The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. Read our review. Where to Buy: $349.99 $249 at Amazon $349.99 $249.99 at Best Buy If you want over-ears and are comfortable going without active noise cancellation, the Beats Solo 4 are on sale starting at $79.99 ($120 off) at Amazon and Target — a new low price. The wireless earbuds feature a slick, eye-catching transparent option and solid noise cancellation, especially at this price. MacBook deals MacBook Neo Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review . Where to Buy: $799 $699.99 at Amazon (512GB, Touch ID) $699 $649 at Best Buy (256GB) $699 $599 at Amazon (256GB) Apple MacBook Air 13 (M5) Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review . Where to Buy: $1299 $999 at Amazon (512GB) $1299 $999 at Best Buy (512GB) $1599 $1199 at Amazon (1TB) The recently released 16.3-inch MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, 24GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage is on sale starting at $3,099 ($300 off) — a new low price — at Amazon . The redesigned laptop is Apple’s first with an OLED touchscreen, which allows for rich colors and deep blacks. It’s also noticeably thinner and lighter than the non-touchscreen 16-inch MacBook Pro, and features a new Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and provides quick access to controls and notifications. Read our review . The 14-inch M6-powered MacBook Pro is on sale starting at $1,749 ($250 off) at Amazon and Best Buy , which is a new low price. The Pro builds on its predecessor with a faster chip and support for Wi-Fi 7. In our testing, it handled multitasking, photo editing, and occasional video editing with ease while still delivering exceptional battery life. It lacks the newer MacBook Pro’s gorgeous OLED display, but its Mini LED screen still looks great, especially given its smooth 120Hz refresh rate. It also offers excellent speakers and a good selection of ports, including three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, and an SD card slot. Read our review . Apple Watch deals Apple Watch Series 12 The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review . Where to Buy: $399 $299 at Amazon (GPS, 42mm) $399 $329 at Best Buy (GPS, 42mm) $449 $349 at Amazon (GPS, 46mm) The Apple Watch SE 3 is on sale in the 40mm / GPS configuration starting at $179 ($50 off) at Amazon and Walmart , matching its best price to date, while Best Buy is currently $20 higher. Apple’s newest entry-level smartwatch remains our top recommendation for anyone who wants a basic fitness tracker, as it offers all the essentials alongside an always-on display and Apple’s S10 chip, which enables on-device Siri requests. Read our review . AirTags, chargers, and other deals Apple AirTag (second-gen) Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review. Where to Buy: $29 $18 at Amazon $29 $18 at Walmart $29 $18 at Best Buy Baseus AM52 power bank (with built-in cable) The Baseus PicoGo AM52 is a 10,000mAh magnetic power bank that supports fast 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging and up to 45W wired charging via its built-in USB-C cable. It was one of the fastest wireless chargers we tested, bringing an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 65 percent in an hour. Read our guide to the best Qi2 batterie

item.title: Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State, Mr Melvin Ejeh, has vowed to ensure the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killing of an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Inspector Anyebe Anya. Anya was reportedly killed by armed men who attacked him at his duty post at a checkpoint in Agatu a few days ago. The assailants were also said to have carted away his service rifle after the attack. Ejeh gave the assurance when he visited the deceased officer’s family in Otukpo to commiserate with them, describing Anya as a hardworking, honest and dedicated officer. He vowed that those behind the killing would not escape justice, assuring the bereaved family that efforts were already underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Those that killed him will not go unpunished. We will get all of them. I knew him personally. He was a very hardworking, honest man who was committed to his work. “The whole community is mourning his death. The people of Agatu are shocked and grieving over his death. “We console his family. He was a committed officer. I can assure you that we will get those involved and they will be brought to justice. There is a hunt for them already. “The entire Agatu people will not rest until he gets justice, that I can assure his family,” the chairman said. Efforts to reach the Public Relations Officer of the Benue State NSCDC Command, SC Michael Ejelikwu, for comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: The best robot vacuums we’ve tested are up to 60 percent off for Black Friday
item.description: The Eufy Omni C28 has dropped to a new low of $379.99 for Black Friday. | Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge Black Friday is here, and if you want a little help keeping your floors clean this holiday season, now is a great time to pick up a robot vacuum. Some of the best models we’ve tested over the last year or two are on sale for up to 60 percent off, whether you’re after a basic robovac for quick cleanups or a more advanced model that vacuums, mops, and practically takes care of itself. This year’s sale has made some pricier robot vacuums a lot more affordable. The Eufy Omni C28 , for example, now costs about what you’d expect to pay for a budget bot, while the Matic — which impressed us with its almost humanlike navigation — is getting a rare discount in the form of a bundle. If none of those are quite what you’re looking for, we’ve also found good deals on models from Roborock , Dreame, and more, with picks below for a variety of budgets and cleaning needs. Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design. Read our review . Where to Buy: $999.99 $549.99 at Amazon $999.99 $549.99 at Roborock Roborock Q10 S5 Plus Despite lacking a multifunction dock, the budget-friendly robot vacuum and mop offers an impressive set of features for the price, including AI-powered obstacle avoidance, sonic mopping, automatic mop lifting, and a self-emptying dock. Where to Buy: $549.99 $229.99 at Amazon $549.99 $229.99 at Roborock Matic robot vacuum The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost humanlike navigation, tackling high-pile rugs and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review. Where to Buy: $1795 $1395 at Matic (Standard Bundle) $1995 $1595 at Matic (Serene Bundle) Eufy Omni C28 The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors. Where to Buy: $799.99 $379.99 at Amazon $799.99 $379.99 at Eufy (with code WS24C28200NEW1) Dreame X60 Ultra The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets. item.title: Sony’s 1000XM4C headphones are a Black Friday bargain at $198
item.description: The fan-favorite folding design returns with the comfortable, slightly improved XM4C headphones. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge Instead of purely looking forward with its headphone designs, Sony went back to its popular WH-1000XM4 design and made some improvements to make it even better. The 2026 version, called the WH-1000XM4C, sounds nearly as good as the pricier XM6 model (currently $348), but is down to $198 during Black Friday at Amazon , Best Buy , and Walmart . That’s $100 off their October launch price. Sony WH-1000XM4C Where to Buy: $299.99 $198 at Amazon $299.99 $198 at Walmart $299.99 $199.99 at Best Buy There’s a reason why Sony went back to refine the XM4. Our former reviewer Chris Welch praised them for being super comfortable and for having close to perfect features for the price, especially compared to its successor, the XM3 (still my daily driver, for what it’s worth). The XM4s had better sound quality and noise cancellation, plus improved mics, multipoint connectivity, and a sensor that can detect when you remove them to automatically pause audio. Now, with the XM4C, there are further improvements, most notably a 10-band equalizer in the app (compared to the original XM4’s five-band) that my colleague John Higgins says really helped the headphones’ midrange frequencies open up. These are a great buy, but they aren’t your only Sony headphones deal to consider right now. Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are available during Black Friday at Best Buy for $169, their lowest price yet from a major retailer. There are upsides and downsides to this model: They feature improved noise cancellation thanks to more mics, despite using the same ANC chip as the XM4C, but they can’t fold up as compactly, making them a little bigger to pack in your bag. Either one you choose, you’ll have some great headphones to listen to going into 2027. Read our Sony WH-1000XM4C review .

item.title: Yooka-Laylee’s free upgrade is skipping Xbox
item.description: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition | Image: Playtronic Games Playtronic Games is getting ready to launch Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition as a free update on PlayStation 5, Switch 2, and PC on December 15th. Unfortunately for Xbox owners, the developer says it "can't commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future." In a statement posted on X , Playtronic said that it understands the frustration some players may feel, but that bringing the Definitive Edition to Xbox just isn't viable "given the technological challenges and costs," and reminded people that they're a small team. item.title: Many of our favorite Blu-ray movies are over 50 percent off for Black Friday
item.description: Blade Runner 2049 looks fantastic, even if you pick up the 1080p Blu-ray version. | Image: Alcon Entertainment No shade to those who love their subscription services, but viewing physical movies is a time-honored tradition that shouldn’t go away. Watching them doesn’t feel all that different, but deciding which movie to watch feels less annoying; sifting through a movie collection on your shelf or in a storage binder is so much more fun (and less overwhelming) than scrolling endlessly in apps. While standard Blu-ray players that display movies at up to 1080p are fairly inexpensive, 4K Blu-ray counterparts that can show movies in all their 4K HDR glory are significantly pricier (but totally worth it if you’re a movie buff). No matter the player you own, there are always Blu-ray deals, and the discounts are especially good during Black Friday. We’ve highlighted some of our favorites below, though Amazon, Barnes & Noble, and Gruv are each overflowing with more deals than we could realistically wedge into our coverage. KPop Demon Hunters The once-Netflix-exclusive animated film is now available on 4K Blu-ray at a great price. This movie’s part of Gruv’s “3 for $33” sale. The set includes the theatrical cuts of the trilogy, plus the extended editions. Where to Buy: $67.8 $49.49 at Amazon (4K Blu-ray) The Matrix: 4-Film Déjà Vu Collection Setting aside that not every Matrix movie is amazing, the Déjà Vu set includes them all for less than if you bought them separately. item.title: Meet Emmanuel Emegha, Chelsea’s new striking sensation who has Nigerian roots
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Chelsea’s latest attacking prospect, Emmanuel Emegha, is already giving supporters reasons to pay attention after scoring against Nottingham Forest on Friday. While the Blues trailed by two goals to nil, the 23-year-old striker, who joined Chelsea from French side Strasbourg, came off the bench to replace Danny Welbeck, found the net in the 54th and 89th minutes, and offered the Blues a lifeline in their Premier League encounter. However, his goals were not enough as Forest held unto their lead after Morgan Gibss-White had extended it immediately after, bringing the game to a 3-2 full-time result. Before the Forest clash, Emegha put Chelsea ahead at home when they hosted Leeds United last week. Unfortunately, he could not save the team from capitulating to a 1-4 defeat in the game. But beyond his growing reputation in England, Emegha has an interesting connection to Nigeria. Born in The Hague, Netherlands, to a Togolese father and a Nigerian mother, the powerful forward has West African roots. His Nigerian heritage makes him a player of interest to Nigerian football fans, particularly those following the growing number of players of Nigerian descent making waves in European football. However, Emegha has chosen to represent the Netherlands internationally. He made his senior debut against Poland in November 2025, explaining that the Netherlands is his country and that he is proud to be Dutch. Although Nigeria missed out on having him represent the Super Eagles, his progress at Chelsea gives Nigerian fans another reason to follow his career closely. At 23, Emegha has the physical presence, pace and goalscoring instincts to make an impression in English football. His latest goals against Nottingham Forest are another early signs of what he could offer Chelsea. The post Meet Emmanuel Emegha, Chelsea’s new striking sensation who has Nigerian roots appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Arteta sets Arsenal 100-point Premier League target to emulate Manchester City
item.description: ‘It’s only been done once and that’s what we want’ Arteta not being drawn on City’s financial charges Mikel Arteta has set Arsenal the ­target of emulating Manchester City by becoming only the second team in Premier League history to record 100 points in a season. Arteta was an assistant for Pep Guardiola’s side when they achieved the landmark in the 2017-18 campaign, beating second-placed Manchester United by 19 points. City head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday already trailing Arsenal by six points after just 11 games, with Enzo Maresca’s side having failed to win any of their four previous league matches. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘My Tottenham was born’: De Zerbi harks back to opening defeat for Sunderland return
item.description: Spurs head coach intends to draw on last season’s trauma Italian praises club after Williams-Barnett signs contract Tottenham’s trip to Sunderland takes Roberto De Zerbi back to the start. The Italian’s first game as the club’s manager came at the Stadium of Light in April and relegation was on the cards when his new side slipped to a 1-0 defeat . The result left Spurs in the bottom three, two points below West Ham, and De Zerbi has not forgotten the reaction in the dressing room after the final whistle. Survival was secured on the final day of last season but he is taking nothing for granted after a promising run of form. Continue reading...

item.title: The new iPad Mini is getting its first major discount for Black Friday
item.description: I’m not saying you should read on an iPad next to fountain. I’m just saying you can. | Photo: David Pierce / The Verge We were big fans of Apple’s new iPad Mini when we reviewed it in early November, but its steep starting price of $699 was hard to swallow. Thankfully, the small tablet is already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. Right now, Amazon and Walmart are both selling the 2026 iPad Mini with Wi-Fi and 128GB of storage starting at $599 ($100 off), its lowest price to date. iPad Mini (2026) Where to Buy: $699 $599 at Amazon (Wi-Fi, 128GB) $699 $599 at Walmart (Wi-Fi, 128GB) $799 $749 at Amazon (Wi-Fi, 256GB) The new Mini is a notable upgrade over its predecessor, with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display that delivers deeper blacks and better contrast than the previous model’s 8.3-inch LCD. Despite the bigger screen, the tablet itself is smaller and lighter, making it easier to carry. Apple also added IP67 dust and water resistance, so you have less reason to worry about where you use it. As my colleague David Pierce noted in his review, that made a big difference in his day-to-day use; he felt more comfortable handing the Mini to his spill-prone toddler or keeping it nearby in the kitchen to follow recipes. He even took it into the shower to keep watching a football game. The upgraded A20 Pro chip also made apps load faster and demanding games run better in Pierce’s testing, while battery life held steady at around nine hours of screentime. At $599, though, the new Mini is still relatively expensive if you mainly want a tablet for browsing the web or streaming shows. The last-gen iPad Mini, which runs on Apple’s A17 Pro chip, is available for under $500 if you’d rather save another $100 and can live without the OLED screen and water resistance. But if you’ve been waiting for a more worthwhile upgrade to Apple’s smallest tablet, the current Black Friday discount makes the new model easier to justify. iPad Mini (2024) Where to Buy: $599 $484 at Amazon (128GB, Wi-Fi) $699 $584 at Amazon (256GB, Wi-Fi) $899 $784 at Amazon (512GB, Wi-Fi) Read our full iPad Mini review .

item.title: Chelsea beaten at Nottingham Forest as poor run continues
item.description: Nottingham Forest claimed a memorable 3-2 victory over Chelsea at the City Ground on Friday night, November 27, piling further pressure on Blues manager Xabi Alonso after another disappointing performance from his side. Forest made a flying start to the encounter, taking the lead just five minutes into the game through Igor Jesus, who produced a superb volley from Daniel Muñoz’s cross to put the hosts ahead. Chelsea struggled to find their rhythm in the opening half, with Forest looking more dangerous and organised in attack. Despite enjoying more possession, the visitors failed to turn their dominance on the ball into meaningful goalscoring opportunities. The hosts doubled their advantage shortly after the restart when Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the penalty spot in the 51st minute. The penalty was awarded after Wesley Fofana brought down Liam Delap inside the Chelsea box. However, Chelsea responded three minutes later through substitute Emmanuel Emegha, who pulled one back after Pedro Neto’s effort took a deflection and fell kindly into his path. The goal briefly offered Chelsea hope of mounting a comeback, but Forest remained dangerous and restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute when Gibbs-White grabbed his second of the evening. Chelsea refused to surrender, with Emegha scoring again in the 89th minute to reduce the deficit to 3-2 and set up a tense finish. However, Forest held on through the closing moments to secure all three points and condemn Chelsea to another painful defeat. The result represents another setback for Alonso, whose team have struggled for consistency in recent weeks. Chelsea’s defensive weaknesses and inability to control crucial moments once again proved costly. For Nottingham Forest, the victory provides a significant boost and a valuable reward for their determination and attacking efficiency. Chelsea must now turn their attention to their next Premier League fixture against Crystal Palace as they look to recover from another frustrating night. The post Chelsea beaten at Nottingham Forest as poor run continues appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Spygate tensions erupt at Southampton after Finn Azaz’s cry-baby celebration riles Boro
item.description: When asked whether he had any regrets about running the length of the pitch to goad the Middlesbrough supporters he used to call his own with a mock crying celebration, Finn Azaz was unequivocal. “None whatsoever,” said the Southampton playmaker. And you get the sense that very few associated with his club disagreed. Southampton, and their manager Tonda Eckert, long ago admitted their Spygate crime. Based on the behaviour of many connected to the south-coast club – their manager a notable exception – they have embraced it. The sense of aggrievement that it cost them the chance of promotion last season remains. Continue reading...

item.title: Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus fire Nottingham Forest past shaky Chelsea
item.description: Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. But, at the end of a week in which he invited opprobrium by making light of missing a penalty at Liverpool in an unsanctioned French interview, he endured the ultimate ignominy when Chelsea supporters followed a four-letter suggestion to tell the defender: “You’re not welcome here.” Fofana was humiliated by Liam Delap before fouling the former Chelsea striker for a penalty that Morgan Gibbs-White converted for the first of his two goals. The result, coming after Forest’s win against Manchester City in their last match at the City Ground, means they climb three points clear of the Premier League’s relegation zone. Continue reading...

item.title: Nigeria’s $1bn Monthly Remittance Has Been Achieved – CBN Governor Cardoso
item.description: Nigeria has achieved its $1 billion monthly diaspora remittance target, the Central Bank of Nigeria has said. CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso, who disclosed this at the 61st Annual Bankers’ Dinner of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) in Lagos on Friday, said Nigeria now targets $1.5 billion in monthly remittances by the end of the first half of 2027. “The fact that you can go abroad, put in your card, and make payment, yes, that is great convenience for everybody, great convenience. But beyond all that, one thing we should never forget — three years ago, two years ago, you couldn’t do all these things. “And what used to happen, you go somewhere, you want to make payments, you either have to pay in cash or use a card, which gets thrown away, and you’re disrespected,” he said. “What this has done, it has brought back the respect of all Nigerians abroad. “When I stood before you last year. I spoke of our ambition to increase monthly remittances to $1 billion a month. I am pleased to report that this milestone has been achieved. “We are now working towards increasing monthly remittances to $1.5 billion by the end of the first half of 2027,” Cardoso added. He commended licensed International Money Transfer Operators (IMTOs) for their efforts to strengthen transparency, invest in technology, and expand formal remittance channels, particularly across Asia. ﻿ Cardoso said that the next phase of Nigeria’s financial reforms must focus on deepening liquidity, broadening participation, and expanding the range of financial instruments available to businesses and investors. “The naira has strengthened by approximately six per cent over the past year, while daily foreign exchange market turnover has at times exceeded $1 billion. “In the fixed income market, daily turnover averages N1.5 trillion, supported by a credible tradable benchmark yield curve extending to 10 years. “What, what does all this mean? It is an encouraging sign of growing market confidence. The market deepens; more activity takes place when there’s confidence in the market,” he said. According to him, the priority is to ensure that markets continue to support efficient price discovery and capital allocation. “As recent movements in the foreign exchange market remind us, a well-functioning market does not mean that prices remain static. It does not mean that prices remain static. “They go up, they come down. Volatility is an inherent feature of global financial markets, and a market-determined exchange rate must be allowed to move in both directions in response to macroeconomic fundamentals and global development. “Emerging market currencies, including ours, have experienced volatility amidst changes in the United States’ interest rate environment and global risk sentiment. “Nigeria, as I have said, is part of this interconnected global financial system, but believe me, we are considerably better equipped to manage external shocks than we were three years ago.” According to him,

item.title: From Asake to Darkoo: 5 New Nigerian & African Music Videos to Watch This Weekend
item.description: Zlatan, Peruzzi, and Shoday from the official visuals for their collaborative single “Inferno.” Between Friday traffic in Lagos, Sunday afternoon wind-downs, and the official countdown to Detty December already kicking into gear across Nigeria, the final weekend of November arrives with a stacked line-up of fresh visuals worth queuing up on your screen. From street-hop swagger and a ninth-anniversary gospel love note by one of Nollywood and Afrobeats’ favourite couples to a pan-African dancefloor link-up between Benin and Tanzania, these five music videos deliver plenty to replay all weekend long. Skilful – Asake Lifted from his chart-topping 2026 album M$NEY, Asake brings his unmistakable log-drum bounce and choir-backed street-hop cadence to the official visual for “Skilful”. item.title: A Weekend For Proof
item.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Okere
item.content:encoded: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations. The summit should therefore be assessed through what participants authorise, who carries out the decisions and when implementation begins. Any agreement must reach state organisations, constituency candidates and polling agents to become electorally useful. Obi’s Campaign Faces An Organisational Dispute A fresh disagreement within the support-group environment complicates the NDC’s preparations. A group led by John Ughulu announced on Friday that it was withdrawing campaign and mobilisation support under the OK Movement name. The NDC rejected its claim to represent the authentic movement, while Obi’s spokesman said his campaign did not recognise Ughulu’s group as one of its support organisations. This establishes a dispute over authority and affiliation. It does not establish how many voters, organisers or functioning structures have changed allegiance. Its practical significance depends on identifiable capacity: people organising locally, maintaining campaign operations and preparing for election day. For Obi and Kwankwaso, the broader challenge is to coordinate their recognised organisations and give volunteers clear responsibilities. For anyone claiming to withdraw support, the test is whether the claimed structures can be independently demonstrated. Political labels alone cannot measure electoral strength. Delta’s Aftermath, Edo’s Warning The violence has continued to demand attention beyond Tuesday’s edition. Reporting records visits by Obi and Kwankwaso to a hospitalised survivor of the Delta attack. Separately, the House of Representatives called for investigations and action against perpetrators and sponsors. Its discussion of possible emergency measures was conditional; it did not declare a state of emergency. In Edo, the police account confirms an attack and a gunshot injury. The NDC alleges a broader pattern of political intimidation. The APC rejects allegations that it is coordinating attacks, and the Edo governor has denied government involvement. Those accusations and denials require examination against evidence. The immediate standard is equal protection. Campaign organisers need reliable security arrangements. Victims need care and access to justice. Investigators need to identify individual responsibility and any sponsorship. Repeated condemnation without visible investigative progress risks teaching citizens that intimidation carries little consequence. That perception can discourage participation even where no attack occurs. The Government’s Performance Remains On Trial Campaign disputes must leave room for scrutiny of governing choices. Atiku has questioned a reported decline in oil receipts, while Makinde’s campaign has challenged the relationship between expenditure plans and borrowing. The figures being debated concern an earlier reporting period; their renewed prominence does not make them newly incurred losses. For Tinubu’s administration, the response should explain revenue performance, spending priorities and what citizens receive from public expenditure. For challengers, criticism should lead to a credible alternative. Promises on security, jobs, electricity and education require resources. Voters deserve to understand the proposed trade-offs. The governing party seeks another mandate on its record and plans. The opposition seeks one on its diagnosis and proposed remedies. Both should face questions of cost, delivery and accountability. APC/Tinubu: The immediate test is whether the governing camp can combine its campaign strength with confidence in public institutions and equal protection for political competitors. ADC/Atiku: The leadership and nomination appeal remains consequential. The ADC has sought a stay of execution; the latest material reviewed does not establish that a stay has been granted. Its postponed Jigawa rally was attributed by a party spokesperson to mobilisation and logistical preparations, rather than a verified government prohibition. NDC/Obi–Kwankwaso: Campaign safety and coordination among support organisations require attention. The disputed OK Movement announcement cannot yet be translated into a quantified electoral loss. APM/Makinde and other opposition partners: Monday will test their willingness to accept defined responsibilities within a common arrangement. State contests: The Court of Appeal has reserved judgment in the dispute over Isa Pantami’s PDP governorship nomination in Gombe. A reserved judgment is a pending decision, rather than a victory for either side. Recent local and off-cycle elections remain useful indicators when turnout, competitiveness and local conditions are considered. They provide evidence about organisation and participation, without automatically predicting a presidential result. Election Watch assessment : The coming weekend offers measurable tests of readiness and cooperation. No fresh, credible polling reviewed for this edition establishes a national swing. Give Participation A Practical

item.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo
item.description: First, Uganda is heading for the exit in eastern DR Congo. Kampala has announced the withdrawal of its troops from a key town in North Kivu, as relations with Kinshasa deteriorate following provocative comments from Uganda's army chief. Then, pregnant women are struggling to cope with extreme heat, while health experts warn of growing risks for unborn babies, from dehydration to premature births. And, after seeking safety, opportunity and a better life, many migrants in South Africa now face hostility, violence and growing exclusion. As anti-immigration sentiment gains ground, the country's promise is fading for those who once saw it as a land of hope.

item.title: Ogun 2027: Court dismisses Hunye’s suits against Adeola’s APC candidacy
item.description: …Adeola hails judgment …as Hunye heads to Court of Appeal By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Federal High Court sitting in Abeokuta, Ogun State, on Friday dismissed two suits filed by Hon. Abayomi Semako Hunye challenging the emergence of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Delivering judgment in the two consolidated suits, Justice Okeke held that the cases lacked merit and consequently dismissed them. The suits, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1127/2026 and FHC/AB/126/2026, were instituted by Hunye against the APC, Senator Adeola and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), challenging the process through which Adeola emerged as the party’s governorship candidate. Reacting to the judgment, Adeola commended the judiciary, describing the decision as a vindication of the rule of law and the judicial process. In a statement issued by his media adviser, Chief Kayode Odunaro, the senator expressed satisfaction with the outcome while appreciating his legal team for what he described as their painstaking efforts in defending the suits. Adeola said, “I want to commend the Honourable Justice for his erudite judgment in these cases challenging my overwhelming and widely accepted victory in our party primary. I also commend my legal team for the painstaking defense put up during the process. “This victory is yet another milestone in our quest for equity and justice in the Ogun State 2027 election. To God be the glory once again.” The senator said that despite the legal challenges, he had remained focused on consolidating support for his candidacy across the state through engagements with political stakeholders and other interest groups. He added that his engagements had also included the presentation of his nine-pillar ITESIWAJU Agenda, which he described as his development blueprint for Ogun State. According to him, the court’s decision would allow him to concentrate more fully on preparations for the 2027 governorship election and take his campaign message to voters across the state. Adeola also urged APC members and his supporters, irrespective of their political affiliations, to remain united and focused, stressing that his ambition was driven by a desire to serve the people and contribute to the development of Ogun State. However, Hunye has rejected the outcome of the proceedings and indicated his intention to appeal the judgment. In a statement titled, “Our Legal Journey Continues to the Court of Appeal,” Hunye described the Federal High Court as the first stage of the judicial process, insisting that the appellate court would provide another opportunity for his legal team to pursue the issues raised in the suits. He reaffirmed his commitment to constitutional due process, internal party democracy, and the rule of law, saying his decision to continue with the litigation was informed by the need to ensure fairness and strict compliance with establi

He expressed confidence in the appellate process, adding that his legal team was prepared to present its arguments before the Court of Appeal. “Where questions of fairness, legality, and electoral compliance remain unresolved, our legal team is fully prepared to test every issue before the Court of Appeal. We have faith in the appellate process and remain confident that, in time, truth and legality will prevail,” he said. Hunye further appealed to his supporters, APC members, and the general public to remain calm, peaceful, and law-abiding as the legal process continues. item.title: [VIDEO] Mock Accreditation: Yiaga Africa Urges Voter Participation, Says Low Turnout Could Undermine Exercise
item.description: Yiaga Africa has called on registered voters to turn out en masse for the November 28, 2026 mock accreditation exercise across the country. It said that a low turnout would not create a comfortable sense of the effectiveness of the exercise. Executive Director Samson Itodo stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, saying that the mock accreditation is critical to ascertaining INEC’s readiness for the 2027 general elections. An elderly voter at Unit 1, Alajue, Bode Street in Ede South, sits as she is being accredited by an INEC ad hoc official with a BVAS device during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026 Itodo, however, noted that the electoral umpire missed an opportunity to educate voters on how to thumbprint their ballot papers in the mock accreditation. The mock accreditation will be held across 17,676 selected polling units in the country. It is designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. item.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
item.description: Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia. The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1. According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment. With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects. A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel. Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents. The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network. Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search. Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest. The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence. One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days. Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation. The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation. The reported immigration charges do not amount to convictions for romance fraud. The post Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Adesua Etomi celebrates negative cancer test
item.description: Nollywood actress Adesua Etomi-Wellington has celebrated testing negative for cancer after months of medical procedures, hospital visits and uncertainty over her health. The actress announced the development on Friday in an Instagram video, expressing gratitude to God following the latest result from her medical tests. “The doctor just called me back with the result from the lab, no cancer… God is good,” she said. The video showed some of the medical procedures she underwent, while other pictures revealed bruises on her body and redness beneath one of her eyes. Etomi-Wellington also shared a video of friends and well-wishers celebrating the result with her. Reflecting on her experience, the actress described 2026 as one of the most difficult periods of her life, explaining that her reduced public appearances were linked to her health struggles. “2026 really tried it. I know I’ve been quieter than usual this year (and that’s saying something), but behind the silence were some of the most difficult months of my life,” she wrote. She disclosed that the ordeal involved several medical procedures, scans, injections and hospital visits, adding that she received treatment from medical teams in Nigeria and the United States. “This year threw everything at me, but by the grace of God, I am NOT EASILY BROKEN,” she added. The actress also expressed appreciation to her husband, singer and politician Bankole Wellington, popularly known as Banky W, their children, friends and family members for supporting her throughout the difficult period. “To my friends and family who prayed for me, stood in the gap and held me through some of my darkest days, I will never take your love for granted,” she wrote. The health update comes two days after the couple released a gospel song, On My Way , on November 25 to celebrate their ninth wedding anniversary. The track, credited to Etomi-Wellington, who performs under the musical name Susu, and Banky W, is the lead single from their forthcoming joint album, Not Easily Broken , expected in 2027. The actress described the song as “the soundtrack to our testimony and thanksgiving”, linking its message to their personal experiences. The couple have previously spoken about their health challenges. In May 2024, Banky W disclosed that he had undergone his fourth surgery for cancer after earlier procedures to remove cancerous tumours. Etomi-Wellington also revealed in March 2025 that she battled hyperemesis gravidarum, a severe form of pregnancy sickness, during her second pregnancy. The condition left her ill for months and required hospitalisation before she underwent an emergency Caesarean section. The post Adesua Etomi celebrates negative cancer test appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Damilola Bolarinde Just Made History as Nigeria’s First Miss International Africa
item.description: Damilola Bolarinde styled in a yellow floral brocade cape gown and crown as Miss International Nigeria 2026. Photo Credit: Damilola Bolarinde/Instagram Did you know that since the Miss International organisation introduced continental crowns in 2015, no Nigerian delegate had ever won the regional title—until now? Damilola Bolarinde has officially broken that record, making history as the first Nigerian ever to be crowned Miss International Africa 2026 following the 64th edition of the pageant in Tokyo, Japan. Competing against 73 delegates at Kanadevia Hall (formerly Tokyo Dome City Hall) on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, the Nigerian beauty queen—widely known as Queen Dammy —secured a place in the Top 20 before being named Miss International Africa 2026 on Thursday, 26 November. Beyond bringing home Nigeria’s first-ever continental sash, her Top 20 placement also matched the country’s highest-ever finish in the competition since Nigeria first debuted at Miss International in 1990. Damilola Bolarinde in her Nigerian heritage-inspired national costume for the 64th Miss International pageant. Photo Credit: Damilola Bolarinde/Instagram If you have been following Nigerian pageantry over the past few years, Damilola’s latest milestone will come as no surprise. Outside of pageantry, she works as a model, actress, and entrepreneur, and is the founder of The Unconventional Quest , an advocacy platform focused on helping young Nigerians—particularly women—explore career paths beyond conventional expectations. Her journey to Tokyo was built on years of steady competition on major national and international stages. She earned her spot to represent Nigeria on 19 April 2026 after winning the Face of Hope pageant at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos, which carried the Miss International Nigeria 2026 title. Before that, she represented Lagos State at Miss Universe Nigeria 2025 , finishing as first runner-up, and won Miss Grand Nigeria 2022 , where she also placed in the Top 20 at Miss Grand International in Indonesia. Damilola Bolarinde during a courtesy visit to Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu after winning Miss International Nigeria 2026. Photo Credit: Damilola Bolarinde/Instagram Reacting to her historic win on Instagram, Damilola reflected on the people and experiences behind the achievement: To everyone who contributed to making this journey possible, please know that I do not take your kindness, sacrifices, generosity, or love for granted. Behind this sash is a young woman who has been carried by the love and support of so many people. To my country, Nigeria, thank you for giving me a reason to dream bigger. To Africa, thank you for the privilege of representing our beauty, strength, culture, and resilience. This is not just a sash to me. It represents every hand that helped me get here, every prayer that covered me, every sacrifice that went unseen, and every person who reminded me that I was never walking this journey alone. Nigerian beauty queen
