item.title: The End of Spain’s ‘Frankenstein’ Coalition? Presidential Plotting in Paris, Kushner & Kremlin Trap
item.description: Catch up with the World This Week with Gavin Lee. In just 45 minutes, make sense of seven extraordinary days in global affairs, as Gavin and his handpicked panel of four leading international correspondents unpack the stories shaping the world — and the questions behind the headlines. This week: Spain’s snap election; the presidential plotting unfolding over lunch at the Brasserie Concorde in Paris; Ukraine, Kushner and the ‘Kremlin Trap’; and the question hanging over Iran: whose side is time on? Joining Gavin are New World Magazine columnist Emma-Kate Symonds; Constant Méheut, The New York Times correspondent in Ukraine; Venetia Rainer, Daily Telegraph Foreign Editor and host of Iran: The Latest; and Sarah Morris, France 24’s correspondent in Spain.

This week: Spain’s snap election; the presidential plotting unfolding over lunch at the Brasserie Concorde in Paris; Ukraine, Kushner and the ‘Kremlin Trap’; and the question hanging over Iran: whose side is time on? Joining Gavin are New World Magazine columnist Emma-Kate Symonds; Constant Méheut, The New York Times correspondent in Ukraine; Venetia Rainer, Daily Telegraph Foreign Editor and host of Iran: The Latest; and Sarah Morris, France 24’s correspondent in Spain.

item.title: [VIDEO] Why Mock Accreditation Won’t Have Logos, Names Of Political Parties — INEC
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has explained why the sample ballot papers that will be used for Saturday’s nationwide mock accreditation will not bear the identities of political parties. Speaking during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, INEC’s Deputy Director (Voter Education and Publicity), Wilfred Ifogah, said the November 28, 2026 exercise is not partisan but aimed at testing the agency’s readiness for the 2027 general elections. Ifogah said that materials for the exercise had been deployed, explaining that selected polling units will give a true picture of what accreditation and voting will look like on election day in 2027. This is a mock exercise; we are not using it for any partisanship event. It is just something for those who come out to feel a sense of participation -Deputy Director, Voter Education, INEC, Wilfred Ifogah #PoliticsToday https://t.co/pfBZXtsXq2 — Channels Television (@channelstv) November 27, 2026 The exercise, which is expected to begin at 8:30 a.m. and end at 2:30 p.m., will see INEC deploy the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units to test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. It will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas. The 2027 general elections will begin with the presidential and National Assembly polls on January 16 and end with the governorship and state houses of assembly polls on February 6. Watch the video below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] Why Mock Accreditation Won’t Have Logos, Names Of Political Parties — INEC appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Why have things started to go wrong for Manchester City under Enzo Maresca?
item.description: A sensational start for the Italian was swiftly followed by a dismal run and long faces in the team This is the great known unknown in Manchester City’s run of one win – in addition to victory on penalties against Brighton in the Carabao Cup – in seven matches. After guilty verdicts were returned regarding the breaking of Premier League financial rules, Enzo Maresca’s team went to Anfield and handed Liverpool a 3-0 schooling . Yet this proved the falsest of dawns, with Andoni Iraola’s nascent side perhaps caught in a bad moment. City have since managed one league victory ( 3-2 over Ipswich , six days later) and two more wins in regulation time (in the Champions League) in 10 matches. The sequence includes one point from the past four league fixtures. Maresca argues that his, too, is an embryonic project so there will be uneven form. “I am not a magician,” he said on Friday. But it is also fair to ponder whether, after the adrenaline surge of an us-against-the-world mentality carried City to the Liverpool and Ipswich wins, the grim reality of what the guilty verdict may mean for careers is affecting players. City have appealed against the ruling, saying they are “innocent of the accusations”. Continue reading...

item.description:
Harry joined Space.com in December 2024 as an e-commerce staff writer covering cameras, optics, and skywatching content. Based in the UK, Harry graduated in 2019 with a Bachelor's degree in American Literature with Creative Writing from the University of East Anglia. A keen photographer, Harry has strong experience with astrophotography and has captured celestial objects with a range of cameras. As a lifelong skywatcher, Harry remembers watching the Perseid meteor shower every summer in his hometown and being amazed by the wonders of the night sky.

Camera deals have been a bit harder to find this Black Friday but we have found these great reductions on models we gave some of our highest ratings to. If you are in the market for a new camera , whether for astrophotography, general shooting or another particular style, one of these might fit the bill for your needs. High-resolution models like the Sony A7R V and the Canon EOS R5 are great for those who need the most detail from their shots and a strong amount of pro-functionality. One of our low-light favorites has dropped to its lowest-ever price on Walmart thanks to this year's release of a new version. We loved the Canon EOS R6 II for its amazing high ISO noise handling and impressive -6.5 EV low-light autofocus, so despite the release of the EOS R6 III , this is still one of the best mirrorless cameras you can get for astrophotography. Best Black Friday camera deals live right now EOS R6 Mark II: was $2298 now $1713.95 Canon's low light beast is now at its cheapest price ever. It has a 24MP resolution sensor, 100-102,400 ISO and eight stops of in-body image stabilization. We gave it 4/5 stars in our Canon EOS R6 II review. We gave it four and a half stars out of 5 in our Sony A7R V review. We gave it four and a half stars out of five in our full Nikon D850 review. We gave it four and a half stars out of five in our full Canon EOS R5 review. View Deal

item.title: Courage, Creativity and Impact as Indomie Heroes Awards 2026 Series Continues
item.description: Children make a difference in many ways, and the 18th Indomie Heroes Awards (IHA) 2026 Series brings some of these stories to the forefront. An initiative by Dufil Prima Foods , the series celebrates children whose actions demonstrate bravery, creativity and compassion. Tomike Adeoye presents this eight-part series which features 18 young Nigerians, sharing their experiences and the different ways they have made a positive impact. Courage, Creativity and the Power to Inspire With six episodes aired so far, viewers have encountered stories of children saving lives, helping others, overcoming challenges and using their creativity to solve problems. Each story offers a reminder that children can make a difference, regardless of their age or circumstances. More Stories Worth Watching Beyond celebrating these young heroes, the series offers families an opportunity to watch, learn and discuss values such as courage, kindness and responsibility. It also gives children relatable examples of how their actions can positively affect others. With Episode 7 airing this week, there are more stories to discover and celebrate. Catch the Indomie Heroes Awards Series on NTA (Fridays, 5:00 p.m.), AIT and TVC (Saturdays, 5:30 p.m.), Channels Television (Saturdays, 6:00 p.m. and 6:30 p.m.), Indomie Nigeria YouTube (Saturdays, 6:00 p.m.), BCOS and CTV Kano (Sundays, 5:30 p.m.), and Africa Magic Family (Sundays, 9:00 p.m.). item.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

item.title: The AI revolution: Will I lose my job?
item.description: Have you heard of FOBO? It stands for fear of being obsolete. So as AI spreads, is it going to impact women in the workforce more than men? And are we right to be fearful of becoming obsolete? The International Labour Organization has already found occupations dominated by women are nearly twice as likely to be exposed to job losses thanks to generative AI, compared to those dominated by men.

item.title: Is Spain 'nostalgic' for Franco? Would traditional right PP consider an alliance with far-right Vox?
item.description: After eight years of socialist-led government, Spain is at a crossroads. Can Pedro Sánchez pull off another electoral comeback, or will the conservative Partido Popular make way for the far right into national government for the first time since the end of Franco's 40-year brutal reign? Just back from Madrid, Richard Werly, Europe correspondent for the Swiss daily Blick, joins Angela Diffley to examine the final days of campaigning and the generational divisions shaping Sunday’s snap elections. The youth are divided between the left and the far-right Vox party. Sánchez, nicknamed the “Teflon politician”, has campaigned heavily on housing and social issues. “We may see an outgoing prime minister performing better than expected,” says Werly.

item.title: 'From bad to catastrophic: Iran's justice system was already unfair for many decades'
item.description: Amid war with the US and Israel, Iranian protesters continue to face death sentences following what Amnesty International describes as grossly unfair, torture-tainted trials. “The situation has changed from bad to catastrophic,” says Raha Bahreini, Iranian-Canadian human rights lawyer and Amnesty International's researcher on Iran. Bahreini discusses the aftermath of the January 2026 protests, the authorities' efforts to equate peaceful dissent with treason and espionage, and the extrajudicial killings of peaceful protesters. Amnesty International is calling for an international criminal justice mechanism, potentially a special tribunal. “There needs to be criminal accountability for these crimes against humanity.”

item.description: Uganda's army on Friday said it planned to withdraw from the eastern DR Congo town of Lubero in North Kivu. The announcement came days after Ugandan army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba – son of President Yoweri Museveni – threatened to take control of Walikale, another North Kivu town, sparking a diplomatic spat between the two neighbouring nations.

item.title: The Com: the global cybercrime network posing a ‘chilling threat’ to children
item.description: FBI estimates thousands of people identify as members, or recent members, of group linked to indecent images of girls and blackmail It sounds benign: the Com, short for the Community. But crime agencies around the world warn that it is far from that and the young cybercriminals involved are causing havoc and putting children at chilling, sickening risk. Beau-Jack Mensforth was jailed by a UK judge on Friday for his activities as part of the Com. He was one individual operating from his bedroom in north-east England, but there are probably thousands more like him and parents are being urged by police to be aware and to check their children’s devices. Continue reading...

item.title: The best cordless vacuum cleaners for a spotless home: 10 tried and tested favourites
item.description: Stick vacuums are a convenient alternative to corded designs, but which model wins for overall cleaning prowess? Our expert reveals all • The best robot vacuums • How to make your vacuum last longer Choosing a cordless vacuum is a big decision. Whichever model you go for, you’re likely to use it for years, relying on its ability to suck up dust, crumbs, mud, pet hair and any other dry spillages or sheddings. Choosing the right model can be the difference between an effective cleaner that’s a delight to pull out of the cupboard and a dud that you dread having to unblock, detangle and clean after every use. In this review, I took 18 of the leading cordless vacuum cleaners from a range of manufacturers and at various prices and inflicted the same cleaning tests on each one. That takes all the guesswork out of picking your next cleaner: I can tell you exactly which ones picked up the most mess, and how easy and enjoyable they were to use. Continue reading...

item.title: Osun LG Crisis Will Be Fully Resolved In The Next One Week — Gov Adeleke
item.description: Governor Ademola Adeleke has assured the people of Osun State that the protracted local government crisis in the state will be resolved within the next week, following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention. Governor Adeleke gave this assurance in his inaugural speech during his second-term inauguration held at Osogbo City Stadium, where he listed some of the priorities of his second-term administration across all sectors. “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter and in the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres,” he said. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke was sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. As part of his priorities, the re-elected governor promised to set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission, as well as infrastructural expansion and recruitment of teachers and rehabilitation of schools, including reviving technical colleges. He also said that job and wealth creation will be at the heart of his second term. “We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy,” Adeleke said. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” In the health sector, he said about 70 per cent of existing primary health care centres were rehabilitated and equipped with solar and power facilities in his first term. “We upgraded and completed 232 out of 332 primary health care centres. item.title: France is dealing with water insecurity – a new study shows it's a global problem
item.description: Tens of thousands of people in France are living under water restrictions as the country deals with a drought despite recent rains, according to the environment ministry. But this is a global problem, as a new study released Wednesday revealed "the largest global decline in surface water resources recorded" since 1991, when data collection began.

item.title: The best Black Friday deals Ars could find
item.description: Every year has a Prime Day—some years even have two Prime Days!—where we celebrate the life and achievements of the greatest leader the Autobots have ever known: the inimitable Optimus Prime. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime's bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005 . It is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and launched a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron's schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City— heroes, all of them !—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator , against which there appeared to be no defense. And then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: " Megatron must be stopped, no matter the cost ." The fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though that cost was high. Many brave Autobots besides Optimus Prime lost their lives during the fighting. It was truly a dark day, a black day—and so, every year on the Friday after Thanksgiving, we pause to remember the noble sacrifices made by Prime and by so many others. This is why today is known as Black Friday. Read full article Comments

item.title: Big EU defence projects under threat from proposed budget cuts: Commissioner Andrius Kubilius
item.description: We speak to the EU's Commissioner for Defence and Space, Andrius Kubilius. The former prime minister of Lithuania – who grew up during the Soviet era – tells us how he sees the confrontation between Europe and Russia. He also sounds the alarm over proposed cuts in the EU's future budget, saying that they could jeopardise major European projects in defence and space. Kubilius praises the EU's SAFE defence loans programme, remarking that it has been "really very successful".

item.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
item.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. How and when I'm watching it The names and distances of the stars in Cassiopeia. (Image credit: Starry Night) I'm going to observe Cassiopeia twice on the same evening this week, which is about as complicated as the experiment needs to get. The first time will be shortly after darkness falls. I'll find the W, note which way it seems to be pointing and use something fixed — a rooftop, tree or chimney — to give myself a rough reference for its position. I'll return to my backyard before bed, and see where the pattern ha
item.dc:creator: Jamie Carter
item.content:encoded: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. How and when I'm watching it The names and distances of the stars in Cassiopeia. (Image credit: Starry Night) I'm going to observe Cassiopeia twice on the same evening this week, which is about as complicated as the experiment needs to get. The first time will be shortly after darkness falls. I'll find the W, note which way it seems to be pointing and use something fixed — a rooftop, tree or chimney — to give myself a rough reference for its position. I'll return to my backyard before bed, and see where the pattern has shifted. Cassiopeia's main stars are bright enough to survive urban and suburban light pollution, so you don't need a particularly dark sky or a telescope. While I'm gazing at Cassiopeia, I'll try to see the stars as they really are, and not just how they appear to us. Check out the distances of its stars from the sun : Caph: 55 light-years Schedar: 228 light-years Navi: 550 light-years Ruchbah: 99 light-years Segin: 440 light-years Only Caph and Ruchbah are within 100 light-years — the sun's local interstellar neighborhood. Does that destroy the very concept of Cassiopeia as a group of related stars? Cassiopeia, like all constellations, is a mirage, with a capital M. There's another reason I love Cassiopeia. Proxima Centauri, the closest star to our sun, lies just 4.24 light-years away. Travel there and look back towards our solar system , and our sun would appear as an extra star in Cassiopeia — effectively giving the constellation a sixth bright point. From a certain perspective, we are all Cassiopeians. Stargazer's corner: Nov. 27-Dec. 4, 2026 NGC 457 (the Owl Cluster) is in Cassiopeia. (Image credit: Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) The last few evenings of November bring back darker early-night skies as the moon wanes from full earlier in the week and rises progressively later. It will rise in the middle of the night as it reaches its last-quarter phase on Dec. 1. It's an ideal time to sweep a pair of binoculars across the rich star fields around Cassiopeia and Perseus . On the boundary between the two constellations is the Double Cluster (NGC 869 and NGC 884), one of the finest binocular sights in the entire northern sky. These two dense concentrations of young stars sit side by side against the richer background of the Milky Way . Under a dark sky, you can see it with the naked eye. M52, NGC 457 (the Owl Cluster) and NGC 663 are other clusters also worth seeking out in Cassiopeia. Conjunction of the week: Moon, Jupiter, Mars and Regulus Four objects will trace a striking crescent on Nov. 30. (Image credit: Starry Night) Get outside about 45 minutes before sunrise on Monday, Nov. 30, and look high in the southern sky for a fitting month-ending finale. A 61%-lit waning gibbous moon will appear alongside brilliant Jupiter , reddish Mars and Regulus, the brightest star in Leo. Together, the four objects will trace a striking crescent spanning just over five degrees of sky — roughly the width of three fingers held at arm's length. It's a much tighter version of a similar arrangement visible on Nov. 2, with Jupiter by far the brightest point and the contrasting colors of Mars and blue-white Regulus adding to the spectacle. No equipment will be needed, though binoculars will help you get a close-up of this rather unusual conjunction.

item.title: Sierra Leone: Maternal deaths fall as healthcare improves, but challenges remain
item.description: Sierra Leone was once considered one of the most dangerous countries in the world to give birth. Maternal deaths have since fallen dramatically, thanks to improvements in healthcare, medical training and maternity services. But despite this progress, significant challenges remain. Activists warn that continued efforts are needed to ensure safer pregnancies and childbirth for women across the country. Clarisse Fortuné reports.

A few weeks ago, Alessio Dionisi was forced to deny the “fake news” he had joined Sean Dyche, Gianfranco Zola, Beppe Sannino, Óscar García, Billy McKinlay, Slavisa Jokanovic, Quique Sánchez Flores (twice), Walter Mazzarri, Marco Silva, Javi Gracia (twice), Nigel Pearson, Vladimir Ivic, Xisco Muñoz, Claudio Ranieri, Roy Hodgson, Rob Edwards, Slaven Bilic, Chris Wilder, Valérien Ismael, Tom Cleverley, Paulo Pezzolano and Edward Still in being sacked by the Pozzo family since 2012. There was no denial on Sunday, when the axe inevitably fell on the head coach following a 4-0 shellacking at Sheffield United and the Italian left after only 18 games in charge. While his reign is unlikely to live long in the memory of anyone at Vicarage Road, Dionisi can at least boast on his LinkedIn page that in terms of longevity under the Pozzos, he took charge of 18 more matches than Dyche, 17 more than García and 16 more than McKinlay. Indeed, he even outlasted Rob Edwards, who was assured he would be backed “come hell or high water” upon his 2022 appointment, only to be fired from the ejector seat 11 games later. item.title: Stream Detty December From Anywhere: LivDot Brings BNXN, Ruger, Oxlade and Fola Concerts to Global Audiences
item.description: Bada Akintunde-Johnson: MD/CEO Livdot Technologies Liimited. Fans who can’t make it to Lagos this December no longer have to miss it. LivDot , a new live-event streaming platform, will stream concerts by BNXN , Fola , Oxlade and Ruger live and exclusively to audiences worldwide from 19 to 22 December. The launch also rewrites the maths of a sell-out. When a 5,000-capacity concert sells out, the ticketing opportunity usually ends there. On LivDot, the same show can sell 50,000 or more streaming tickets to fans across Nigeria, Africa and the diaspora. LivDot was founded by Bada Akintunde-Johnson , former Country Manager of Paramount Skydance Africa, whose career spans MTV Base, BET, Nickelodeon and Comedy Central in Nigeria. “Imagine being in London, Houston or Toronto and experiencing the energy of Detty December in real time,” said Akintunde-Johnson. “For fans who can’t make the trip, we are curing your fear of missing out by bringing Lagos’s live entertainment to you, wherever you are.” The December lineup Exclusive streams on LivDot this season include: 12 December — The Worship Project by The Fountain of Life Church 19 December — BNXN (formerly known as Buju) 20 December — Fola 21 December — Oxlade 22 December — Ruger 25 December — Saheed Osupa and Friends White Party Date [TBC] — The Digital Product Growth Summit More headline concerts, faith and business events are lined up for the season. Fans can buy streaming tickets or watch free events at www.livdot.co Beyond the venue walls For event organizers, LivDot is the infrastructure behind that extra audience. It brings production, live streaming and payments together in one place, with content distributed free or behind a pay-per-view access fee. A built-in marketplace of vetted photographers and videographers makes hiring quality production talent easier and more consistent. “For too long, the reach and economics of live events have been defined by the walls of the venue,” said Akintunde-Johnson. “A sold-out room should be the floor of an event’s audience and earning potential, not the ceiling.” For artists, it means reaching fans abroad far more often. Instead of waiting for an occasional arena date in London or New York, an artist can stage a lean live performance in Nigeria, sell affordable digital tickets to fans worldwide, and let LivDot handle production, streaming and payment. That opens the door to intimate shows, exclusive sessions, album listenings and other fan experiences. “Artists should be able to perform more often, on their own terms, and earn directly from fans around the world,” Akintunde-Johnson added. “We want to make that commercially practical.” Concerts are only the start. item.title: DR Congo: Copper reserves put Africa at the centre of the global race for critical minerals
item.description: Africa is emerging as a key player in the global race for copper, accounting for around 10 per cent of the world's estimated reserves. The Democratic Republic of Congo is at the centre of this growing interest, having mined 3.4 million metric tons of copper in 2025. Its vast mineral resources are attracting growing attention from countries and companies around the world, as demand for the metal rises due to its importance in energy infrastructure, electric vehicles and the global transition to cleaner energy.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
item.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: With Spain’s far right on the cusp of power, can women bail Sanchez out once again?
item.description: Spanish women’s refusal to surrender hard-won rights helped Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez stave off defeat in a snap election three years ago. As he gambles with another early vote on Sunday, his hopes of defying the odds rest on women again rallying to block the far right from governing Spain for the first time since Franco’s dictatorship.

item.title: Nigeria: Political violence and attacks on candidates raise fears ahead of January elections
item.description: Political violence is escalating in Nigeria ahead of the general elections scheduled for January. Candidates and their supporters have increasingly come under attack, with armed groups disrupting campaign rallies and some assaults resulting in deaths. Despite the growing number of incidents, security forces have struggled to contain the violence. With less than two months to go before the vote, fears are mounting that intimidation and deadly attacks could prevent many Nigerians from freely taking part in the democratic process.

item.title: French student protests: A 'very bizarre' government response
item.description: “The government had a very bizarre way of dealing with the student protests,” says Jean-Rémi Girard, a secondary school teacher and union representative in Asnières-sur-Seine. He explains how teachers sought to defuse tensions by listening to students, and respecting their right to protest, while keeping classes running. He recounts a police intervention last October and the case of a student facing trial for defending a classmate, and has the full support of several teachers. Girard questions the government's heavy-handed policing and largely symbolic proposals on class sizes and university admissions. “There wasn't really a negotiation,” he says, also highlighting the number of education workers injured during the protests.

Heck, we're even offering the chance to win a smart telescope worth $419 ! But as exciting as all the Black Friday deals are, there's the very real risk that you could get scammed, particularly given how exciting it is to snag a deal. That's where my scam-spotting guide comes in. Not only do I get paid to hunt down Black Friday savings, but I've also snapped up more stargazing deals than I care to think about, and I know how to spot a shady offer or suspect site. So, read on and I'll show you how to stay safe online this Black Friday. How to shop safely and spot suspect sites The best way to avoid getting scammed is to take advantage of our carefully curated Black Friday Deals . We put the work in to find you the best deals on stargazing equipment, cameras, tech and even toys, double and triple-checking that they're genuine savings from reputable retailers. And if you're hunting for deals on your own, you should do the same; shop with known and trusted retailers such as Amazon, Best Buy, Target and others. Ideally, you'll want items that are sold and shipped by that retailer; you can usually tell if that's the case by looking at the buy box, the area with 'Buy Now', 'Add to Cart ', or similar. Some sites, Amazon included, let third-party companies sell through their sites. That's not a scam, and most are legitimate. However, I'd still recommend you check out the seller's feedback and if you see a lot of negative feedback, you should probably steer clear. In doubt? item.content:encoded: There are some real bargains to be had this Black Friday, including discounts on telescopes , cameras , drones , Lego and streaming to watch your favorite sci-fi. Heck, we're even offering the chance to win a smart telescope worth $419 ! But as exciting as all the Black Friday deals are, there's the very real risk that you could get scammed, particularly given how exciting it is to snag a deal. That's where my scam-spotting guide comes in. Not only do I get paid to hunt down Black Friday savings, but I've also snapped up more stargazing deals than I care to think about, and I know how to spot a shady offer or suspect site. So, read on and I'll show you how to stay safe online this Black Friday. How to shop safely and spot suspect sites The best way to avoid getting scammed is to take advantage of our carefully curated Black Friday Deals . We put the work in to find you the best deals on stargazing equipment, cameras, tech and even toys, double and triple-checking that they're genuine savings from reputable retailers. And if you're hunting for deals on your own, you should do the same; shop with known and trusted retailers such as Amazon, Best Buy, Target and others. Ideally, you'll want items that are sold and shipped by that retailer; you can usually tell if that's the case by looking at the buy box, the area with 'Buy Now', 'Add to Cart ', or similar. Some sites, Amazon included, let third-party companies sell through their sites. That's not a scam, and most are legitimate. However, I'd still recommend you check out the seller's feedback and if you see a lot of negative feedback, you should probably steer clear. In doubt? Myself and a team of experts spend all of Black Friday finding the best, most reliable deals from reputable retailers so you don't have to, testing links and checking they're legitimate and safe. We'll drop our favorites into the page below, but check out our Black Friday Deals page for more. Plus, Hulu bundle Black Friday!: was $12.99 now $4.99 Disney Plus is the home of both the Star Wars and Marvel cinematic universes. You can save 62% by getting the Disney and Hulu ad-supported bundle and get two huge libraries of content for less than $5 a month. View Deal Save 77% by signing up for two years of NordVPN's Prime plan (nothing to do with Amazon) and getting three months extra for free. There are also other cheaper options which offer lesser savings. NordVPN features an ad and tracker blocker, anti-malware protection, a data breach scanner, browsing protection and much more. View Deal How to spot scam sites when shopping Black Friday 2026 You can check just how secure a website is through your browser (Image credit: Amazon / Best Buy) However, while Amazon , Best Buy and so on have been around for a long time, it's surprisingly easy to set up a fake website. Here's how to check if a website is secure. Look at the address bar at the top of the browser. Make sure the address matches the website you think you're on. Look for a padlock icon by the address bar. Not all browsers offer this but if you see it it's a sign your details will be secure. If there's no padlock icon, your browser will have another icon, such as Firefox's shield, or Google Chrome's tune icon. Look for the words 'connection secure'. Even if the website isn't an imitation, it's important to be wary of sites that pop up offering massive discounts. While lightning deals are absolutely a thing, some of these sites offer fake countdowns in an effort to pressure you into buying goods. If you see one of the best smart telescopes for a quarter of its normal price, for example, you should immediately be suspicious. Your credit card or debit card may offer some protection if you are scammed but you should always be wary. Other warnings include misspelled product names, stock text, buttons that don't work and other oddities. You can also use a domain name checker to find out how old a website is. If the website was registered just a few months ago, that's a big red flag. Editor's pick NexStar 8SE: was $1699 now $1499 Save $200 on what we've ranked as one of the best telescopes on the market today. You can see everything from nearby planets to far-reaching deep sky objects with bright and sharp views across the entire frame. View Deal How to spot off-brand and fake goods (Image credit: Getty Images) Editor's pick NexStar 4SE Telescope: was $749 now $649 Save on a telescope that has featured in our best telescopes guide since our hands-on Celestron NexStar 4SE review early in 2023. View Deal If you're shopping for a Black Friday bargain for the space or sci-fi fan in your life, it's important to keep an eye out for off-brand and fake goods. Not all building block sets are Lego, for example, and there's nothing illegal about other companies making their own sets, but it could lead to disappointment come Christmas Day. And there are also shady companies who will sell direct copies of existing Lego sets. We have a guide to imitation Lego , but the shortcut is to just look out for the Lego logo. You may come across unfamiliar brands of telescopes, binoculars and other gear. Often, companies will take a generic product, add their own branding, and sell it at a markup. There's no guarantee that product will last and support may well be lacking. Reading a product's feedback can help, but I've also stumbled across many suspicious reviews. Then there are some products that are just copies of branded goods; forgeries, essentially. I've seen knock-off MicroSD cards, bootleg chargers, and even Celestron has had to warn against fraudulent websites and fake telescopes. The best advice in this regard is to use trusted websites and remember that if a deal is too good to be true, it probably isn't. Editor's pick Save on one of the best star projectors . In our Pococo Galaxy Projector review , we loved how vibrant and bright the projections appear and that there is a heap of add-on disks available. View Deal How to protect your identity online A VPN is an excellent way of shielding yourself from hackers and other hazards (Image credit: Getty Images) Even if you've grabbed a great Black Friday deal , you still need to take steps to protect your identity. One of the best ways to do that is with one of the best VPN services and, this Black Friday there are huge savings on NordVPN and Surfshark . Both services shield you from hackers, hiding your true location and, depending on the tier you choose, can alert you if your identity is compromised. Plus, if you're away from home this holiday season, they're handy for accessing the best sci-fi streaming services . Save big on Paramount's Premium Plan for two months. Paramount Plus is the home of all Star Trek content as well as its considerable library of original content. View Deal How to spot phishing scams Hackers aside, phishing scams are another risk to your online safety and security. If you get an email that claims to be from a retailer, there's the possibility it's a phishing scam, looking to steal your details. Here are some warning signs: The email doesn't mention you by name It's for a purchase you haven't made If you hover your mouse over the links, the website address is wrong A common phishing scam I've seen, and one which I almost fell for, is fake emails from a shipping company, telling you there's an extra charge on a package. Click through and the scammer will steal your money and/or credit card details. The best option, if you genuinely have ordered something, is to go to the official website you ordered from and click on your order history. And above all, never, ever share your passwords with anyone, friend or otherwise. How to enter our smart telescope giveway Want a Dwarflab Dwarf Mini smart telescope? item.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
item.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. item.dc:creator: Dan Robinson
item.content:encoded: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. "The unusually low 2027 base creates the potential for a robust rebound in 2028 once the memory bottleneck begins to ease. But this should not be interpreted as a return to the old market trajectory," Wang said. "Some low-end demand has been permanently lost, and the 2028 market will still be about 14 percent below 2025 shipments." Potential availability of 6G-capable smartphones toward the end of the decade could give the market a boost, but Counterpoint does not expect it to regain its 2025 shipment levels by 2030. ®

item.title: Your Career Is Probably Ignoring Your Strongest Leadership Training: Community
item.description: Community involvement can be a powerful source of leadership skills, professional connections and career opportunities. By recognizing the value of their community experiences, building genuine relationships and making clear requests for support, professionals can turn existing connections into lasting career growth and influence.

item.title: Manchester United extend Fernandes contract until 2028 to stop free transfer
item.description: Club activate option and plan further talks with captain ‘I am not nice,’ says Pochettino as he targets improvement Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes. Fernandes’ deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”. He has turned down two United contract offers. Continue reading...

item.title: Trish O Couture Returns With ‘Polka & Play’: More Dazzling Celebration Of Fashion, Feathers And Diamonds
item.description: Following the resounding success of its maiden annual fashion showcase, which also celebrated 18 remarkable years of Trish O Couture under the theme “Classics Across All Seasons” , award-winning fashion house Trish O Couture is set to return with an even more ambitious presentation. This year’s edition, aptly titled Polka & Play , holds on Sunday, December 13, 2026, at The Royal Box, Mikano Building, Victoria Island, Lagos. The inaugural showcase attracted impressive media attention and was widely received as a fitting celebration of the fashion house’s creative journey. Building on that success, the second edition promises a more expansive and engaging celebration of fashion, personal style and luxury. With its creative inspiration drawn from 2 distinctive fashion elements- polka dots and feathers: Polka & Play explores the more playful, expressive side of couture while retaining the elegance, craftsmanship and sophistication synonymous with the Trish O Couture identity. At the centre of the evening will be an exclusive women’s wear runway presentation featuring the creative vision of Trish O Couture. Expect an engaging interplay of silhouettes, textures, patterns and embellishments, with polka dots and feathers providing the inspiration for a visually compelling fashion narrative. Adding another dimension to the occasion is a showcase by Lady Trish Diamonds, the jewellery subsidiary of Trish O Couture. The presentation will celebrate the brilliance and timeless appeal of fine diamonds, bringing the worlds of couture and exquisite jewellery together in one carefully curated luxury experience. Founded by Lady Dr. Tricia Onumonu , who also serves as its Creative Director, Trish O Couture has cultivated a distinctive fashion identity around creativity, elegance and individual expression. Its annual showcase provides an opportunity to bring that vision to life, while creating a meeting point for fashion enthusiasts, industry personalities, style connoisseurs and lovers of luxury. With the success and considerable publicity of the maiden edition setting a compelling precedent, expectations are understandably high for this year’s presentation. The ambition is to deliver an experience that surpasses its predecessor in creativity, presentation and overall impact, further establishing the Trish O Couture annual showcase as a notable fixture on Lagos’ fashion and luxury lifestyle calendar. Guests are invited to interpret the evening’s dress code, Polka & Feathers: Glitz Chic, with imagination and flair. It is an invitation to indulge in sartorial expression, embrace the playful spirit of the theme and arrive ready for an evening of fashion and glamour. The evening commences at 7:00 p.m. Event Details Event: Polka & Play: Women’s Wear Runway Show & Display of Lady Trish Diamonds Host: Trish O Couture Date: Sunday, December 13, 2026 Time: 7:00 p.m. Venue: The Royal Box, Mikano Building, 65 Adeola Odeku, Victoria Island, Lagos. Dress Code: Polka & Feathers:

item.title: Renée Slegers leaves job as Arsenal Women’s coach after dismal run of results
item.description: Club languishing sixth in WSL after six home draws Held high hopes of mounting title challenge this term Renée Slegers has left her job as Arsenal Women’s head coach after a dismal set of results, with the club saying she has gone by mutual consent. The 37-year-old had been under contract until 2029 after signing a three-and-a-half-year deal in January but six consecutive home draws in the Women’s Super League this season have left Arsenal sixth, 12 points behind the leaders, Chelsea, and eight points adrift of a European place. Continue reading...

item.title: Artemis III Astronaut Andre Douglas Visits VAB
item.description: NASA/Kim Shiflett NASA astronaut Andre Douglas, Artemis III mission specialist, stands inside an RS-25 engine test article during a visit to the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. During Artemis III, four RS-25 engines will power the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket core stage to send the Orion spacecraft to conduct critical rendezvous and docking tests with lunar lander systems in low Earth orbit, advancing the capabilities needed before astronauts return to the lunar surface on Artemis IV. Image credit: NASA/Kim Shiflett

item.title: Artemis III astronauts meet their spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 27, 2026
item.description: null NASA's Artemis III astronauts pose holding up three fingers to symbolize their mission as they visit the Orion spacecraft they will ride to space. (Image credit: NASA/Kim Shiflett) Training for a mission to space is hard work. But sometimes you have to take a minute and have a little fun with your crewmates. What is it? Crowded together with the Orion spacecraft, the four astronauts that make up the Artemis III crew hold up three fingers, taking a brief pause in their rigorous training for some lighthearted crew bonding. In the snapshot , the crew — from left to right, NASA astronauts Randy Bresnick (mission commander) and Frank Rubio (mission specialist), European Space Agency astronaut Luca Parmitano (mission pilot) and NASA astronaut Andre Douglas (mission specialist) — is spotted posing alongside the same Orion spacecraft that they will fly to space as part of their mission. This brief moment of levity took place where the spacecraft currently resides at the Neil A. Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Why is it incredible? This crew has a serious mission ahead of them. The four astronauts will launch to low-Earth orbit around Earth where they plan to practice rendezvous and docking with both Blue Origin and SpaceX's lunar landing vehicles , Blue Moon and Starship, respectively. To prepare, the crew has to undergo months of critical training to both be physically ready while prepared to handle any situation that might come up during their mission. And while Artemis III isn't landing astronauts on the moon, it is a critical step toward that goal. If Artemis III goes to plan and NASA has a lunar landing vehicle that passes rendezvous and docking tests with the Orion spacecraft, Artemis IV might see astronauts land on the moon for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.

item.title: NASA’s NG-25 Mission to Launch Pioneering Space Crops Research
item.description: Experiments in the Ohalo III facility (pictured above) aim to validate plant-water delivery, optimize volume, and advance crop-production research. These insights could inform the design of plant production systems for future deep-space missions. NASA NASA experiments, including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system, will travel to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency. Investigations from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division will advance research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration, expanding knowledge of space crops and human health. Groundbreaking space crops Astronauts will need sustainable sources of food to travel farther and stay longer in space. To help understand how crop production works in microgravity, NASA is launching a novel space crops growth chamber called Ohalo III. The new prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing safe, nutritious, and reliable crop production strategies for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Knowledge gained from the space crop production system also could help inform agricultural practices such as vertical farming and indoor growing systems. Researchers will validate the system’s water delivery and volume optimization technology aboard the space station. Tiny brain models aboard station A precision health investigation is the next step toward enabling long-duration studies of human brain tissues in space. The research builds on a previous investigation that sent small, lab-grown models of the human brain, called miBrains, to the space station. This experiment will validate a miniature fluid-handling system designed to mix, deliver, and maintain the nutrient-rich liquid needed to keep the tissues alive. Researchers could use the findings to help identify potential neurological risks associated with spaceflight and develop strategies to protect astronaut health. It also may advance human tissue research and neurological disease modeling on Earth. Biological & Physical Sciences Division NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division pioneers scientific discovery and enables exploration by using space environments to conduct investigations not possible on Earth. Studying biological and physical phenomena under extreme conditions allows researchers to advance the fundamental scientific knowledge required to go farther and stay longer in space, while also benefitting life on Earth.

item.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
item.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. item.content:encoded: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. Council taxpayers can be assured the new system has gone live without major problems, but that is hardly cause for celebration. ®

item.title: It’s the biggest ever month for video games – so why am I playing a title from 2006? | Dominik Diamond
item.description: While everyone else is giddy over Zelda and GTA, Dominik Diamond finds himself behind the times on a Nintendo Wii I find myself on the wrong side of gaming history this month. I have zero zeitgeist. My takes are as fresh as something found at the rear of the fridge. I haven’t even played Grand Theft Auto VI yet, but we’ll get to that. Worse, all month, the Nintendo sector of the gaming world has been going googly eyed over Zelda. The Ocarina of Time remake seems to have produced more joy than all the puppies in the world. But not for me. I have never liked Zelda. It’s like being a movie reviewer who doesn’t like Disney, or a vegan shark. Continue reading...

item.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
item.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. It seems that where the US leads, the UK still often follows. item.dc:creator: Dan Robinson
item.content:encoded: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. It seems that where the US leads, the UK still often follows. The Covenant sets out efficiency targets and reporting expectations, but does not explain how compliance will be enforced or specify penalties for failing to meet its tests. Protect the Wild notes that it "barely acknowledges wildlife, habitats or biodiversity. In fact, it doesn't mention any of those things at all." The Covenant does, however, call on operators to "protect nature," without spelling out specific safeguards for wildlife, habitats, or biodiversity. While the government encourages all server farms to meet the tests, only those it considers "strategic" are required to do so, as we noted above. And even that is only in order to qualify for extra government support, not in order to gain approval for a project. Further, the campaign group contends that having environmental concerns addressed on a project-by-project basis at the planning level is a major barrier to tackling greenhouse gas emissions at a national level. It cites the draft National Policy Statement for Data Centres, under which operational emissions from nationally significant projects in England, including those from on-site power generation, would be managed against national climate commitments at an economy-wide level rather than assessing each application's contribution to those targets. Protect the Wild also argues that project-level assessments do not adequately capture nationwide habitat loss, even though the planning process requires consideration of cumulative environmental effects. Datacenters have become a growing public concern in the UK, although opposition has not reached the level it has in the US, where anti-datacenter sentiment played a major part in political campaigns for the recent midterm elections. But there were protests around the country at the start of November, such as in London and at Great Torrington, a town in Devon where a proposed 1.5 GW data campus and battery energy storage facility would cover 850 acres of nearby farmland. Celebrity TV cook Delia Smith recently joined protests over a proposed datacenter on the edge of Norwich in Norfolk over concerns it may threaten a nearby nature reserve. Protesters are unlikely to find much sympathy in Westminster. The government has already pinned its hopes for growing the economy on AI, as detailed in its AI Opportunities Action Plan last year, and it sees building more datacenters as key to achieving this. The Guardian reports that Natural England, the government's own advisory body for the natural environment, is being threatened with abolition weeks after raising objections to a large AI campus near Bristol because of the threat it poses to protected wildlife and habitats. A separate report found that the government met with 137 different businesses to discuss datacenters between July 2024 and June 2026, but did not meet a single community group or environmental organization during the same period. ®
